    rmarkdown::render(input, output_dir = outdir, envir = new.env())
  })

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# 2026-09-29 (report overhaul): warnings and messages are CAPTURED, not discarded. Until this
# date the global options were message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, which threw away every R
# warning a run raised (the PE consistency flag, a shared_tau that was ignored, the season-
# window checks, the census frame). The hooks below keep them out of the body of the page and
# record each one, with the chunk it came from, for the "Run warnings and notes" section at the
# end of the report and for run_warnings.csv.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.align = "center", fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, out.width = "100%")
.report_conditions <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.report_conditions$log <- data.frame(chunk = character(0), type = character(0), message = character(0),
                                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
.problem_pattern <- "warn|fallback|fall back|skip|fail|could not|cannot|unavailable|unusable|not available|dropped|ignored|error|clipped|outside the window|stuck|refus"
.record_condition <- function(type) function(x, options) {
  # knitr can hand the hook SEVERAL conditions at once (a character vector): record each.
  x <- gsub("(^|\n)## ?", "\\1", as.character(x))       # knitr's comment prefix, on every line
  msg <- trimws(gsub("^(Warning|Message)( in [^:]*)?:\\s*", "", gsub("\\s*\n+\\s*", " ", x)))
  msg <- msg[nzchar(msg) & !grepl("^[=-]*$", msg)]
  # message() is also how many chunks print progress banners; a note is kept only when it
  # reports a problem (a warning, fallback, skip or failure), so the section is not a console dump.
  if (identical(type, "message"))
    msg <- msg[grepl(.problem_pattern, msg, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  if (length(msg))
    .report_conditions$log <- rbind(.report_conditions$log,
      data.frame(chunk = options$label %||% "?", type = type, message = msg, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  ""
}
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || length(a) == 0) b else a
knitr::knit_hooks$set(warning = .record_condition("warning"), message = .record_condition("message"))

# A small helper to render a data frame as a clean, captioned report table. digits applies to
# every numeric column; round counts to 0 before calling it (or pass digits = 0).
options(knitr.kable.NA = "-")   # an empty cell reads "-", not "NA"
report_table <- function(df, caption = NULL, digits = 2) {
  if (is.null(df) || !is.data.frame(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  knitr::kable(df, caption = caption, digits = digits, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
}
# A p-value for a table: two significant figures, "< 1e-04" below that, as TEXT so kable's
# digits cannot round it to 0 (the opener and marine screens printed p = 0 before 2026-09-29).
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "-", format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 1e-4))
# A median with its 95% interval as one readable cell.
# A point with no interval (the commercial census, an exact count) reads "<m> (no interval)".
fmt_ci <- function(m, lo, hi, digits = 0) {
  .f <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
  ifelse(is.na(m), "-", ifelse(is.na(lo) | is.na(hi), sprintf("%s (no interval)", .f(m)),
                               sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", .f(m), .f(lo), .f(hi))))
}

# Short, HTML-friendly fit labels for display tables (e.g. "boat all-gear"). The pot-closure
# sub-season's internal key is ring_net_only, kept for filename continuity.
short_fit <- function(x) gsub("_Dungeness_Kept$", "",
                         gsub("private_boat", "boat",
                           gsub("_ring_net_only", " pot-closure",
                             gsub("_all_gear", " all-gear", x))))

# Pot-closure boundary markers for date-axis plots. Draws a dotted line at the pot-
# closure start and a dashed line at the day pots open (closure end + 1), so every
# season plot brackets the pot-closure window explicitly (added 2026-07-13 with the
# explicit pot_closure_start/end config). Returns a list of ggplot layers, added to a
# plot with `+`. When the closure starts at the season start the left line sits at the
# left edge (correct). labels = FALSE draws the lines only (for secondary panels).
pot_closure_markers <- function(params, labels = TRUE) {
  pc_start  <- as.Date(params$pot_closure_start %||% params$est_date_start)
  pots_open <- as.Date(params$pot_open_date     %||% (as.Date(params$pot_closure_end) + 1))
  layers <- list(
    geom_vline(xintercept = pc_start,  linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 0.5),
    geom_vline(xintercept = pots_open, linetype = "dashed", color = "red",       linewidth = 0.5))
  if (labels) layers <- c(layers, list(
    annotate("text", x = pc_start + 3,  y = Inf, label = "Pot closure start",
             hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "darkgreen"),
    annotate("text", x = pots_open + 3, y = Inf, label = "Pots open",
             hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "red")))
  layers
}

# Read the per-fit CSVs a section wrote to output_dir (files named prefix_<label>.csv)
# and row-bind them for on-page display, tagging each row with a short fit_lbl label from
# the filename. Display-only and defensive: returns NULL if output_dir or the files are
# absent (a PE-only fit writes none), so a display chunk can never break the knit.
read_fit_outputs <- function(prefix, dir = NULL) {
  if (is.null(dir)) {
    if (!exists("output_dir", inherits = TRUE)) return(NULL)
    dir <- get("output_dir", inherits = TRUE)
  }
  fs <- list.files(dir, pattern = paste0("^", prefix, "_.*\\.csv$"), full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(fs)) return(NULL)
  tryCatch(
    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(fs, function(f) {
      d <- suppressWarnings(utils::read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE))
      d$fit_lbl <- short_fit(sub(paste0("^", prefix, "_"), "",
                              tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))))
      d
    })),
    error = function(e) NULL)
}
```

> **How to read this report.** This is the results report for one harvest estimate from the pooled CPUE model, the method of record. **The headline is [Section 7](#headline-result-port-total)**: the port total and its components, each with a 95% credible interval. Read it with [Section 6](#convergence-gate-and-model-selection) (did every fit converge, and which method each component reports), [Section 13](#pe-vs-bss-comparison) (how far the design-based and Bayesian estimates agree) and [Section 16](#run-warnings-and-notes) (every warning, fallback and skipped step this run recorded). Sections 1 to 5 show the configuration, the inputs and the resolved expansion factors; Sections 8 to 12 break the total down and show the diagnostics behind it. Code is hidden; the **Code** buttons reveal any step. Every number in this report is computed by this run; none is typed into the text.


## 1. Setup and configuration

Loads packages, sources the helper functions in `03_R_functions/`, applies the run configuration from `run_config.R`, and defines the two sub-seasons (pot-closure and all-gear). Every user-selectable toggle for this run lives in `run_config.R`.

```{r config, results='hide'}
###############################################################################
# Crab Creel Estimation - Westport / Grays Harbor  |  Pooled CPUE Model
# Any season, part-season or span (2024-25 is the development test season)
# Pipeline code: last numbered tag v7.9 (2026-07-12); versioned by date since, and the
# model of record is this code as of 2026-09-29 (B44 to B51; see the development history)
#
# Estimates total recreational Dungeness crab harvest at Westport / Grays Harbor
# from a single pooled CPUE process shared across gear types. Three population
# components are estimated independently and summed to the port total:
#   1. Shore crabbers (dock + jetty + beach)   BSS + PE
#   2. Private boat crabbers                    BSS + PE
#   3. Commercial/charter boats                 commercial census + charter expansion
# Two gear-regime sub-seasons per season (build_subseasons(); the dates are run_config's
# pot_closure_start / pot_closure_end): a pot closure (non-pot gear only) and all-gear (pots
# allowed); a multi-season span has one pair per season. "Pot closure" was formerly labeled
# "ring-net only"; non-pot gear other than ring nets is also legal, so the name was
# a misnomer. The internal key stays "ring_net_only" for output-filename continuity.
#
# CURRENT STATE: both fitted components run on the gear-DEPLOYMENT effort
# unit (h = number_of_gear, L = tau), via the shared 03_R_functions/bss_effort_spec.R.
# Helper functions live in 03_R_functions/ (sourced wholesale in the setup chunk),
# and every user-selectable toggle lives in run_config.R (the single file you edit);
# this .Rmd's params block holds only model-internal tuning (sampler settings, gate
# and AR-selector thresholds).
#
# KEY FEATURES: adaptive AR(1) temporal resolution; B1_C weekend CPUE effect;
# Method v2.0: derived shore turnover tau_shore and calibration boat turnover with a shared
# tau_bar; dynamic per-stratum crabbing fraction f with a combo share c; zero-inflated NB2
# shore catch; commercial census + charter expansion; the single-section level
# hierarchies collapsed (A31, T2.5). L_effective / day length only under a time unit (B55);
# data-driven R_G prior;
# gear-deployment effort scale (R_G_boat / tau_boat, tau_shore); scale-aware
# convergence gate; the expected catch from the generated quantities and, since B46, the
# predictive catch drawn after the fit from the fitted zero-inflated NB
# (03_R_functions/bss_predictive_catch.R); every chain started with init_r = 0.5 (B51).
#
# FULL CHANGE LOG (every version, newest first, with working notes):
#   07_documentation/BSS-GH-pooled-CPUE-model-development-history.md
# METHOD REFERENCE (the published method of record):
#   07_documentation/BSS-GH-pooled-CPUE-model-documentation.md
###############################################################################

# ===========================================================================
# 0. SETUP
# ===========================================================================

# 2026-09-28 (B46): one package list and loader (03_R_functions/bss_packages.R): renv.lock's
# versions when renv is active, a stop naming the package when one cannot be had.
if (!requireNamespace("here", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Package 'here' is missing: run renv::restore() first.", call. = FALSE)
source(here::here("03_R_functions", "bss_packages.R")); bss_load_packages()
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
purrr::walk(list.files(here("03_R_functions"), full.names = TRUE), source)

run_date <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")
# Unique per-run subfolder so same-day runs never overwrite each other.
# run_config$run_tag (set in run_config.R, or by run_rg_sweep.R) names the folder,
# e.g. pooled-CPUE-run5; blank falls back to a HHMMSS timestamp. The `knit:` block
# above stashes that timestamp in options(crab_run_tag=) so a standalone RStudio
# knit writes its HTML and this driver's CSVs into the SAME folder.
# 2026-09-28 (B46): bss_output_dir() also refuses a tag naming a season the run does not
# model, never writes into a folder that already holds a run, and makes the tag path-safe.
output_dir <- bss_output_dir("pooled-CPUE-", if (exists("run_config")) run_config else NULL)

# timer_start() / timer_stop() and their timing state now live in
# 03_R_functions/bss_timers.R (auto-sourced). Read collected timings with
# bss_timer_log(). Extracted; behavior unchanged.

run_start_time <- Sys.time()

# ===========================================================================
# 0.1 PARAMETERS
# ===========================================================================

params <- list(
  # NOTE: every user-selectable toggle (season window, structural dates, catch
  # groups, day-typing, effort unit, incomplete-trip filter, I/E settings,
  # holidays, and the model-behavior levers such as collapse_mu_hier) now lives in
  # run_config.R, the single source of truth, and is applied as an override below.
  # This list holds ONLY this model's internal tuning: the Stan model file, the
  # per-fit sampler settings, the convergence-gate thresholds, and the adaptive
  # AR-selector thresholds. These rarely change and legitimately differ from the
  # gear-resolved model, so they stay with the model rather than in run_config.

  # --- Stan model file ---
  bss_model_file    = "crab_bss_pooled.stan",

  # --- Shared reader behavior (merged fetch_crab_data, 2026-08-01) ---
  # TRUE = the historical pooled reader: drop private_boat interviews with no
  # positive gear_time_total. (The gear-resolved driver sets FALSE.)
  boat_require_gear_time = TRUE,

  # --- BSS sampler defaults ---
  bss_adapt_delta   = 0.9,

  # --- BSS convergence tuning (extra iterations for longer sub-seasons / daily AR) ---
  bss_iter_default          = 3000,
  bss_warmup_default        = 1500,
  bss_max_treedepth_default = 10,
  bss_iter_shore_allgear    = 5000,
  bss_warmup_shore_allgear  = 2500,

  # Per-fit treedepth / adapt_delta overrides (v6.1, ported from gear-resolved
  # v5.2). The shore all-gear daily-AR posterior is the densest geometry and
  # saturated max_treedepth=10 on 91.6% of iterations in the 2026-04-08 run;
  # ring-net fits are data-sparse and benefit from tighter adaptation. Any fit
  # without an override uses the *_default values.
  # 2026-09-08: production now caps shore all-gear at WEEKLY (P_n 44, not 289), so
  # these settings, tuned for the daily geometry, are retained as headroom rather
  # than necessity; they also cover the ladder, which can still fit this component
  # at daily. Do not trim them without re-checking a daily rung.
  bss_treedepth_shore_allgear = 14,
  bss_delta_shore_allgear     = 0.95,
  bss_treedepth_ringnet       = 12,
  bss_delta_ringnet           = 0.95,

  # v6.2: boat all-gear sampler tuning. The boat all-gear fit failed in the
  # 2026-04-08 run (5998 divergences, R-hat 1.074, n_eff 76) under defaults.
  # treedepth_pct was 0, so divergences came from step size: adapt_delta is
  # raised to 0.99 (primary lever) and max_treedepth to 13 (buffer), with more
  # iterations to give n_eff a chance to clear 400.
  bss_iter_boat_allgear       = 5000,
  bss_warmup_boat_allgear     = 2500,
  bss_treedepth_boat_allgear  = 13,
  bss_delta_boat_allgear      = 0.99,

  # bss_min_interviews MOVED to run_config.R (improvement 6, 2026-08-25). It lived here,
  # in params_model, which is merged ON TOP of run_config -- so a value set in run_config
  # was silently overridden by this one. Both the pre-filter floor
  # (bss_min_interviews) and the new post-filter floor (bss_min_interviews_fitted) are
  # now single-sourced from run_config.R.

  # --- B1.8: SCALE-AWARE convergence gate thresholds --------------------------
  # The gate rejects a BSS fit whose divergent transitions have BIASED the
  # reported totals, while accepting a fit whose divergences are diffuse and
  # harmless (Betancourt 2017). It measures the divergent draws' impact on each
  # reported TOTAL in units of that total's posterior SD (scale-invariant):
  #   impact = |median(all_draws) - median(bulk_draws)| / sd(all_draws)
  # A fit passes when max(impact_C, impact_E) is below max_divergence_total_impact_sd,
  # with a hard divergent-FRACTION backstop (max_divergence_fraction). See the
  # model documentation and development history for the full B1.8 rationale.
  max_divergence_total_impact_sd = 0.10,
  # P7 (2026-07-12): tightened from 0.15 to 0.05. The scale-aware impact test above
  # (max_divergence_total_impact_sd) is the primary gate; this fraction is only a hard
  # backstop, and 0.15 was too loose to defend for a publication method (a fit at ~14%
  # divergences would have passed as BSS). 0.05 matches the gear-resolved model. The
  # 2026-07-11 pooled fits (0.54%, 2.23%, 2.5% divergences) are all under 5%, so this
  # changes no current gating decision; divergences indicate biased HMC exploration
  # (Betancourt 2017), so the backstop belongs near 5%.
  max_divergence_fraction        = 0.05,

  # D37 (2026-09-29): the deprecated max_divergences / max_divergence_distortion keys were
  # removed; nothing read them. The level-normalized distortion is still COMPUTED and
  # reported in convergence_report.csv (distortion_C / distortion_E), without a threshold.

  # --- Adaptive AR temporal-resolution thresholds -----------------------------
  # The model selects the finest AR resolution the data can support:
  #   daily:   effort obs on >= ar_daily_min_coverage of days AND >= ar_daily_min_obs
  #   weekly:  >= ar_weekly_min_per_week effort obs per week on average
  #   monthly: fallback for sparse data
  ar_daily_min_coverage  = 0.25,
  ar_daily_min_obs       = 20,
  ar_weekly_min_per_week = 1.5

  # v6.5 (B1): per-population cap on AR resolution. The map now lives in run_config.R
  # (ar_max_resolution$pooled) so both models' caps sit in one place; this model's cap
  # is selected from it just after the merge below (P5, 2026-07-12). The boat
  # (trailer-count) effort series is too weakly informative for daily AR, so the boat
  # is capped at MONTHLY; the shore is capped at WEEKLY for all-gear and BIWEEKLY for the
  # pot closure (both adopted 2026-09-07 after the ladder, and the evidence is in Section 18
  # of the method document). A population absent from the map defaults to "daily" (no cap).
  # Read ar_max_resolution$pooled in run_config.R for the shipped values; the cap only ever
  # COARSENS, so a cap finer than the data-driven pick is ignored.
  # (D37, 2026-09-29: ie_use_all_dates_for_diagnostics was removed; nothing read it.)
)

# --- Run-level config from run_config.R (single source of truth) --------------
# run_config.R owns every user-selectable toggle (season window, structural dates,
# catch groups, day-typing, effort unit, filters, I/E settings, holidays, the AR
# resolution map, and the model-behavior toggles). When launched via run_estimation.R
# the orchestrator has already defined `run_config`; when this .Rmd is knit standalone
# the guard below sources run_config.R so the same toggles are used either way.
if (!exists("run_config")) source(here::here("run_config.R"))
# P5 (2026-07-12): run_config is the BASE parameter set; this model's internal tuning
# (defined above) is layered on top. The two key sets are disjoint, so the merge order
# carries intent only (run_config is the base, the model updates it with its specifics).
params <- modifyList(run_config, params)
# 2026-08-30: the ONE sanctioned way for run_config to reach a sampler setting, applied
# AFTER the merge because params_model wins it (03_R_functions/bss_sampler_override.R).
# Unset in production, so this is a no-op on a normal run; it errors loudly on a
# non-sampler key rather than silently dropping it.
params <- bss_apply_sampler_override(params, model_label = "pooled")
# Select this model's AR-resolution cap from the shared per-model map in run_config.
params$ar_max_resolution <- run_config$ar_max_resolution$pooled

# Crabbing holidays now live in an editable workbook (04_input_files/crabbing_holidays.xlsx),
# read here via 03_R_functions/read_crabbing_holidays.R and filtered to season_filter, so the
# season update is a spreadsheet edit rather than a code edit. Populate params$crabbing_holiday_dates
# ONCE here; every downstream consumer (classify_day_type, prep_days_crab, estimate_comm_charter)
# reads it from params unchanged. Kept as a bare object too so inline references still resolve.
params$crabbing_holiday_dates <- read_crabbing_holidays(params)
crabbing_holiday_dates <- params$crabbing_holiday_dates


# Dungeness only. The Red Rock catch group and its estimate_red_rock switch were removed
# 2026-09-28 (B44): never shipped on, and never validated (turning it on summed the two
# species in the monthly tables). The loops over catch_groups stay, over one group.
catch_groups <- "Dungeness_Kept"

# Sub-seasons split by the pot-closure window (03_R_functions/build_subseasons.R).
# The pot closure is when pots are not legal (non-pot gear only); its window is set
# explicitly in run_config (pot_closure_start / pot_closure_end). For the current
# config (closure at the season start) this returns the historical two sub-seasons
# with unchanged internal names ("ring_net_only" is the pot-closure key, kept for
# output-filename continuity; display_name is "Pot closure"), so keys and filenames
# do not change. A mid-season closure adds pre/post all-gear periods automatically.
# Model logic keys off ss$gear_regime ("pot_closure" | "all_gear"), never ss$name.
subseasons <- build_subseasons(params)
for (ss in subseasons) {
  cat(sprintf("Sub-season: %-26s %s to %s (%d days)\n",
              paste0(ss$display_name, " [", ss$name, "]"),
              ss$start, ss$end, as.integer(ss$end - ss$start + 1)))
}
cat(sprintf("Catch groups: %s\n", paste(catch_groups, collapse = ", ")))

# Sub-season aggregation is now GENERAL (2026-07-13): the PE port summary, the catch-by-
# mode table, and the final harvest table sum over whatever sub-seasons build_subseasons
# produced (via pe_pop_sum / pe_port_total below), rather than the hardcoded historical
# pair. A mid-season pot closure (which adds all_gear_pre / all_gear_post keys) is
# therefore handled end-to-end. That general path has NOT yet been validated against a
# fitted run, so emit a loud note when the sub-season set departs from the historical
# pair; verify the port total against the per-component PE table before citing such a run.
ss_name_set <- vapply(subseasons, function(z) z$name, character(1))
if (!setequal(ss_name_set, c("ring_net_only", "all_gear"))) {
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "\n*** NOTE: non-historical sub-season set {%s}. The report aggregation sums over all ",
    "sub-seasons per population, but this configuration has not been validated against a ",
    "fitted run; verify the port total against the per-component PE table before citing. ***\n"),
    paste(ss_name_set, collapse = ", ")))
}

# --- Generalized PE aggregation over the sub-season set (build_subseasons) -----------
# Sum a PE field over all sub-seasons of a population so the port total, the by-mode
# table, and the final-table PE rows follow build_subseasons instead of a fixed 5-row
# layout. These close over the run globals `pe_all` (populated by the PE loop) and
# `subseasons`; they are only called after the PE loop, so pe_all exists by call time.
# pe_all keys are "<population>_<subseason-name>"; a missing key or field contributes 0.
pe_field   <- function(key, field) pe_all[[key]][[field]] %||% 0
pe_pop_sum <- function(pop, field)
  sum(vapply(subseasons, function(ss) pe_field(paste0(pop, "_", ss$name), field), numeric(1)), na.rm = TRUE)
pe_port_total <- function(field)  # na.rm matches the baseline sum([1:5], na.rm=TRUE):
  sum(pe_pop_sum("shore", field), pe_pop_sum("private_boat", field),
      pe_field("comm_charter", field), na.rm = TRUE)


# Every step below calls a function in 03_R_functions/ (sourced above): fetch_crab_data(),
# fetch_ie_data() and estimate_shore_turnover() (bss_day_length.R), prep_days_crab(),
# prep_population_summary(), run_pe_pooled(), prep_bss_crab_pooled(), estimate_comm_charter()
# and the diagnostics writers. README-R-functions.md lists every file. (Stub comments that
# described each function as "extracted verbatim" from this file, some of them describing a
# day-length L that is no longer the expansion factor, were removed 2026-09-29.)

```

```{r config-show, echo=FALSE}
# 2026-09-29: the configuration as a TABLE a reader can check against run_config.R. Until this
# date Section 1 printed nothing; the resolved values lived only in run_parameters.txt.
.git <- function(args) tryCatch(suppressWarnings(system2("git", c("-C", here::here(), args), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)),
                                error = function(e) character(0))
run_git_sha   <- (.git(c("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")) %||% "unavailable")[1]
run_git_dirty <- length(.git(c("status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"))) > 0
.ss_tab <- paste(vapply(subseasons, function(ss) sprintf("%s %s to %s", ss$display_name, ss$start, ss$end), ""), collapse = "; ")
.fmt <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) "(unset)" else if (is.list(x)) paste(names(x), vapply(x, function(v) paste(format(v), collapse = "/"), ""), sep = " = ", collapse = "; ") else paste(format(x), collapse = ", ")
config_disp <- data.frame(check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  Setting = c("Season(s)", "Estimation window", "Sub-seasons", "Shore effort unit", "Model",
              "Chains / cores / seed / init_r", "Iterations (shore all-gear; boat all-gear; others)",
              "Convergence gate", "AR cap (pooled)", "Level hierarchy, one section (A31)",
              "Shore turnover prior", "Boat turnover prior", "Shared turnover", "Crabbing fraction f",
              "Marine hazard term", "Opener covariates", "Census / charter", "PE unsampled cells",
              "Code (git)", "Output folder"),
  Value = c(paste(params$season_filter, collapse = " + "),
            sprintf("%s to %s", params$est_date_start, params$est_date_end), .ss_tab,
            params$shore_effort_unit %||% "gear-deployments", params$bss_model_file,
            sprintf("%s / %s / %s / %s", params$bss_chains, params$bss_cores, params$bss_seed, params$bss_init_r %||% 2),
            sprintf("%s (warmup %s); %s (warmup %s); %s (warmup %s)", params$bss_iter_shore_allgear, params$bss_warmup_shore_allgear,
                    params$bss_iter_boat_allgear, params$bss_warmup_boat_allgear, params$bss_iter_default, params$bss_warmup_default),
            sprintf("R-hat < 1.01, n_eff > 400, divergent fraction < %s, impact < %s SD",
                    params$max_divergence_fraction, params$max_divergence_total_impact_sd),
            .fmt(params$ar_max_resolution), as.character(params$mu_hier_collapse_single %||% "both"),
            sprintf("%s (resolved in Section 3.1)", .fmt(params$tau_shore_prior_mu)),
            sprintf("%s, log-SD %s (resolved in Section 3.1)", .fmt(params$tau_boat_prior_mu), .fmt(params$tau_boat_prior_sigma)),
            .fmt(params$shared_tau),
            sprintf("dynamic = %s, strata = %s, source = %s", .fmt(params$crab_fraction_dynamic), .fmt(params$crab_fraction_strata), .fmt(params$crab_fraction_source)),
            sprintf("mode = %s; boat = %s; shore = %s; sub-seasons = %s", .fmt(params$marine_hazard_mode), .fmt(params$marine_hazard_manual_boat),
                    if (length(params$marine_hazard_manual_shore)) .fmt(params$marine_hazard_manual_shore) else "none", .fmt(params$marine_hazard_gear_regimes)),
            .fmt(params$opener_covariate_mode %||% "off"),
            sprintf("census_expansion = %s; charter_frame = %s; charter_expansion = %s; census_uncertainty = %s",
                    .fmt(params$census_expansion), .fmt(params$charter_frame), .fmt(params$charter_expansion), .fmt(params$census_uncertainty)),
            sprintf("effort fill = %s; CPUE fill = %s; variance = %s", .fmt(params$pe_empty_effort_stratum), .fmt(params$pe_empty_stratum), .fmt(params$pe_variance)),
            sprintf("%s%s", run_git_sha, if (run_git_dirty) " (working tree has uncommitted changes)" else ""),
            basename(output_dir)))
report_table(config_disp, caption = "This run's configuration (run_config.R merged with the driver's model settings). Every key is in run_parameters.txt.")
```

## 2. Data ingestion

Reads the effort counts, crabber interviews, the commercial tally and charter roster, the ingress/egress (I/E) surveys, the sampler contacts and the OSP boat counts, and classifies each interview as shore, private boat, or commercial/charter. The table after this step counts what each stream delivered for this run's window.

```{r load-data, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.0 LOAD DATA ----
timer_start("1_load_data")
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n LOADING DATA\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
dwg <- fetch_crab_data(params)
ie_data <- fetch_ie_data(params)
# Review item 1 (2026-09-08): the crabbing-fraction classification rows come from the
# sampler contacts (dwg$boat_contacts, every private boat approached) and/or the egress
# columns of the I/E workbook, per params$crab_fraction_source. See crab_fraction.R.
params$crab_fraction_rows <- crab_fraction_source_rows(dwg, ie_data, params)

# --- Review item 2 (2026-09-08): the shore turnover at the hours the counts were taken.
# Derived from the I/E interval rows (the workbook's `time` column) and the shore count
# hours EVERY run and written to shore_turnover_*.csv; it becomes the prior centre only
# when run_config sets tau_shore_prior_mu = "derived" (bss_resolve_tau_shore_prior), because
# it moves the shore component by the ratio of the two priors (about 1.47 on 2024-25).
shore_turnover <- estimate_shore_turnover(attr(ie_data, "ie_intervals"), dwg$shore_effort, params)
write_shore_turnover(shore_turnover, output_dir)
params <- bss_resolve_tau_shore_prior(params, shore_turnover)

# --- 2026-09-09: the sampler shifts and the shift-coverage diagnostic. The crabbing
# fraction is read from boats contacted DURING a shift (about 9:45 to 15:50); this writes
# how much of the day's boat returns the shift covers (from the boat I/E return profile)
# and whether the trip-type mix drifts with the hour inside the shift. Diagnostic only;
# guarded so a missing shifts file cannot break a run (03_R_functions/sampler_shifts.R).
sampler_shifts <- tryCatch(fetch_sampler_shifts(params),
                           error = function(e) { bss_warn("sampler shifts", paste("Sampler shifts skipped:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })
shift_coverage <- tryCatch(diagnose_shift_coverage(sampler_shifts, ie_data, dwg$boat_contacts_detail, params, output_dir = output_dir),
                           error = function(e) { bss_warn("sampler shifts", paste("Shift coverage diagnostic skipped:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })

# --- Phase 0: OSP Westport boat-count ingest + overlap calibration ---
# NOT diagnostic only since 2026-09-08: under tau_boat_prior_mu = "calibration" the overlap
# result sets the boat turnover prior centre (bss_resolve_tau_boat_prior below), and an error
# caught here falls back to tau_boat_prior_mu_fallback (3.03, the 2024-25 calibration; D36,
# 2026-09-29), and both the error and the fallback go to the run-warnings log (bss_warn),
# which the report prints in its last section.
# fetch_osp_boat_counts() and diagnose_osp_trailer_overlap() live in 03_R_functions/
# (auto-sourced). The diagnostic writes osp_trailer_overlap_calibration.csv,
# osp_trailer_overlap_pairs.csv, osp_coverage_audit.csv and osp_trailer_overlap.png to
# output_dir. osp_boat is the per-day OSP series (boat_effort schema) that Phase 1
# consumes as a second boat effort stream. Guarded so a missing file cannot break a run.
osp_boat <- tryCatch(fetch_osp_boat_counts(params),
                     error = function(e) { bss_warn("OSP", paste("OSP ingest skipped:", conditionMessage(e))); NULL })
osp_overlap <- tryCatch(diagnose_osp_trailer_overlap(osp_boat, params, output_dir = output_dir),
                        error = function(e) { bss_warn("OSP", paste("OSP overlap diagnostic skipped:", conditionMessage(e))); NULL })
# improvement 8: OSP crab-ONLY counts (a LOWER bound on the crabbing fraction f, because
# OSP labels combo trips by the non-crab fishery). Lifted here so both the PE and the BSS
# read the same rows from one file read. Empty until the crab-only column exists, in which
# case every f feature is inert and f behaves exactly as it does today.
params$osp_crab_rows <- attr(osp_boat, "osp_crab_rows")
if (!is.null(params$osp_crab_rows) && nrow(params$osp_crab_rows) > 0)
  cat(sprintf("  OSP crab-only rows lifted for the f lower bound: %d day(s).\n",
              nrow(params$osp_crab_rows)))
# B48 (2026-09-28): the per-day crab-only rows as the model reads them (the boats SAMPLED, the
# rate behind that n and where it came from), so the f floor can be audited day by day.
if (!is.null(params$osp_crab_rows) && nrow(params$osp_crab_rows) > 0)
  tryCatch(utils::write.csv(dplyr::mutate(params$osp_crab_rows, crab_only_share = osp_crab_only / osp_total),
                            file.path(output_dir, "osp_crab_only_daily.csv"), row.names = FALSE),
           error = function(e) bss_warn("OSP", paste("osp_crab_only_daily.csv not written:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"))

# --- Review item 3 + 5 (2026-09-08): resolve the boat turnover prior centre from THIS
# window's OSP/trailer overlap when tau_boat_prior_mu = "calibration". The resolved
# number replaces params$tau_boat_prior_mu, so the PE (run_pe_pooled), the shared-turnover
# prior (bss_effort_spec -> bss_shared_tau_data) and the tau-sensitivity projection all
# expand the trailer count by one quantity. See 03_R_functions/bss_turnover_prior.R.
params <- bss_resolve_tau_boat_prior(params, osp_overlap)

# --- Fit L_effective regression ---
# B55 (2026-09-29): only when a day length is used (a time-denominated shore unit, or
# day_length_diagnostics = TRUE). Under gear-deployments nothing reads it; the I/E survey's
# job is the shore turnover above (shore_turnover_*.csv) and the I/E observation stream.
L_eff_model <- NULL
if(isTRUE(params$use_ie_day_length) && bss_needs_day_length(params) && nrow(ie_data) > 0) {
  L_eff_model <- estimate_L_effective(ie_data, params)
  if(!is.null(L_eff_model)) {
    # Save regression diagnostics
    if(!is.null(L_eff_model$detail)) {
      write.csv(L_eff_model$detail,
                file.path(output_dir, "L_effective_ie_detail.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
timer_stop("1_load_data")


```

```{r inputs-show, echo=FALSE}
# 2026-09-29: what each input stream delivered, so a thin or missing stream is visible here
# rather than only as a PE fallback or a prior-only parameter much later.
.in_win <- function(d) { d <- as.Date(d); d >= as.Date(params$est_date_start) & d <= as.Date(params$est_date_end) }
.int_n <- table(factor(dwg$interview$population, levels = c("shore", "private_boat", "comm_charter")))
.ie_n  <- if (nrow(ie_data)) table(factor(ie_data$population, levels = c("shore", "private_boat"))) else c(shore = 0, private_boat = 0)
inputs_disp <- data.frame(check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  Stream = c("Shore gear counts", "Private-boat trailer counts", "Interviews: shore", "Interviews: private boat",
             "Interviews: commercial/charter", "Sampler boat contacts (crabbing fraction)", "OSP returning-boat days",
             "OSP crab-only days", "Commercial/charter tally days", "Charter roster trips",
             "I/E survey days: shore (all seasons)", "I/E survey days: boat (all seasons)"),
  Rows = c(nrow(dwg$shore_effort), nrow(dwg$boat_effort), .int_n[["shore"]], .int_n[["private_boat"]], .int_n[["comm_charter"]],
           nrow(dwg$boat_contacts_detail %||% data.frame()),
           if (is.null(osp_boat)) 0 else nrow(osp_boat), nrow(params$osp_crab_rows %||% data.frame()),
           sum(.in_win(dwg$comm_tally$date)), nrow(dwg$charter_roster %||% data.frame()),
           .ie_n[["shore"]], .ie_n[["private_boat"]]),
  `Days in window` = c(dplyr::n_distinct(dwg$shore_effort$event_date), dplyr::n_distinct(dwg$boat_effort$event_date),
                       dplyr::n_distinct(dwg$interview$event_date[dwg$interview$population == "shore"]),
                       dplyr::n_distinct(dwg$interview$event_date[dwg$interview$population == "private_boat"]),
                       dplyr::n_distinct(dwg$interview$event_date[dwg$interview$population == "comm_charter"]),
                       dplyr::n_distinct((dwg$boat_contacts_detail %||% data.frame(event_date = as.Date(character())))$event_date),
                       if (is.null(osp_boat)) 0 else sum(.in_win(unique(osp_boat$event_date))),
                       nrow(params$osp_crab_rows %||% data.frame()),
                       sum(.in_win(dwg$comm_tally$date)),
                       if (is.null(dwg$charter_roster)) 0 else sum(.in_win(unique(as.Date(dwg$charter_roster$date)))),
                       if (nrow(ie_data)) sum(.in_win(unique(ie_data$event_date[ie_data$population == "shore"]))) else 0,
                       if (nrow(ie_data)) sum(.in_win(unique(ie_data$event_date[ie_data$population == "private_boat"]))) else 0))
report_table(inputs_disp, digits = 0, caption = paste(
  "What each input stream delivered. 'Rows' counts records as read (the I/E rows span every season in the",
  "workbook, because the shore turnover pools them; D24); 'Days in window' counts distinct days inside the",
  "estimation window. The OSP crab-only column is optional (B48): zero days means OSP has not delivered it."))
```

## 3. Input diagnostics: effort and CPUE

The raw inputs before any modelling: the shore gear counts and the private-boat trailer counts (each point is a day's MEAN count, the quantity the effort likelihood is scaled to; days with more counts are larger), the OSP returning-boat totals, and the interview catch rate per gear deployment, the unit the model uses. Look for gaps (a run of unsampled weekends) and anomalies (an implausible spike).

```{r input-figures, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# ---- 7.1 DIAGNOSTIC PLOTS ----
timer_start("2_diagnostic_plots")
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n DIAGNOSTIC PLOTS\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

days_full <- prep_days_crab(params$est_date_start, params$est_date_end,
                            params, L_eff_model = L_eff_model)

# Plot 1: Shore gear count timeseries
p_shore_effort <- dwg$shore_effort |>
  group_by(event_date) |>
  # 2026-09-29: the day's MEAN count (it was the SUM over the day's 1 to 3 counts, which
  # inflated a multi-count day 2 to 3x on the page; the model never used the sum).
  summarise(mean_gear = mean(count_quantity), n_counts = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(day_type = classify_day_type(event_date, params)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = event_date, y = mean_gear, color = day_type, size = n_counts)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  pot_closure_markers(params, labels = TRUE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1,3), breaks = 1:3, name = "Counts that day") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Shore gear in the water (Floats 20 and 17-21), mean per count",
       subtitle = "Float 17-21 filled by the month's time-paired ratio where only Float 20 was counted (shore_f17_fill)",
       x = "Date", y = "Gear deployments per count", color = "Day type") +
  theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_shore_effort_timeseries.png"), p_shore_effort, width = 10, height = 6)

# Plot 2: Boat trailer count timeseries
p_boat_effort <- dwg$boat_effort |>
  group_by(event_date) |>
  summarise(value = mean(count_quantity), n_counts = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(day_type = classify_day_type(event_date, params), series = "Trailers, mean per count") |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (!is.null(osp_boat) && nrow(osp_boat))
      osp_boat |> group_by(event_date) |> summarise(value = sum(count_quantity), n_counts = 1L, .groups = "drop") |>
        dplyr::filter(event_date >= as.Date(params$est_date_start), event_date <= as.Date(params$est_date_end)) |>
        mutate(day_type = classify_day_type(event_date, params), series = "OSP returning private boats, daily total")
    else NULL) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = event_date, y = value, color = day_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  pot_closure_markers(params, labels = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~series, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Private-boat effort streams", x = "Date", y = NULL, color = "Day type") +
  theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_boat_effort_timeseries.png"), p_boat_effort, width = 10, height = 8)

# Plot 3: CPUE by population, per GEAR DEPLOYMENT (2026-09-29: it was per crabber-hour, the
# unit the model left in v7.7), as the day's ratio of sums, the estimator the PE uses.
cpue_data <- dwg$interview |>
  mutate(.g = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(number_of_gear))) |>
  filter(is.finite(.g), .g > 0, dungeness_kept >= 0, population %in% c("shore", "private_boat")) |>
  group_by(event_date, population) |>
  summarise(cpue = sum(dungeness_kept) / sum(.g), n_int = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(day_type = classify_day_type(event_date, params),
         population = dplyr::recode(population, shore = "Shore", private_boat = "Private boat"))

p_cpue <- cpue_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = event_date, y = cpue, color = day_type)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_int), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, span = 0.3, se = TRUE, color = "grey30") +
  pot_closure_markers(params, labels = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~population, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.8, 3), name = "Interviews") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(title = "Interview catch rate: Dungeness kept per gear deployment (daily ratio of sums)",
       x = "Date", y = "Crab per gear deployment", color = "Day type") +
  theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_cpue_timeseries.png"), p_cpue, width = 10, height = 8)

# Plot 4: Gear counts by month and day type (boxplot of the day's mean count)
p_effort_month <- dwg$shore_effort |>
  group_by(event_date) |>
  summarise(mean_gear = mean(count_quantity), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(day_type = classify_day_type(event_date, params),
         month_label = factor(format(event_date, "%Y-%m"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = month_label, y = mean_gear, fill = day_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Shore gear counts by month and day type (mean per count)",
       x = "Month", y = "Gear deployments per count", fill = "Day type") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_effort_by_month.png"), p_effort_month, width = 12, height = 6)

# L_effective regression and day-length plots: ONLY under a time-denominated unit (B55). Under
# gear-deployments nothing reads a day length, and these two figures used to present one as the
# quantity "propagated into the Stan model", which it is not.
if(bss_needs_day_length(params) && !is.null(L_eff_model) && !is.null(L_eff_model$detail) && nrow(L_eff_model$detail) >= 3) {
  # Predict L over the estimation window (2026-09-28, B46: it was a fixed 2024 calendar year,
  # so the prediction line and the I/E points sat on different dates in every other season)
  viz_dates <- seq.Date(as.Date(params$est_date_start), as.Date(params$est_date_end), by = "day")
  viz_pred <- L_eff_model$predict_fn(viz_dates, rep("weekday", length(viz_dates)))
  viz_pred_wkend <- L_eff_model$predict_fn(viz_dates, rep("weekend", length(viz_dates)))

  p_L_regression <- ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(data = tibble(date = viz_dates, lo = viz_pred$L_mu * exp(-1.96 * viz_pred$L_sigma),
                              hi = viz_pred$L_mu * exp(1.96 * viz_pred$L_sigma)),
                aes(x = date, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, fill = "steelblue") +
    geom_line(data = tibble(date = viz_dates, L = viz_pred$L_mu),
              aes(x = date, y = L, color = "Weekday prediction"), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = tibble(date = viz_dates, L = viz_pred_wkend$L_mu),
              aes(x = date, y = L, color = "Weekend prediction"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(data = L_eff_model$detail,
               aes(x = event_date, y = L_effective, shape = day_type_group), size = 3) +
    labs(title = "L_effective Regression (log-scale quadratic + day type)",
         subtitle = sprintf("Method: %s | n=%d I/E days | Shaded = 95%% prediction interval",
                            L_eff_model$method, L_eff_model$n_obs),
         x = "Date", y = "L_effective (hours)", color = "Prediction", shape = "I/E day type") +
    theme_bw()
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_L_effective_regression.png"), p_L_regression, width = 12, height = 6)
}

# Day length comparison (civil twilight vs regression), time units only (B55)

p_day_length <- days_full |>

### 3.1 The expansion factors: shore and boat turnover

A creel count is a snapshot, so each population's daily effort is the counted gear times a **turnover** `tau`: how many gear deployments pass through one counted slot in a day. It is the largest single lever on the total (the shore and boat components scale with it one for one), and both centres are **derived from data every run**, not set. The shore turnover comes from the I/E survey's `time` column, as arrivals over the presence at the hours the counts were actually taken; the boat turnover from the days OSP counted every returning private boat and the samplers counted trailers. With `shared_tau = TRUE` each fit estimates one season-level turnover `tau_bar` around this centre (Section 12.3). **Read the in-window shore value**: the derived centre pools every I/E day in the workbook (CHANGE_REGISTER D24), and where this window's own days give a different value the shore component moves with it. No day length appears in the expansion (B55); `L_effective` in hours is computed only under a time-denominated effort unit.

```{r turnover-show, echo=FALSE}
.st <- shore_turnover
turnover_disp <- data.frame(check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  Population = c("Shore", "Private boat"),
  `Prior centre used` = c(sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(params$tau_shore_prior_mu)), sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(params$tau_boat_prior_mu))),
  `Prior log-SD` = c(sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(params$tau_shore_prior_sigma)), sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(params$tau_boat_prior_sigma %||% 0.5))),
  Source = c(params$tau_shore_prior_source %||% "config", params$tau_boat_prior_source %||% "config"),
  `Alternatives this run` = c(
    if (!is.null(.st)) sprintf("this window's own %d I/E day(s): %s; geometric mean %.3f; arrivals over PEAK presence (the retired 1.7 quantity) %.3f",
                               .st$n_days_in_window %||% 0L, if (is.finite(.st$tau_in_window %||% NA)) sprintf("%.3f", .st$tau_in_window) else "n/a",
                               .st$tau_geomean %||% NA, .st$tau_peak %||% NA) else "derivation unavailable",
    if (!is.null(osp_overlap$calibration)) paste(sprintf("%s %.2f (n = %d, r = %.3f)", osp_overlap$calibration$trailer_metric,
                                                       osp_overlap$calibration$implied_turnover, osp_overlap$calibration$n,
                                                       osp_overlap$calibration$corr), collapse = "; ") else "no OSP/trailer overlap"))
report_table(turnover_disp, caption = paste(
  "The turnover prior centres this run used and where each came from. A 'fallback' source means the per-run",
  "derivation could not run and the 2024-25 value was used instead (Section 16 records it)."))
```

```{r ie-analysis, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# ---- 7.1b I/E ANALYSIS ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n I/E ANALYSIS\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

if(nrow(ie_data) > 0) {
  ie_validation <- ie_data |>
    filter(population == "shore") |>
    left_join(
      dwg$shore_effort |>
        group_by(event_date) |>
        summarise(mean_gear = mean(count_quantity), n_counts = n(), .groups = "drop"),
      by = "event_date"
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(mean_gear), mean_gear > 0)

  if(nrow(ie_validation) > 0) {
    # Shared helper (03_R_functions/bss_day_length.R) so the [9, 17] cap lives in
    # exactly one place; this previously hardcoded a 16.0 cap.
    # B55: the civil-twilight comparison only where a day length is used (suncalc).
    ie_validation$day_length_ct <- if (bss_needs_day_length(params)) bss_day_length_civil(ie_validation$event_date, params) else NA_real_

    summ_shore_full <- prep_population_summary(dwg, "shore", params$est_date_start, params$est_date_end, params)
    cpg <- summ_shore_full$crabbers_per_gear

    ie_validation <- ie_validation |>
      mutate(
        gear_est_crabber_hrs = mean_gear * cpg * day_length_ct,
        f_temporal = ie_crabber_hours / gear_est_crabber_hrs,
        pct_error = (gear_est_crabber_hrs - ie_crabber_hours) / ie_crabber_hours * 100
      )

    cat("\n  I/E vs Gear-Count Comparison (paired days):\n")
    for(i in 1:nrow(ie_validation)) {
      r <- ie_validation[i,]
      cat(sprintf("  %-12s %-8s IE=%.0f Gear_est=%.0f f=%.2f\n",
                  as.character(r$event_date), r$day_type, r$ie_crabber_hours,
                  r$gear_est_crabber_hrs, r$f_temporal))
    }
    # 2026-08-27: report the deployment-scale columns too. ie_trips is the observation the
    # shore likelihood consumes under gear-deployments (improvement 1/A); turnover is what
    # `L` carries there; hours_per_trip is their ratio and should sit near the
    # interview-reported trip length (~3.2 h). Without these three, this file could not be
    # used to audit the unit the model actually ran on.
    write.csv(ie_validation |>
      mutate(turnover       = if_else(max_present > 0, ie_trips / max_present, NA_real_),
             hours_per_trip = if_else(ie_trips > 0, ie_crabber_hours / ie_trips, NA_real_)) |>
      select(event_date, day_type, ie_crabber_hours, ie_trips, max_present, mean_present,
             L_effective, turnover, hours_per_trip,
             mean_gear, n_counts, gear_est_crabber_hrs, f_temporal, pct_error),
      file.path(output_dir, "ie_analysis.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }
} else {
  bss_warn("I/E", "No I/E data in the workbook: the shore turnover falls back to its prior centre and no I/E observation enters any fit.", severity = "note")
}

### 3.2 Shore I/E representativeness (diagnostic)

The shore turnover above is derived from the I/E survey days, so it is only as representative as those days are. This check compares the shore daily gear counts on I/E days against every other sampled day: a mean percentile rank near 0.5 and a non-significant rank test mean the I/E days look like the rest of the season; a rank far from 0.5 means the turnover was measured on unusually busy (or quiet) days, and the shore scale should be read with that in mind (CHANGE_REGISTER D24). The fitted `sigma_IE` (Section 12) is the in-model counterpart: it grows when the I/E arrivals and the counts disagree.

```{r ie-representativeness, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
ie_rep <- tryCatch(diagnose_ie_representativeness(dwg, ie_data, params),
                   error = function(e) { bss_warn("I/E", paste("I/E representativeness diagnostic not computed:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })
if (!is.null(ie_rep)) {
  write.csv(ie_rep$table, file.path(output_dir, "ie_representativeness.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("**Shore I/E days: %d.** %s\n\n", ie_rep$n_ie, ie_rep$verdict))
  print(report_table(ie_rep$table |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~round(., 2))) |>
                       dplyr::rename(dplyr::any_of(c(`Days` = "group", `Sampled days` = "n", `Mean gear count` = "mean_gear",
                                                     `Median gear count` = "median_gear"))),
    paste("Shore daily gear counts on I/E observation days against every other sampled day. A mean",
          "percentile rank near 0.5 with a non-significant rank test means the I/E days, and so the",
          "turnover derived from them, are representative of the season's effort.")))
} else {
  cat("_Shore I/E representativeness diagnostic unavailable (no shore I/E data)._")
}
```

### 3.3 Other-fishery openers

Whether other coastal fishery openers (Marine Area 2 finfish, razor-clam digs) enter the EFFORT model as covariates this run. The spillover diagnostic behind the screen, a day-type and month adjusted comparison of crab effort and catch rate on opener days, is in [Appendix B](#appendix-b-other-fishery-opener-spillover); it changes no estimate. `opener_covariate_mode` selects `"off"` (no covariates), `"manual"` or `"auto"` (a candidate enters only if its adjusted effect clears `opener_auto_p` after a Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the effort tests). **A screen is not a verdict**: a term selected on a p-value from the data it is then fitted to has an inflated coefficient, and the arbiter is the effort streams' held-out predictive fit. A boat opener term should be paired with `crab_fraction_strata = "month_opener"`, not with `"opener"`: a crabbing fraction that cannot see opener days converts the opener surge in all-boat counts into crab effort, and plain `"opener"` anchors EVERY stratum to the level prior and silently discards the walk.

```{r fishery-spillover, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# ---- 3.5 OTHER-FISHERY OPENER SPILLOVER (diagnostic; changes no estimate) ----
spillover <- NULL; sp_raw_disp <- NULL; sp_adj_disp <- NULL; p_spill_eff <- NULL; p_spill_cpue <- NULL
if (isTRUE(params$run_fishery_spillover_diag)) {
  timer_start("2b_fishery_spillover")
  spillover <- tryCatch(
    diagnose_fishery_spillover(dwg, params),
    error = function(e) { bss_warn("openers", sprintf("Fishery-opener spillover diagnostic skipped: %s", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })
  if (!is.null(spillover)) {
    write.csv(spillover$raw,      file.path(output_dir, "fishery_spillover_raw.csv"),      row.names = FALSE)
    write.csv(spillover$adjusted, file.path(output_dir, "fishery_spillover_adjusted.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    for (nt in spillover$notes) bss_warn("openers", paste("Spillover diagnostic:", nt), severity = "note")

    sp_raw_disp <- spillover$raw |>
      dplyr::transmute(Series, Opener,
        `n (opener)` = n_opener, `Mean (opener)` = round(mean_opener, 2),
        `n (other)`  = n_other,  `Mean (other)`  = round(mean_other, 2),
        `Raw diff`   = round(raw_diff, 2), `Raw %` = round(raw_pct, 0),
        `t-test p`   = fmt_p(t_p))
    sp_adj_disp <- spillover$adjusted |>
      dplyr::transmute(Series, Opener,
        `Adj. estimate` = round(adj_estimate, 2), SE = round(se, 2),
        `95% CI` = ifelse(is.na(ci_lo), "-", sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", ci_lo, ci_hi)),
        p = fmt_p(adj_p), Note = note)

    mk_long <- function(df) df |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(spillover$flag_cols), names_to = "opener", values_to = "is_open") |>
      dplyr::mutate(Opener = unname(spillover$flag_labels[opener]),
                    Status = ifelse(is_open, "Opener", "Other"))
    p_spill_eff <- ggplot(mk_long(spillover$effort_long), aes(Status, value, fill = Status)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.85) +
      facet_grid(series ~ Opener, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(Opener = "#c0392b", Other = "grey70")) +
      labs(title = "Crab effort: other-fishery opener days vs other days", x = NULL, y = "Daily effort count") +
      theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
    p_spill_cpue <- ggplot(mk_long(spillover$cpue_long), aes(Status, value, fill = Status)) +
      geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.85) +
      facet_grid(series ~ Opener, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(Opener = "#c0392b", Other = "grey70")) +
      labs(title = "Interview CPUE: other-fishery opener days vs other days", x = NULL, y = "Dungeness per gear deployment") +
      theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
  }
  timer_stop("2b_fishery_spillover")
}
```

```{r opener-covariate-decision, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# --- improvement 4: opener effort covariates ---------------------------------------
# Per-date opener flags for every candidate, used both by the screen and to build each
# fit's X_open matrix. Guarded: a missing calendar disables the feature, never the run.
params$opener_flags <- tryCatch(opener_flag_series(params),
                                error = function(e) { bss_warn("openers", paste("Opener calendar unavailable; no opener covariate can enter:",
                                                          conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })

# Compatibility switch: razor_dig_mode still works and is implemented as one column of
# the opener machinery, so a razor-only run reproduces the retired B3 term exactly.
# It keeps its historical RAW (unadjusted) p-value rule on purpose, so a run pinned to
# the old behaviour is not silently re-decided by the new multiplicity adjustment.
params$razor_dig_dates <- tryCatch({
  ev <- prep_fishery_events(params)
  ev$razor |> dplyr::filter(razor_nearby_dig) |> dplyr::pull(event_date)
}, error = function(e) as.Date(character(0)))

razor_mode   <- tolower(params$razor_dig_mode %||% "no")
razor_thresh <- params$razor_dig_auto_p %||% 0.05
razor_auto_p <- NA_real_
if (razor_mode == "auto" && !is.null(spillover)) {
  ap <- spillover$adjusted |>
    dplyr::filter(Series == "Shore gear (effort)", grepl("Razor", Opener))
  if (nrow(ap) > 0) razor_auto_p <- ap$adj_p[1]
}
params$razor_dig_active <- switch(razor_mode,
  yes  = TRUE,
  no   = FALSE,
  auto = is.finite(razor_auto_p) && razor_auto_p < razor_thresh,
  FALSE)
if (razor_mode == "auto" && is.null(spillover))
  bss_warn("openers", "razor_dig_mode = 'auto' but the spillover diagnostic is off (run_fishery_spillover_diag = FALSE); the razor term stays OFF.", severity = "note")

# The generalized screen.
opener_sel <- tryCatch(opener_select(spillover, params),
                       error = function(e) { bss_warn("openers", paste("Opener screen failed; no opener covariate enters:", conditionMessage(e)))
                                             list(shore = character(0), private_boat = character(0),
                                                  table = NULL, mode = "off", note = "screen failed") })
params$opener_selected <- list(shore = opener_sel$shore, private_boat = opener_sel$private_boat)

cat(sprintf("Opener effort covariates: mode=%s\n  shore: %s\n  private boat: %s\n",
            opener_sel$mode,
            if (length(opener_sel$shore)) paste(opener_sel$shore, collapse = ", ") else "(none)",
            if (length(opener_sel$private_boat)) paste(opener_sel$private_boat, collapse = ", ") else "(none)"))
if (length(opener_sel$note)) cat("  ", opener_sel$note, "\n", sep = "")
cat(sprintf("Razor-dig compatibility switch: mode=%s, active=%s%s\n",
    razor_mode, params$razor_dig_active,
    if (razor_mode == "auto")
      sprintf(" (RAW adjusted shore-effort p=%s, threshold=%.3f)",
              ifelse(is.finite(razor_auto_p), sprintf('%.3f', razor_auto_p), 'NA'), razor_thresh)
    else ""))

# --- the f interaction warning (improvement 4 x improvement 8) ---------------------
if (length(opener_sel$private_boat) > 0 &&
    !identical(params$crab_fraction_strata %||% "none", "opener") &&
    !identical(params$crab_fraction_strata %||% "none", "month_opener") &&
    isTRUE(params$use_crab_fraction)) {
  bss_warn("openers", paste0("A BOAT opener covariate is active while crab_fraction_strata = '", params$crab_fraction_strata %||% "none",
                             "': a crabbing fraction that cannot see opener days converts the opener surge in all-boat counts into crab effort. Use 'month_opener'."))
  cat(paste0("\n  *** WARNING: a BOAT opener covariate is active while crab_fraction_strata = '",
             params$crab_fraction_strata %||% "none", "'.\n",
             "      The covariate makes latent boat effort track the opener-day surge in ALL-boat\n",
             "      counts more faithfully, and a constant f then converts that surge to crab effort\n",
             "      at the same rate as a closed-fishery day. Those are exactly the boats we know are\n",
             "      NOT crabbing, so this combination can INCREASE the boat bias on opener days.\n",
             "      Set crab_fraction_strata = 'opener' or 'month_opener' (params$opener_f_flag picks\n",
             "      which opener defines the stratum). ***\n\n"))
}

# Days on which the f-defining opener was open, for crab_fraction_strata = opener /
# month_opener. Harmless when those strata are not in use.
params$opener_f_dates <- tryCatch({
  fl <- params$opener_flags; ff <- params$opener_f_flag %||% "ma2_halibut_open"
  if (!is.null(fl) && ff %in% names(fl)) fl$event_date[as.logical(fl[[ff]])] else as.Date(character(0))
}, error = function(e) as.Date(character(0)))
```

### 3.4 The marine hazard effort covariate (the method of record since 2026-09-27)

**The method of record** (CHANGE_REGISTER A30, adopted 2026-09-27): whether an NWS **Small Craft Advisory or higher** was in effect for the Grays Harbor Bar or the coastal waters off Westport at any moment of the local 04:00 to 16:00 window enters the **private-boat all-gear** effort process as one season-constant term (`marine_hazard_mode = "manual"`, `marine_hazard_manual_boat = "nws_sca_any"`, `marine_hazard_gear_regimes = "all_gear"`). No shore term, not the samplers' bar-restriction tick, and not the pot-closure fit, which stays covariate-free. The flag is known on every day of the window from the archived NWS products in `04_input_files/nws_marine_hazards.xlsx`, which is what a covariate on a daily latent process needs. The other modes remain for experiments: `"off"` (nothing is read), `"auto"` (a candidate enters only if its day-type and month adjusted effect clears `marine_hazard_auto_p` after a multiplicity adjustment), `"on"` (every candidate). The term rides on the effort-covariate block as a column, and its fitted coefficient is in [Section 12.4](#effort-day-covariates-as-fitted); the table below is the pre-fit screen on the sampled days.

**What to hold when reading the boat term.** A boat term describes ALL private boats: if crabbing boats respond to an advisory differently from finfish boats, the crabbing fraction `f` differs on those days and the monthly `f` cannot see it (D30). The term is one coefficient for the season, and the four-season trailer record says the winter effect is about half the summer's, so the winter months are probably over-corrected while the season total is insensitive to that shape (D32). The evidence behind the adoption, and these caveats, are in `VALIDATION_CAMPAIGN.md` Sections 1x to 1z. If an experiment enters the bar-restriction tick, note that it is observed on sampled days only and **imputed** on the rest (an expected value from a logistic regression on the archived advisories, `bar_restriction_impute`), so its unsampled-day contribution rests on the NWS flags, not on an observation.

```{r marine-hazard-decision, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# --- 2026-09-25: marine hazard effort covariates (03_R_functions/bss_marine_hazard_covariates.R)
# The method of record since 2026-09-27 is "manual" with nws_sca_any on the boat (A30); the
# selection is per population here, and the preps confine it to the sub-seasons named in
# marine_hazard_gear_regimes ("all_gear"). With marine_hazard_mode = "off" this reads nothing
# and only installs an empty selection. Any other mode STOPS on a missing or non-covering
# archive rather than running without the covariate the config names, so a fit can never
# silently lack a term it should carry.
marine_hazard <- marine_hazard_prepare(dwg, params, output_dir = output_dir)
params <- marine_hazard$params
```

      Covariate     = label,
      `Rate ratio`  = round(rate_ratio, 3),
      `Rate ratio (per count)` = if ("rate_ratio_per_count" %in% names(marine_hazard$sel$table)) round(rate_ratio_per_count, 3) else NA_real_,
      `p (raw)`     = fmt_p(p_raw),
      `p (adjusted)` = if ("p_adj" %in% names(marine_hazard$sel$table)) fmt_p(p_adj) else "-",
      Selected      = selected,
      Reason        = reason),
    caption = paste("Marine hazard effort-covariate screen. 'Rate ratio' is exp(coefficient) from",
                    "glm(daily count ~ day-type + month + covariate, quasipoisson) on the window's sampled",
                    "days (bar restriction: observed days only); 'Rate ratio (per count)' is the same GLM",

              params$marine_hazard_mode %||% "off"))
}

## 4. Point Estimator (PE)

The design-based estimator: it averages the sampled days within each week by day-type stratum and expands to the unsampled days. The PE is fast and transparent, it is the independent check on the Bayesian estimate ([Section 13](#pe-vs-bss-comparison)), and it is what a component reports if its Bayesian fit fails the convergence gate.

**Many of a component's days rest on one sampled day or none.** With weekly strata and partial day coverage, a (week x day-type) cell often has one sampled day and sometimes none; the table below gives this run's share for each component (also in `pe_empty_effort_strata.csv`). Three settings decide what happens to those cells, all documented in `run_config.R` and implemented once in `03_R_functions/pe_effort_strata.R`:

- an unsampled cell's **effort** is imputed from the same day type in the same month (`pe_empty_effort_stratum = "local_day_type"`). Until 2026-09-12 it contributed nothing, which removed effort disproportionately from weekend and holiday days. `"zero"` restores that, and `pe_empty_effort_strata.csv` reports `zeroed_effort_bias`, the effort those cells would have carried, so that choice states its own cost.
- an unsampled cell's **CPUE** is that month's ratio of sums (`pe_empty_stratum = "local"`), matching the scale of the effort fill. Whether that is the right fill is an open question (CHANGE_REGISTER D19).
- an unsampled or singleton cell's **variance** (`pe_variance = "impute_aware"`): a singleton cell borrows its donor's spread (the collapsed-stratum estimator), an imputed cell carries the donor mean's sampling variance plus a between-cell surrogate, and the component SE carries the covariances between cells that share a donor (B44). `effort_se_sampled_only` in the CSV keeps the sampled-cells-only arithmetic.

The point estimate is unaffected by the third setting. **This is not PE-only bookkeeping**: a component whose gate fails reports its PE point in the port total as a constant, so these settings reach the headline whenever a component falls back.

```{r pe-estimates, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.2 PE ESTIMATES ----
timer_start("3_PE_estimates")
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n PE ESTIMATES\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

pe_all <- list()
for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
  for(ss in subseasons) {
    label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
    days_ss <- prep_days_crab(ss$start, ss$end, params, L_eff_model = L_eff_model)
    summ_ss <- prep_population_summary(dwg, pop, ss$start, ss$end, params)
    pe_all[[label]] <- run_pe_pooled(summ_ss, days_ss, params, label)
  }
}
# 2026-08-27: the empty-effort-stratum audit as a FILE, not a console line. This chunk is
# results='hide', so the per-component report run_pe_pooled() cat()s never reached a reader
# on this track. See write_pe_empty_stratum_report() in 03_R_functions/save_run_diagnostics.R.
pe_empty_report <- write_pe_empty_stratum_report(pe_all, output_dir, params)
timer_stop("3_PE_estimates")


```

```{r pe-thin-cells-show, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# 2026-09-28 (B46): THIS run's thin cells and PE totals, replacing 2024-25 figures that were
# written into the section text.
.pe_comp <- pe_all[!names(pe_all) %in% "comm_charter"]
.tc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.pe_comp), function(k) { x <- .pe_comp[[k]]
  data.frame(Component = k, Cells = x$n_effort_strata_total %||% NA, Unsampled = x$n_empty_effort_strata %||% NA,
             `One sampled day` = x$n_single_effort_strata %||% NA,
             `Share of calendar days` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * ((x$n_empty_effort_days %||% 0) + (x$n_single_effort_days %||% 0)) / max(x$n_calendar_days %||% 1, 1)),
             `Effort SE` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(round(x$effort_se %||% NA), big.mark = ","), 100 * (x$effort_se %||% NA) / max(x$effort_total %||% 1, 1)),
             `PE catch` = round(x$Dungeness_Kept %||% NA), check.names = FALSE) }))
if (!is.null(.tc) && nrow(.tc)) { .tc$Component <- short_fit(.tc$Component)
  print(report_table(.tc, digits = 0, caption = "This run's (week x day-type) cells: unsampled, resting on one sampled day, the share of calendar days they cover, the effort SE and the PE catch.")) }
```

### 4.1 Incomplete-trip treatment diagnostic (improvement 5)

An incomplete trip is one where the crabber had not finished when we spoke to them. All their gear is in the catch-rate denominator but only part of their catch is in the numerator, so their measured rate reads low. Production drops them; the table below gives this run's incomplete share by component, which is what the filter costs in sample size.

**The structural fact that bounds what any treatment can do.** Effort in this pipeline does not come from interviews. It comes from the dock gear counts and the trailer/OSP boat counts. Interviews supply only the catch **rate** and the gear **ratios** (`R_G`, gear per crabber; `R_G_boat` / the PE's gear-per-group). So no treatment of incomplete trips can add effort to the expansion; each arm below moves the estimate through the catch rate or through the gear ratios, and nothing else.

Four arms are run against the fast design-based PE. **This section changes no reported number**; the production estimator remains `exclude`.

- **exclude**, production today: drop them from both the catch rate and the gear ratios.
- **gear_only**, drop their catch, keep their gear counts in the gear ratios. An interrupted trip's gear count is fully observed; only its catch is truncated. The pipeline does not do this: the PE and the BSS both build their gear ratios from the filtered frame (`pe_gear_ratio_arm = "match_bss"`, aligned 2026-09-02).
- **impute_mean_cpue**, keep them with catch replaced by (complete-trip catch rate × their gear count). Expect close to no movement, and that is arithmetic rather than luck: a ratio-of-sums over complete-plus-imputed returns the complete-trip rate identically. Any movement is thin-stratum shrinkage toward the pooled rate.
- **keep**, no filter (pre-v7.5 behaviour).

Read `gear_ratio` and `gear_lengthbias_p` before acting on `gear_only`: intercepted trips over-represent long trips by construction, and if long trips also deploy more gear then folding them into `R_G` would bias the effort expansion up.

Not implemented here, and the statistically correct answer: a **censored likelihood**, in which an incomplete trip's observed catch is treated as a lower bound (`neg_binomial_2_lccdf`) rather than an observation. That recovers the whole sample without the bias, but it is a Stan change with a validation burden and cannot be evaluated by a design-based arm. See `PIPELINE_STATUS.md` Tier 2.

```{r pe-sensitivity, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.2b POOL-2 / improvement 5: INCOMPLETE-TRIP TREATMENT DIAGNOSTIC ----
# Four arms through the fast design-based PE (no MCMC). DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: it changes no
# reported total and is tryCatch-wrapped so it can never break the run. The arm logic and
# the reasoning behind each arm live in 03_R_functions/diagnose_incomplete_trips.R.
# Output: sensitivity_incomplete_trips.csv.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n INCOMPLETE-TRIP TREATMENT DIAGNOSTIC (improvement 5)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
sens_df <- NULL   # persists to the display chunk below even if the tryCatch errors
if (isTRUE(params$diagnose_incomplete_trips %||% TRUE)) {
  tryCatch({
    sens_df <- diagnose_incomplete_trips(dwg, subseasons, params, L_eff_model,
                                         pe_fun = run_pe_pooled)
    if (!is.null(sens_df))
      write.csv(sens_df, file.path(output_dir, "sensitivity_incomplete_trips.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) bss_warn("PE", sprintf("Incomplete-trip diagnostic skipped: %s", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"))
}


```

  # 2026-09-29: print() -- the table was the non-final value of this block and never rendered.
  print(report_table(
    dplyr::transmute(sens_df,
      Component         = component_disp,
      Arm               = arm,
      `Interviews used` = n_cpue_used,

      `Gear ratio`      = gear_ratio,
      `Gear vs exclude (%)` = gear_vs_exclude_pct,

    caption = paste("Incomplete-trip treatment arms (improvement 5), design-based PE. Production is",
                    "'exclude' and is the reference row for the two '% vs exclude' columns. 'Gear ratio'",
                    "is gear per crabber (shore) or gear per boat group (boat); for shore on",
                    "gear-deployments it affects only the BSS, not the PE, so a flat shore PE across",

  .lb <- dplyr::distinct(dplyr::select(sens_df, component_disp, gear_lengthbias_p))
  cat("\n\n**Length-bias check on the gear counts** (Welch t-test, incomplete vs complete trips; a small p with a HIGHER incomplete-trip gear count is what would disqualify the `gear_only` arm): ",
      paste(sprintf("%s p = %s", .lb$component_disp,
                    ifelse(is.na(.lb$gear_lengthbias_p), "n/a", format(.lb$gear_lengthbias_p))),
            collapse = "; "), "\n\n")
} else {
  cat("_Incomplete-trip diagnostic produced no output this run._")
}

### 4.2 Commercial and charter census

The commercial and charter harvest is not modelled: it is **two estimators**. The **commercial** vessels fishing recreationally are a **census**: the daily tally counts them and the samplers are scheduled on the days those vessels operate, so a window day without a tally is a day with no commercial operation (`census_expansion = "none"`). The component is the exact sum over the tally days of vessels times the mean catch per interviewed vessel; the count is exact, and the per-vessel mean is a near-census sample mean that enters the port interval only under `census_uncertainty = "sampling"` (CHANGE_REGISTER D16). The **charter** vessels are not fully sampled, so their component is an **expansion** over the operators' trip roster (`charter_trips.xlsx`, unioned per day with the tally's charter column), stratified by vessel, with the finite-population-corrected variance `N^2 (1 - n/N) s^2 / n`; that SE is what `census_uncertainty = "charter"` carries into the port interval. The census runs over the part of the census window inside the estimation window (B52). The frame conditions below say how the number should be read; none of them stops the run.

```{r pe-comm, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.4 COMMERCIAL/CHARTER ----
timer_start("4_commercial_charter")
pe_all$comm_charter <- estimate_comm_charter(dwg, params)
# 2026-09-29: the frame conditions go to the run-warnings log as well as census_frame_warnings.csv
# (written in the port-total chunk); a missing frame or a census outside the window is a warning.
for (.w in pe_all$comm_charter$frame_warnings %||% character(0))
  bss_warn("census", .w, severity = if (grepl("^(NO CENSUS FRAME|CENSUS OUTSIDE)", .w)) "warning" else "note")
# census_daily.csv flags every calendar day observed / no operation; census_variance.csv
# carries the per-stratum imputation variance behind Dungeness_Kept_se. Whether that SE
# reaches the port interval is params$census_uncertainty ("charter" SHIPS | "none" |
# "sampling"; "imputed_days" survives only as the 2026-09-08 alias for "sampling").
if (!is.null(pe_all$comm_charter$daily_full))
  write.csv(pe_all$comm_charter$daily_full, file.path(output_dir, "census_daily.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
if (!is.null(pe_all$comm_charter$variance_detail))
  write.csv(pe_all$comm_charter$variance_detail, file.path(output_dir, "census_variance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
timer_stop("4_commercial_charter")


```

### 4.3 PE port totals

The Point Estimator port total, summed across the three population components. Compare it against the Bayesian total below.

```{r pe-port, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.5 PE PORT TOTALS ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n PE PORT TOTALS\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

# component_keys / component_names now follow the sub-season set (build_subseasons):
# one row per population x sub-season, then comm_charter, then a PORT TOTAL computed from
# the semantic sums (pe_port_total), not by a fixed row index. component_keys is still
# consumed by the PE-consistency check chunk below (comm_charter has no check, skipped there).
pe_pops    <- c("shore", "private_boat")
pop_disp   <- c(shore = "Shore", private_boat = "Private Boat")
ss_names   <- vapply(subseasons, function(ss) ss$name,         character(1))
ss_disp    <- vapply(subseasons, function(ss) ss$display_name, character(1))
component_keys  <- c(unlist(lapply(pe_pops, function(p) paste0(p, "_", ss_names))), "comm_charter")

                     "Commercial/Charter")

  Component  = c(component_names, "PORT TOTAL"),
  # 2026-09-29: named for its unit. It was Effort_hrs; the fitted components are in gear

  Effort = c(vapply(component_keys, function(k) pe_field(k, "effort_total"),  numeric(1)), pe_port_total("effort_total")),
  Dungeness  = c(vapply(component_keys, function(k) pe_field(k, "Dungeness_Kept"), numeric(1)), pe_port_total("Dungeness_Kept"))
)

print(pe_summary |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.))))
