### 4.4 PE internal consistency (ratio-of-sums)

Each component's PE stratum CPUE is a ratio-of-sums (`sum(catch)/sum(hrs)` within each week-by-day-type stratum), not a mean of per-day ratios (backlog P0). The mean-of-ratios was unstable in thin strata, a day with very little sampled effort produced an extreme daily ratio that was then multiplied by the full stratum effort, and it made the shore PE's implied CPUE about 2.9x its own interview ratio-of-sums. Ratio-of-sums removes that and matches the gear-resolved track. The check below is the guardrail: the PE's implied CPUE (its catch divided by its effort) should sit near the ratio of sums over the same interviews. Outside 0.5 to 2 the likeliest cause is a unit mismatch, though a steep within-season CPUE gradient can put a legitimate component there; such a component is flagged here and raises a warning (Section 16), and the run continues.

```{r pe-consistency-show, echo=FALSE}
# P0: render the PE internal-consistency check returned by run_pe_pooled per component
# (component_keys is defined in the pe-port chunk above). comm_charter is a census, not
# run_pe_pooled, so it has no check and is skipped.
pe_chk <- tryCatch(
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(component_keys, function(k) {
    d <- pe_all[[k]]$pe_cpue_check
    if (is.null(d)) NULL else dplyr::mutate(d, Component = k)
  })),
  error = function(e) { bss_warn("PE", paste("PE consistency table not assembled:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })
if (!is.null(pe_chk) && nrow(pe_chk) > 0) {
  report_table(
    dplyr::transmute(pe_chk,
      Component         = short_fit(Component),
      Unit              = effort_unit,
      `PE implied CPUE` = round(pe_implied_cpue, 3),
      `Interview RoS`   = round(interview_ros, 3),
      Ratio             = round(ratio, 2),
      `Within 0.5-2`    = if ("within_0.5_to_2" %in% names(pe_chk)) within_0.5_to_2 else NA),
    caption = paste("PE internal-consistency check (P0). 'PE implied CPUE' is the",
                    "component's PE catch / PE effort; 'Interview RoS' is the ratio-of-sums",
                    "over the same interviews. Healthy: Ratio near 1; outside 0.5 to 2 is flagged and",
                    "warned, not stopped (B46)."))
} else {
  cat("_PE consistency check unavailable (no fitted components produced it)._")
}
```

## 5. Bayesian state-space model fits

Each population by sub-season is fitted independently with a Bayesian state-space (BSS) model: daily effort and catch rate are latent series that evolve as AR(1) processes at the resolution in the table below, observed through the gear or trailer counts, the OSP boat totals, the I/E arrivals and the interviews, and the model fills the unsampled days with full credible intervals. The table records how each fit was run. Whether each fit converged, and so whether its component reports the Bayesian estimate, is [Section 6](#convergence-gate-and-model-selection).

```{r bss-fits, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# ---- 7.6 BSS MODEL RUNS ----
timer_start("5_BSS_model_runs")
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n BSS MODEL RUNS (Adaptive AR)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

bss_catch_groups <- catch_groups
bss_all <- list()
ar_resolutions <- list()  # track AR resolution per fit (the FINAL attempt's, when escalating)
ar_escalation_log <- list()  # improvement 7: one row per fit attempt (see ar_escalation_log.csv)
fit_settings_log <- list()   # 2026-09-29: how each fit was run, for the report's Section 5 table
.kept_attempt <- list()      # fit label -> the attempt index whose stanfit was retained

for(cg in bss_catch_groups) {
  for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
    for(ss in subseasons) {
      label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_", cg)
      cat(sprintf("\n--- BSS: %s ---\n", label))

      days_ss <- prep_days_crab(ss$start, ss$end, params, L_eff_model = L_eff_model)
      summ_ss <- prep_population_summary(dwg, pop, ss$start, ss$end, params)

      # NOTE (POOL-2): n_int is the UNFILTERED interview count. The fitted CPUE
      # count is lower once prep_bss_crab drops h<=0 rows and (with
      # filter_incomplete_trips = TRUE) incomplete trips, so this sufficiency
      # guard reads looser than the count the fit actually uses. Behavior is
      # unchanged from prior versions (the guard was always pre-filter); on the
      # 2024-25 data every fitted component keeps well over bss_min_interviews
      # complete interviews. If a future component is marginal, gate on the
      # complete-only count instead.
      n_int <- nrow(summ_ss$interview)
      n_eff <- nrow(summ_ss$effort_index)

      if(n_eff < 5 || n_int < params$bss_min_interviews) {
        cat(sprintf("  Insufficient data (%d effort, %d interviews), PE fallback.\n", n_eff, n_int))
        bss_warn("fit", sprintf("%s: insufficient data (%d effort counts, %d interviews; floor %d); the component reports its PE.",
                                label, n_eff, n_int, params$bss_min_interviews))
        bss_all[[label]] <- list(C_sum=NA, E_sum=NA, pe_fallback=TRUE,
                                 population=pop, subseason=ss$name, catch_group=cg)
        next
      }

      # ================================================================================
      # improvement 7: AR RESOLUTION ESCALATION LADDER
      # --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      # ar_escalate = FALSE (default) -> exactly one attempt at the resolution the
      # coverage rule picks, capped by ar_max_resolution. Identical to previous runs.
      #
      # ar_escalate = TRUE -> start at the FINEST rung (daily, ignoring the caps) and
      # refit one rung coarser each time the fit fails the SAME convergence gate that
      # decides PE-vs-BSS, stopping at the first rung that passes. Each rung is a real
      # multi-hour fit, so this is a deliberate runtime-for-guarantee trade; see
      # run_config.R. Every attempt is logged to ar_escalation_log.csv.
      #
      # The gate is computed here per attempt, on a minimal list(fit, pe_fallback), which
      # is exactly what bss_compute_gate() reads. The authoritative gate pass in Section 6
      # still recomputes it on the final fit, so the two cannot disagree.
      # ================================================================================
      eff_d_ladder <- summ_ss$effort_index |>
        filter(count_sequence <= params$bss_max_count_seq) |>
        left_join(days_ss |> select(event_date, day_index), by = "event_date") |>
        filter(!is.na(day_index))
      ar_ladder <- bss_ar_ladder(days_ss, eff_d_ladder, pop, params,
                                 fixed_resolution = NULL, gear_regime = ss$gear_regime)
      # Incumbent trackers for the rung-selection rule below. Reset per component.
      .incumbent_passed <- FALSE; .incumbent_pi_rel <- Inf
      # 2026-09-04: ar_escalate is resolved PER FIT, because it now accepts a per-population
      # or per-sub-season scope as well as a scalar (03_R_functions/bss_ar_resolution.R).
      # Every rung is a multi-hour fit, so escalating a component whose cap is already
      # settled burns known-bad fits to rediscover it.
      .esc_on <- .bss_resolve_ar_escalate(params, pop, ss$gear_regime)
      if (.esc_on)
        cat(sprintf("  AR escalation ladder [%s/%s]: %s\n", pop, ss$gear_regime,
                    paste(ar_ladder, collapse = " -> ")))

      # improvement 6: the POST-FILTER interview floor. The guard above counts UNFILTERED
      # interviews and therefore reads looser than the count the CPUE likelihood sees;
      # that was harmless at a floor of 20 with hundreds to spare and is not harmless at
      # 15 with the boat pot-closure's 17. NULL reuses bss_min_interviews.
      min_fitted <- params$bss_min_interviews_fitted %||% params$bss_min_interviews

      is_shore   <- (pop == "shore")
      is_boat    <- (pop == "private_boat")
      is_allgear <- (ss$gear_regime == "all_gear")
      is_ringnet <- (ss$gear_regime == "pot_closure")

      fit <- NULL; bss_data <- NULL; too_thin <- FALSE

      for (attempt in seq_along(ar_ladder)) {

        # force_resolution only when escalating: with the ladder off we must go through
        # the historical data-driven + cap path so the run is bit-comparable to Run 6.
        #
        # 2026-09-04 DEFECT FIX. This line read `isTRUE(params$ar_escalate)`. When
        # ar_escalate became scoped (`list(shore = "all_gear")`, or a character vector of
        # populations) on the same day, `isTRUE()` on a list is FALSE, so force_res stayed
        # NULL while `.esc_on` above correctly resolved TRUE. The ladder was therefore BUILT
        # with four rungs and the loop ran four attempts, but every attempt re-derived the
        # SAME resolution from the data-driven selector. The 2026-09-03 A1 stage fitted
        # shore all-gear at `daily` four consecutive times, 333 divergences and
        # catch_median 20,897.819 on every rung, and burned 14.7 h of a 23.6 h batch to
        # learn nothing. Resolve it the same way `.esc_on` does, from the one helper.
        force_res <- if (.esc_on) ar_ladder[attempt] else NULL
        bss_data_try <- prep_bss_crab_pooled(days_ss, summ_ss, cg, params, pop,
                                             gear_regime = ss$gear_regime, ie_data = ie_data,
                                             force_resolution = force_res)

        n_fitted <- attr(bss_data_try, "n_interviews_fitted") %||% bss_data_try$IntC
        if (n_fitted < min_fitted) {
          cat(sprintf(paste0("  Post-filter interviews %d < bss_min_interviews_fitted = %d ",
                             "(pre-filter count was %d); PE fallback.\n"),
                      n_fitted, min_fitted, n_int))
          bss_warn("fit", sprintf("%s: %d interviews after the filters, below bss_min_interviews_fitted = %d; the component reports its PE.",
                                  label, n_fitted, min_fitted))
          bss_all[[label]] <- list(C_sum=NA, E_sum=NA, pe_fallback=TRUE,
                                   population=pop, subseason=ss$name, catch_group=cg)
          too_thin <- TRUE
          break
        }

        # v6.1/v6.2: per-fit sampler tuning. Each branch sets iter, warmup,
        # max_treedepth, and adapt_delta; any fit without a specific override
        # uses the *_default values. Ported from the gear-resolved track (v6.1)
        # and extended with a boat all-gear branch (v6.2). The boat all-gear fit
        # produced 5998 divergences with treedepth_pct = 0 in the 2026-04-08 run,
        # so step size (adapt_delta), not trajectory length, was the binding
        # constraint: adapt_delta is raised to 0.99 and max_treedepth to 13 (the
        # smaller steps from a higher adapt_delta lengthen trajectories, so the
        # deeper tree is a buffer against new treedepth saturation).
        if(is_shore && is_allgear) {
          fit_iter    <- params$bss_iter_shore_allgear
          fit_warmup  <- params$bss_warmup_shore_allgear
          fit_treedep <- params$bss_treedepth_shore_allgear %||% params$bss_max_treedepth_default
          fit_delta   <- params$bss_delta_shore_allgear     %||% params$bss_adapt_delta
        } else if(is_boat && is_allgear) {
          fit_iter    <- params$bss_iter_boat_allgear      %||% params$bss_iter_default
          fit_warmup  <- params$bss_warmup_boat_allgear    %||% params$bss_warmup_default
          fit_treedep <- params$bss_treedepth_boat_allgear %||% params$bss_max_treedepth_default
          fit_delta   <- params$bss_delta_boat_allgear     %||% params$bss_adapt_delta
        } else if(is_ringnet) {
          fit_iter    <- params$bss_iter_default
          fit_warmup  <- params$bss_warmup_default
          fit_treedep <- params$bss_treedepth_ringnet %||% params$bss_max_treedepth_default
          fit_delta   <- params$bss_delta_ringnet     %||% params$bss_adapt_delta
        } else {
          fit_iter    <- params$bss_iter_default
          fit_warmup  <- params$bss_warmup_default
          fit_treedep <- params$bss_max_treedepth_default
          fit_delta   <- params$bss_adapt_delta
        }

        cat(sprintf("  Stan [attempt %d/%d]: iter=%d, warmup=%d, max_treedepth=%d, adapt_delta=%.2f, init_r=%.2f, D=%d days, P_n=%d (%s), %d interviews\n",
                    attempt, length(ar_ladder), fit_iter, fit_warmup, fit_treedep, fit_delta, params$bss_init_r %||% 2,
                    bss_data_try$D, bss_data_try$P_n,
                    attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution"), bss_data_try$IntC))

        fit_settings_log[[length(fit_settings_log) + 1]] <- tibble(
          fit = label, attempt = attempt, ar_resolution = attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution") %||% NA_character_,
          P_n = bss_data_try$P_n, days = bss_data_try$D, interviews = bss_data_try$IntC,
          effort_obs = bss_data_try$n_effort_obs %||% NA_integer_, ie_obs = bss_data_try$IE_n %||% 0L,
          iter = fit_iter, warmup = fit_warmup, max_treedepth = fit_treedep, adapt_delta = fit_delta,
          init_r = as.numeric(params$bss_init_r %||% 2), level_collapse = as.character(params$mu_hier_collapse_single %||% "both"))
        timer_start(paste0("BSS_", label, "_att", attempt))
        # 2026-08-26: guarded wrapper, 03_R_functions/bss_stan_fit.R. On the happy path
        # this is rstan::stan() with the same arguments, same seed, same RNG stream, so
        # fits are unchanged. It adds two pre/post checks that would have turned the
        # 2026-08-25 "dim(X) must have a positive length" failure into a one-line error
        # naming the missing Stan data variable: a data-completeness check before the
        # sampler, and an empty-stanfit check after it. log_file keeps the Stan console
        # for this fit in output_dir, so a chain failure stays diagnosable even though
        # this chunk is results='hide'.
        fit_try <- bss_stan_fit(
          file = here("02_stan_models", params$bss_model_file),
          data = bss_data_try,
          label = sprintf("%s att%d", label, attempt),
          log_file = file.path(output_dir,
                               sprintf("stan_console_%s_att%d.log", label, attempt)),
          chains = params$bss_chains, iter = fit_iter, warmup = fit_warmup,
          control = list(adapt_delta=fit_delta, max_treedepth=fit_treedep),
          seed = params$bss_seed,
          cores = params$bss_cores,
          # B51 (2026-09-29): the initial-value radius, run_config$bss_init_r (0.5 shipped;
          # rstan's default is 2, the value every render before B51 used). D33.
          init_r = params$bss_init_r %||% 2
        )
        timer_stop(paste0("BSS_", label, "_att", attempt))

        gate_try <- tryCatch(
          bss_compute_gate(list(fit = fit_try, pe_fallback = FALSE), label,
                           catch_par        = "C_expected_sum",
                           effort_par       = "E_sum",
                           max_impact_sd    = params$max_divergence_total_impact_sd %||% 0.10,
                           max_div_fraction = params$max_divergence_fraction %||% 0.05,
                           ar_resolution    = attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution")),
          error = function(e) { bss_warn("gate", sprintf("%s attempt %d: the convergence gate could not be computed (%s).", label, attempt, conditionMessage(e))); NULL })

        # 2026-09-04: keep this rung's ANSWER, not only its sampler diagnostics. The loop
        # overwrites `fit` on the next attempt, so without this the estimate produced at
        # every rung except the surviving one is lost, and the whole reason to run a ladder
        # is to see how the answer depends on the resolution. It also makes
        # params$ar_escalate_select's precision tie-break implementable at all.
        .rung <- bss_ar_rung_summary(fit_try)
        # 2026-09-06: adequacy PER RUNG. Only the kept fit reaches write_bss_diagnostics(),
        # so on the 2026-09-04 ladder the two coarser rungs cost 174 minutes and left no
        # p_loo, no Pareto k and no coverage. See 03_R_functions/bss_rung_adequacy.R.
        .radq <- if (isTRUE(params$ar_rung_adequacy %||% TRUE) && length(ar_ladder) > 1)
                   bss_rung_adequacy(fit_try, bss_data_try) else
                   bss_rung_adequacy(NULL, NULL)
        ar_escalation_log[[length(ar_escalation_log) + 1]] <- tibble(
          fit                = label,
          attempt            = attempt,
          n_attempts_planned = length(ar_ladder),
          ar_resolution      = attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution") %||% NA_character_,
          P_n                = bss_data_try$P_n,
          escalation_enabled = .esc_on,
          divergences        = gate_try$divergences        %||% NA_integer_,
          divergence_fraction= gate_try$divergence_fraction %||% NA_real_,
          impact_C_sd        = gate_try$impact_C_sd        %||% NA_real_,
          pass_convergence   = gate_try$pass_convergence   %||% NA,
          # The rung's own estimate. catch_* is the expected-catch season total, the same
          # quantity the gate scores, so the verdict and the number refer to one thing.
          catch_median       = .rung$catch_median,
          catch_lo95         = .rung$catch_lo95,
          catch_hi95         = .rung$catch_hi95,
          pi_width           = .rung$pi_width,
          pi_width_rel       = .rung$pi_width_rel,
          effort_median      = .rung$effort_median,
          p_loo              = .radq$p_loo,
          p_loo_frac         = .radq$p_loo_frac,
          n_pareto_bad       = .radq$n_pareto_bad,
          cov50_gear         = .radq$cov50_gear,
          cov50_catch        = .radq$cov50_catch,
          pit_mean_catch     = .radq$pit_mean_catch,
          selected           = FALSE      # set on the surviving rung after the loop
        )

        # ---- which rung's fit is kept ------------------------------------------
        # params$ar_escalate_stop:
        #   "first_pass" (DEFAULT, and the pre-2026-09-04 behaviour exactly): stop at the
        #      finest rung that passes the convergence gate and report it. Cheapest, and it
        #      is the production rule: a component reports at the finest resolution the
        #      sampler can actually support this season.
        #   "all_rungs": fit EVERY rung on the ladder and keep the one params$
        #      ar_escalate_select names. This is the DIAGNOSTIC mode. It costs one fit per
        #      rung but it answers, in a single run and a single output folder, how the
        #      estimate depends on resolution, which three separate forced runs answer far
        #      more expensively and with the rungs scattered across three folders.
        #
        # Only ONE stanfit beyond the incumbent is ever held in memory: the challenger
        # replaces the incumbent or is discarded immediately. Holding the whole ladder would
        # be several GB for a daily shore fit.
        .stop_rule   <- params$ar_escalate_stop   %||% "first_pass"
        .select_rule <- params$ar_escalate_select %||% "first_pass"
        # 2026-09-28 (B46): a gate that ERRORS is a rung not shown to pass, so it escalates
        # (bounded by ar_escalate_max_attempts) instead of stopping the ladder as a pass.
        # The authoritative gate in the totals section recomputes the verdict either way.
        if (is.null(gate_try)) message(sprintf("  WARNING: %s attempt %d: the convergence gate errored; treated as NOT passed.", label, attempt))
        .passed      <- !is.null(gate_try) && isTRUE(gate_try$pass_convergence)
        .keep <- if (is.null(fit)) TRUE                    # nothing kept yet
                 else if (identical(.stop_rule, "first_pass")) TRUE
                 else if (!.passed) FALSE                  # never report a rung that failed
                 else if (!isTRUE(.incumbent_passed)) TRUE  # first passing rung wins outright
                 else if (identical(.select_rule, "narrowest_pi"))
                   isTRUE(.rung$pi_width_rel < (.incumbent_pi_rel %||% Inf))
                 else FALSE                                # "first_pass": keep the finest
        if (.keep) {
          bss_data <- bss_data_try; fit <- fit_try
          ar_resolutions[[label]] <- attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution")
          .incumbent_passed <- .passed
          .incumbent_pi_rel <- .rung$pi_width_rel
          # 2026-09-04: record the ATTEMPT NUMBER kept, not just its resolution. The
          # post-loop marker used to re-derive the selected row by matching the resolution
          # string and taking the last match, which is wrong whenever two rungs share a
          # resolution. On the 2026-09-03 A1 stage all four rungs read "daily", so the log
          # marked attempt 4 as reported while `.keep` had actually retained attempt 1.
          .kept_attempt[[label]] <- attempt
        }

        if (identical(.stop_rule, "all_rungs") && .esc_on) {
          if (attempt < length(ar_ladder)) {
            cat(sprintf("  [all_rungs] %s AR %s the gate; fitting %s next for the ladder.\n",
                        attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution"),
                        if (.passed) "PASSED" else "failed", ar_ladder[attempt + 1]))
            next
          } else break
        }

        if (.passed) break
        if (!.esc_on) break
        if (attempt < length(ar_ladder)) {
          cat(sprintf(paste0("  Gate FAILED at %s AR; escalating to %s and refitting ",
                             "(improvement 7 ladder).\n"),
                      attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution"), ar_ladder[attempt + 1]))
          bss_warn("gate", sprintf("%s: the gate FAILED at %s AR; refitting at %s (the escalation ladder).",
                                   label, attr(bss_data_try, "ar_resolution"), ar_ladder[attempt + 1]), severity = "note")
        } else {
          cat(paste0("  Gate FAILED at the coarsest rung on the ladder; this component will ",
                     "report the Point Estimator.\n"))
        }
      }

      if (too_thin) next

      # --- Extract BOTH expected and predictive catch ---
      bss_pars <- c("C_sum","C_expected_sum","E_sum","B1","B2","B1_C_out","B2_C_out")
      if(bss_data$IE_n > 0) bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "sigma_IE_out")
      # improvement 4: B3_out (razor only) is replaced by the B_open_out vector; the
      # column labels live in attr(bss_data, "opener_labels").
      if(bss_data$K_open > 0) bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "B_open_out")
      # improvement 8: report the OSP crab-only lower bound alongside f itself.
      if(isTRUE(bss_data$osp_crab_lower == 1L)) bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "f_lower_out")
      if(bss_data$apply_crab_fraction == 1L) bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "f_crab_out")
      # review item 1B (2026-09-08): the dynamic-f scale parameters, when the walk is live.
      if (isTRUE(bss_data$crab_fraction_dynamic == 1L) && isTRUE(bss_data$crab_fraction_estimate == 1L)) {
        bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "sigma_f_out", "cfi_kappa_out")
        # 2026-09-09: the combo-trip share walk, when typed contacts or an OSP stream feed it.
        if (isTRUE(bss_data$combo_dynamic == 1L)) bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "combo_c_out", "sigma_c_out", "cfc_kappa_out")
      }
      if(isTRUE(params$estimate_cpue_density)) bss_pars <- c(bss_pars, "gamma_C_out")           # item 6b
      bss_summ <- summary(fit, pars=bss_pars)$summary
      cat("  BSS Summary:\n"); print(bss_summ)
      write.csv(as.data.frame(bss_summ), file.path(output_dir, paste0("bss_summary_",label,".csv")))

      # review item 1B: f by stratum, LABELLED and beside the data that informed it. Stan
      # reports f_crab_out[k] by index only; this file says which month k is, how many
      # contacts and OSP boats it carried, and where the walk linked it.
      .fs <- attr(bss_data, "f_strata")
      if (bss_data$apply_crab_fraction == 1L && is.data.frame(.fs)) {
        .fq <- summary(fit, pars = "f_crab_out")$summary
        .fs_out <- cbind(as.data.frame(.fs),
                         f_median = .fq[, "50%"], f_lo95 = .fq[, "2.5%"], f_hi95 = .fq[, "97.5%"],
                         f_n_eff = round(.fq[, "n_eff"]), f_Rhat = round(.fq[, "Rhat"], 4))
        # 2026-09-09: the combo-trip share c per stratum and the implied crab-only share
        # f(1 - c), which is what OSP's crabbing-only column should read.
        if (isTRUE(bss_data$combo_dynamic == 1L)) {
          .cq <- summary(fit, pars = "combo_c_out")$summary; .lq <- summary(fit, pars = "f_lower_out")$summary
          .fs_out <- cbind(.fs_out, c_median = .cq[, "50%"], c_lo95 = .cq[, "2.5%"], c_hi95 = .cq[, "97.5%"],
                           crab_only_share_median = .lq[, "50%"], crab_only_share_lo95 = .lq[, "2.5%"], crab_only_share_hi95 = .lq[, "97.5%"])
        }
        write.csv(.fs_out, file.path(output_dir, paste0("crab_fraction_strata_", label, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
      }

      # improvement 4: Stan reports B_open_out[1], B_open_out[2], ... with no idea which
      # opener each index is. Without this map an opener-active run's structural table is
      # unreadable. Written per fit because the surviving columns are per fit (a covariate
      # that is not identifiable inside one sub-season's window is dropped for that fit).
      .olab <- attr(bss_data, "opener_labels")
      if (length(.olab) > 0)
        write.csv(tibble(index = seq_along(.olab), parameter = sprintf("B_open_out[%d]", seq_along(.olab)),
                         opener = .olab),
                  file.path(output_dir, paste0("opener_covariates_", label, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)

      C_draws <- rstan::extract(fit, "C_sum")$C_sum           # Stan's Poisson predictive (reconciliation only)
      C_exp_draws <- rstan::extract(fit, "C_expected_sum")$C_expected_sum  # expected (no noise)
      E_draws <- rstan::extract(fit, "E_sum")$E_sum
      # B46 (2026-09-28): the predictive total from the fitted observation model (party-level
      # ZINB, bss_predictive_catch.R); the Stan C_sum is Poisson and under-dispersed.
      C_pred_draws <- tryCatch(bss_predictive_catch(fit, bss_data, bss_predictive_seed(params$bss_seed, label)),
                               error = function(e) { bss_warn("fit", sprintf("%s: the predictive catch could not be drawn from the fitted observation model (%s); Stan's Poisson C_sum stands in, which UNDERSTATES the predictive interval.", label, conditionMessage(e))); NULL }) %||% C_draws

      bss_all[[label]] <- list(
        C_sum = quantile(C_draws, c(0.025,0.5,0.975)),
        C_expected_sum = quantile(C_exp_draws, c(0.025,0.5,0.975)),
        E_sum = quantile(E_draws, c(0.025,0.5,0.975)),
        C_draws = C_draws, C_exp_draws = C_exp_draws, C_pred_draws = C_pred_draws, E_draws = E_draws,
        fit = fit, pe_fallback = FALSE, bss_data = bss_data, days_ss = days_ss,
        population = pop, subseason = ss$name, catch_group = cg
      )

      # --- Use C_expected (no Poisson noise) for primary estimates ---
      E_bss <- rstan::extract(fit, "E")$E
      C_exp_bss <- rstan::extract(fit, "C_expected")$C_expected

      E_daily <- tibble(
        event_date = days_ss$event_date,
        median = apply(E_bss[,1,,1], 2, median),
        lo95 = apply(E_bss[,1,,1], 2, quantile, 0.025),
        hi95 = apply(E_bss[,1,,1], 2, quantile, 0.975)
      )

      C_daily <- tibble(
        event_date = days_ss$event_date,
        median = apply(C_exp_bss[,1,,1], 2, median),
        lo95 = apply(C_exp_bss[,1,,1], 2, quantile, 0.025),
        hi95 = apply(C_exp_bss[,1,,1], 2, quantile, 0.975)
      )

      # BSS effort plot
      p_bss_eff <- E_daily |>
        ggplot(aes(x = event_date)) +
        geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue") +
        geom_line(aes(y = median), color = "steelblue") +
        labs(title = sprintf("Daily effort: %s", short_fit(label)),
             subtitle = sprintf("Median with 95%% credible interval (%s AR(1))",
                                attr(bss_data, "ar_resolution") %||% "adaptive"),
             # improvement 1: the axis said "Crabber-hours" long after the v7.6/v7.7 move
             # to gear-deployments. E carries the CPUE denominator's unit by construction
             # (bss_effort_spec), so read it from the fit's own data rather than hardcoding.
             x = "Date", y = sprintf("Effort (%s)", bss_data$.effort_unit %||% "gear-deployments")) +
        theme_bw()
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("plot_bss_effort_", label, ".png")),
             p_bss_eff, width = 10, height = 6)

      # BSS catch plot (using expected catch)
      p_bss_catch <- C_daily |>
        ggplot(aes(x = event_date)) +
        geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), alpha = 0.2, fill = "darkgreen") +
        geom_line(aes(y = median), color = "darkgreen") +
        labs(title = sprintf("Daily expected catch: %s", short_fit(label)),
             subtitle = "E[C|data] with 95% CI (no Poisson sampling noise)",
             x = "Date", y = "Expected Dungeness caught") +
        theme_bw()
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("plot_bss_catch_", label, ".png")),
             p_bss_catch, width = 10, height = 6)

      # Posterior densities
      p_bss_post <- tibble(
        `Expected Catch` = C_exp_draws,
        `Predictive Catch` = C_pred_draws,
        `Effort` = E_draws
      ) |>
        pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "param", values_to = "value") |>
        ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = param)) +
        geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
        facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free") +
        scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
        labs(title = sprintf("Season-total posteriors: %s", short_fit(label)),
             subtitle = "Effort in gear deployments; catch in Dungeness crab. Density is relative within each panel.",
             x = "Season total", y = NULL) +
        theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("plot_bss_posteriors_", label, ".png")),
             p_bss_post, width = 14, height = 5)

      write.csv(E_daily, file.path(output_dir, paste0("bss_daily_effort_", label, ".csv")), row.names=FALSE)
      write.csv(C_daily, file.path(output_dir, paste0("bss_daily_catch_", label, ".csv")), row.names=FALSE)

      # Save L posterior if estimated
      if(bss_data$estimate_L == 1) {
        L_post <- rstan::extract(fit, "L_out")$L_out  # [draws, D]
        # improvement 1/2: the old column name L_prior_mu was doubly misleading. It was
        # filled with days_ss$L_mu (the L_effective HOURS regression) even when L in the
        # model is tau_shore / tau_boat (a turnover), so it did not describe the prior the
        # fit actually used. Report the prior CENTRE Stan was given, name the unit, and
        # keep the day-length regression in its own clearly-labelled column.
        L_daily <- tibble(
          event_date = days_ss$event_date,
          L_unit = bss_data$.L_unit %||% NA_character_,
          L_prior_center = bss_data$L_data,
          L_prior_sigma_log = bss_data$L_prior_sigma,
          L_effective_hours_regression = days_ss$L_mu,
          L_posterior_median = apply(L_post, 2, median),
          L_posterior_lo95 = apply(L_post, 2, quantile, 0.025),
          L_posterior_hi95 = apply(L_post, 2, quantile, 0.975)
        )
        write.csv(L_daily, file.path(output_dir, paste0("bss_L_effective_", label, ".csv")), row.names=FALSE)
      }
    }
  }
}
timer_stop("5_BSS_model_runs")

# improvement 7: persist the ladder. One row per attempt, with the gate verdict that
# decided whether to escalate, so the resolution actually used by each component is
# auditable rather than implicit.
ar_escalation_df <- if (length(ar_escalation_log)) bind_rows(ar_escalation_log) else NULL
# Mark the rung whose fit was actually kept, so the log says which number was reported
# rather than leaving the reader to infer it from the ordering. Under "first_pass" that is
# the last row per fit; under "all_rungs" it can be any row, which is exactly why the flag
# is needed.
if (!is.null(ar_escalation_df) && nrow(ar_escalation_df)) {
  for (.lb in unique(ar_escalation_df$fit)) {
    # 2026-09-04: match on the recorded ATTEMPT INDEX. Matching on the resolution string
    # and taking the last hit silently mislabels the reported rung whenever two rungs
    # carry the same resolution, which is precisely the state a broken ladder leaves the
    # log in, i.e. exactly when a reader most needs the flag to be trustworthy.
    .ka <- .kept_attempt[[.lb]] %||% NA_integer_
    .i <- if (!is.na(.ka)) which(ar_escalation_df$fit == .lb & ar_escalation_df$attempt == .ka) else integer(0)
    if (!length(.i)) {   # pre-2026-09-04 logs have no tracker; fall back to the old rule
      .sel <- ar_resolutions[[.lb]] %||% NA_character_
      .i <- utils::tail(which(ar_escalation_df$fit == .lb &
                              ar_escalation_df$ar_resolution %in% .sel), 1)
    }
    if (length(.i)) ar_escalation_df$selected[.i] <- TRUE
  }
}
if (!is.null(ar_escalation_df))
  write.csv(ar_escalation_df, file.path(output_dir, "ar_escalation_log.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

fit_settings_df <- if (length(fit_settings_log)) dplyr::bind_rows(fit_settings_log) else NULL
if (!is.null(fit_settings_df)) {
  .tl <- bss_timer_log()
  fit_settings_df$minutes <- vapply(sprintf("BSS_%s_att%d", fit_settings_df$fit, fit_settings_df$attempt),
                                    function(k) round(as.numeric(.tl[[k]]$elapsed %||% NA), 1), numeric(1))
  utils::write.csv(fit_settings_df, file.path(output_dir, "fit_settings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  report_table(dplyr::transmute(fit_settings_df, Fit = short_fit(fit), Attempt = attempt, AR = ar_resolution,
                                `AR periods` = P_n, Days = days, `Effort obs` = effort_obs, Interviews = interviews, `I/E obs` = ie_obs,
                                `Iter (warmup)` = sprintf("%d (%d)", iter, warmup), `Max treedepth` = max_treedepth,
                                `adapt_delta` = adapt_delta, init_r = init_r, Minutes = minutes),
               digits = 2, caption = paste("How each fit was run: the AR resolution the coverage rule and the cap chose, the data it",

}

```{r ar-escalation-show, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(ar_escalation_df) && nrow(ar_escalation_df) > 0 &&
    # 2026-09-04: read the per-fit flag the loop already recorded. This condition used
    # isTRUE(params$ar_escalate), which is FALSE for every scoped form, so the table was
    # rendered only by the row-count fallback; with a one-rung ladder it would have been
    # dropped entirely.
    (any(ar_escalation_df$escalation_enabled %in% TRUE) ||
     nrow(ar_escalation_df) > length(bss_all))) {
  report_table(
    dplyr::transmute(ar_escalation_df,
      Fit = short_fit(fit), Attempt = attempt, `AR resolution` = ar_resolution,
      `AR periods` = P_n, Divergences = divergences,
      `Div. fraction` = divergence_fraction, `Impact (SD)` = impact_C_sd,
      `Passed gate` = pass_convergence,
      # 2026-09-04: each rung's OWN answer, so a reader can see how the estimate depends on
      # resolution instead of only seeing the one that survived.
      `Catch (median)` = round(catch_median), `95% lo` = round(catch_lo95),
      `95% hi` = round(catch_hi95), `PI width` = round(pi_width),
      `PI width / median` = round(pi_width_rel, 3),
      Reported = selected),
    caption = paste("AR resolution escalation ladder. Each component starts at the finest rung",
                    "and is refit one rung coarser whenever it fails the convergence gate,",
                    "stopping at the first rung that passes (ar_escalate_stop = 'first_pass');",
                    "under 'all_rungs' every rung is fitted and ar_escalate_select decides which",
                    "is reported. The Reported column marks the rung whose fit was kept. Each",
                    "rung's own catch estimate and 95% interval are shown so the sensitivity of",
                    "the answer to resolution is visible here rather than only in the surviving",
                    "row. NOTE that a narrower interval is not by itself evidence of a better",
                    "model: on the 2026-08/09 boat 2x2 the two MISCALIBRATED cells had the",
                    "narrowest relative intervals. With ar_escalate = FALSE there is one row per",
                    "fit and this table simply records the single attempt.")) |> print()
} else if (!is.null(ar_escalation_df)) {
  cat("_AR escalation is off (`ar_escalate = FALSE`); each component was fitted once, at the resolution the coverage rule and `ar_max_resolution` selected._")
}

## 6. Convergence gate and model selection

The scale-aware gate decides, per fit, whether the component reports its Bayesian posterior or falls back to its PE point. A fit passes only if R-hat is below 1.01, the effective sample size is above 400, the divergent fraction is under the 5% backstop, and the divergent draws move neither reported total by more than 0.10 posterior standard deviations (Betancourt 2017). **Method** in the table is what the totals use. A PE fallback on a data-thin component is a measured outcome, not an error; the component's Bayesian draws are then not used anywhere in the totals. Model adequacy, which the gate does not judge, is in [Section 11](#model-diagnostics).

```{r gate, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.6b SCALE-AWARE CONVERGENCE GATE (B1.8) ----
# Compute the pass/fail gate ONCE per fit here, immediately after fitting, and
# store the decision (use_bss) plus a full diagnostic row (gate_info) on each
# bss_all entry. Sections 7.7, 7.8, and 7.8b consume use_bss through bss_use_pe_for()
# below, and 7.11 simply assembles the stored gate_info rows. This makes the gate
# the single authoritative source of method selection: previously 7.7/7.8/7.8b
# keyed off pe_fallback (data sufficiency) alone, so a fit with enough data but a
# failed gate would still have been summed into the BSS totals. Wiring use_bss
# into the totals closes that gap. (When it landed, every fitted 2024-25 component
# passed the gate, so no total moved; the run's own verdicts are in convergence_report.csv.)
# A weakly-identified fit that fails the gate correctly falls back to PE
# everywhere, not only in the report labels.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n CONVERGENCE GATE (scale-aware, B1.8)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

# The scale-aware gate lives in the shared module
# 03_R_functions/bss_convergence_gate.R (bss_compute_gate / bss_use_pe_for), so the
# pooled and gear-resolved tracks share ONE gate and cannot drift. bss_compute_gate()
# takes the two gate thresholds as arguments (pooled passes its own params values)
# and the per-fit AR-resolution label for the report column; it gates on
# C_expected_sum and E_sum. The single
# pooled-only, REPORT-ONLY column B1_C_rhat (weekend-CPUE-effect R-hat, never part
# of the pass/fail decision) is re-attached at the call site so
# convergence_report.csv keeps its historical schema.
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b  <- bss_all[[label]]
  gi <- bss_compute_gate(
    b, label,
    catch_par        = "C_expected_sum",
    effort_par       = "E_sum",
    max_impact_sd    = params$max_divergence_total_impact_sd %||% 0.10,
    # Fallback matches the params value set above (0.05 as of P7, 2026-07-12) and the
    # shared function default, so the gate behaves identically if the param is ever
    # absent (pooled passes params$max_divergence_fraction = 0.05).
    max_div_fraction = params$max_divergence_fraction %||% 0.05,
    ar_resolution    = ar_resolutions[[label]] %||% NA_character_
  )
  # Re-attach the pooled-only B1_C_rhat report column (report-only, NOT gating),
  # right after E_sum_neff to preserve the historical column order. tryCatch
  # yields NA for PE-only entries (no fit to summarize).
  b1c_rhat <- tryCatch(
    round(summary(b$fit, pars = "B1_C_out")$summary["B1_C_out", "Rhat"], 4),
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  gi <- tibble::add_column(gi, B1_C_rhat = b1c_rhat, .after = "E_sum_neff")
  bss_all[[label]]$gate_info <- gi
  bss_all[[label]]$use_bss   <- isTRUE(gi$pass_convergence)
}

# PE-vs-BSS selection uses the shared bss_use_pe_for(): report PE if the fit never
# ran OR failed the gate. Sections 7.7 / 7.8 / 7.8b call bss_use_pe_for() below.


```

```{r convergence-report, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.11 CONVERGENCE REPORT ----
# v7.0 (B1.8): the pass/fail decision and every diagnostic column are computed once
# in 7.6b (bss_compute_gate) and stored as bss_all[[label]]$gate_info, so this section
# is now pure assembly. This guarantees the report agrees with the method actually
# used in the totals (7.7/7.8/7.8b consume the same use_bss flag). All gate
# warnings were already emitted in 7.6b at fit time. Columns now include the
# scale-aware impact (impact_C_sd, impact_E_sd; the gating criterion) and retain
# the legacy level-distortion (distortion_C, distortion_E) as reported-only.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n CONVERGENCE REPORT\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

convergence_df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(bss_all), function(label) bss_all[[label]]$gate_info))
print(convergence_df)
write.csv(convergence_df, file.path(output_dir, "convergence_report.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

```{r convergence-report-show, echo=FALSE}
# Curated, HTML-friendly view of the convergence report: short fit labels and the key
# gate columns only. The full ~20-column table (treedepth, level-distortion, and the
# per-criterion pass flags) is written to convergence_report.csv.
conv_disp <- tryCatch(
  dplyr::transmute(convergence_df,
    Fit             = short_fit(fit),
    AR              = ar_resolution,
    Div             = divergences,
    `Div frac`      = round(divergence_fraction, 3),
    `R-hat C`       = sprintf("%.3f", C_sum_rhat),
    `R-hat E`       = sprintf("%.3f", E_sum_rhat),
    `min n_eff`     = pmin(C_sum_neff, E_sum_neff),
    `Impact C (SD)` = round(impact_C_sd, 3),
    `Impact E (SD)` = round(impact_E_sd, 3),
    Pass            = pass_convergence,
    Method          = method_selected),
  error = function(e) { bss_warn("gate", paste("Curated convergence view not built; the full table is shown:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); convergence_df })
report_table(conv_disp,
  paste("Per-fit convergence summary (key gate columns; full detail in",
        "convergence_report.csv). Div frac is the divergent-transition fraction (backstop",
        "0.05); Impact C/E (SD) is the scale-aware gating criterion (threshold 0.10);",
        "Method is what the totals actually use. Healthy: R-hat near 1.00, min n_eff",
        "above 400, Pass = TRUE."),
  digits = 3)
```


## 7. Headline result: port total

The harvest estimate: the sum of the components, reported as expected catch with a 95% credible interval, which is the number to cite. A component that passed the gate contributes its posterior draws; one that did not contributes its PE point as a constant. The commercial census is exact on the count and enters as a constant; the charter expansion carries its sampling SE. **Read with the extrapolation share in [Section 11.4](#summer-extrapolation-transparency-t1.1)**: much of each fitted component's catch falls on days with no interview, where the catch rate is the model's.

```{r port-total, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.7 COMBINED BSS PORT TOTAL ----
timer_start("6_outputs")
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n COMBINED RESULTS\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

n_draws_max <- max(sapply(bss_all, function(b) {
  if(bss_use_pe_for(b)) return(0)   # B1.8: a gate-failed fit contributes no BSS draws
  length(b$C_exp_draws)
}))
if(n_draws_max == 0) n_draws_max <- params$bss_chains * (params$bss_iter_default - params$bss_warmup_default)

.cc_draws_by_cg <- list()   # 2026-09-28 (B43): the census draws, kept for the season totals below
for(cg in bss_catch_groups) {
  bss_C_total <- rep(0, n_draws_max)    # expected catch
  bss_C_pred_total <- rep(0, n_draws_max) # predictive catch
  bss_E_total <- rep(0, n_draws_max)

  for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
    for(ss in subseasons) {
      label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_", cg)
      pe_label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
      b <- bss_all[[label]]

      if(bss_use_pe_for(b)) {   # B1.8: PE if insufficient data OR failed scale-aware gate
        bss_C_total <- bss_C_total + (pe_all[[pe_label]][[cg]] %||% 0)
        bss_C_pred_total <- bss_C_pred_total + (pe_all[[pe_label]][[cg]] %||% 0)
        bss_E_total <- bss_E_total + pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_total
      } else {
        n <- length(b$C_exp_draws)
        idx <- rep_len(1:n, n_draws_max)
        bss_C_total <- bss_C_total + b$C_exp_draws[idx]
        bss_C_pred_total <- bss_C_pred_total + (b$C_pred_draws %||% b$C_draws)[idx]
        bss_E_total <- bss_E_total + b$E_draws[idx]
      }
    }
  }
  # Review item 4 (2026-09-08/09), split in two on 2026-09-11: the commercial part is a
  # census (a constant), the charter part an expansion over the charter trip frame. What
  # enters the port interval is carried_se, which census_uncertainty selects: "charter"
  # (shipped) the charter expansion alone, "none" nothing, "sampling" everything (the
  # commercial per-vessel mean and, under census_expansion = "day_type", the imputation).
  # Draws are clamped at observed_dung, the commercial census plus the charter crab
  # actually observed on the interviewed trips.
  .cc <- pe_all$comm_charter
  .cc_draws <- rep(.cc[[cg]] %||% 0, n_draws_max)
  if (cg == "Dungeness_Kept" && is.finite(.cc$carried_se %||% NA) && (.cc$carried_se %||% 0) > 0) {
    # 2026-09-26 (B38): seeded, so the port total is reproducible between identical runs.
    # Together with the draw permutation bss_stan_fit() rebuilds from the Stan seed, this removes the ~0.1-0.2%
    # Monte Carlo jitter the port median carried between bit-identical fits.
    # B46 (2026-09-28): the same seeded draws, with the caller's RNG restored afterwards.
    .cc_draws <- bss_with_seed(params$bss_seed %||% 1L, pmax(rnorm(n_draws_max, .cc$Dungeness_Kept, .cc$carried_se), .cc$observed_dung %||% 0))
    cat(sprintf(paste0("  Census enters the port interval with SE %s under census_uncertainty = '%s' (total SE %s: charter expansion %s, ",
                       "commercial per-vessel mean %s, imputation %s; census_expansion = '%s', %d unsampled calendar days).\n"),
                format(round(.cc$carried_se), big.mark = ","), .cc$census_uncertainty %||% "charter",
                format(round(.cc$Dungeness_Kept_se %||% 0), big.mark = ","), format(round(.cc$charter_se %||% 0), big.mark = ","),
                format(round(.cc$commercial_se %||% 0), big.mark = ","), format(round(sqrt(.cc$imputation_var %||% 0)), big.mark = ","),
                .cc$census_expansion %||% "none", sum(!.cc$daily_full$observed)))
  }

  # --- 2026-09-13: THE CENSUS FRAME WARNINGS, IN THE REPORT ------------------------------
  # Matt, on whether estimate_comm_charter() should stop rather than warn on a missing
  # census frame: "a warning is fine - included in the html report." A bare warning() does
  # not satisfy that. knitr defers warnings to the end of a chunk, an html_document can be
  # told to hide them, and a batch runner rendering with quiet = TRUE never shows them at
  # all -- which is how a run whose census component is 0 because the frame is missing can
  # look like a run whose census component is genuinely small. So the conditions come back
  # from the function as DATA and are printed here unconditionally, and written to
  # census_frame_warnings.csv so a verdict block can read them from the output folder
  # without re-running anything.
  # 2026-09-29: this chunk is results='hide', so the block it printed here never reached the page.
  # The conditions are now in Section 4.2 and the run-warnings log (Section 16), and in the CSV.
  .fw <- .cc$frame_warnings %||% character(0)
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(n = seq_along(.fw), warning = if (length(.fw)) .fw else character(0),
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                   file.path(output_dir, "census_frame_warnings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  bss_C_total <- bss_C_total + .cc_draws
  bss_C_pred_total <- bss_C_pred_total + .cc_draws
  bss_E_total <- bss_E_total + pe_all$comm_charter$effort_total
  .cc_draws_by_cg[[cg]] <- .cc_draws
  # 2026-09-29: the component table (Section 7) and the BSS catch by mode (Section 9) read these.
  if (identical(cg, "Dungeness_Kept")) port_C_draws <- bss_C_total

  final_table <- tibble(
    Catch_Group = cg,
    Estimate = c("Effort", "Expected_Catch", "Predictive_Catch"),
    PE = c(round(pe_port_total("effort_total")),
           round(pe_port_total(cg)),
           NA),
    BSS_median = c(round(median(bss_E_total)), round(median(bss_C_total)), round(median(bss_C_pred_total))),
    BSS_lo95 = c(round(quantile(bss_E_total,0.025)), round(quantile(bss_C_total,0.025)), round(quantile(bss_C_pred_total,0.025))),
    BSS_hi95 = c(round(quantile(bss_E_total,0.975)), round(quantile(bss_C_total,0.975)), round(quantile(bss_C_pred_total,0.975)))
  )

  cat(sprintf("\n--- Port Total: %s ---\n", cg))
  print(final_table)
  write.csv(final_table, file.path(output_dir, paste0("port_total_",cg,".csv")), row.names=FALSE)
}


```

```{r season-totals, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# ============================================================================
# SEASON-LEVEL TOTALS (2026-09-10; caption corrected 2026-09-08, review item 7). On a
# multi-season span every sub-season carries a `season` tag from build_subseasons(), so
# the port-total draw assembly above can be rerun PER SEASON: same draws, same PE
# fallbacks, same gate decisions, grouped by the season each fitted sub-season belongs
# to. Each sub-season is an INDEPENDENT Stan fit (the driver loops over the sub-season
# list); a span shares nothing across seasons except the pooled shore turnover derivation and
# the config priors, so season totals from a span match standalone runs up to those. The commercial/charter census contributes
# per season when census_windows is configured (estimate_comm_charter()$by_season);
# with the scalar census keys its single window is attributed to the season containing
# census_start_date, and the table says so. Written to season_totals.csv always;
# rendered in the HTML when the run spans more than one season.
# ============================================================================
.seasons <- unique(na.omit(vapply(subseasons, function(x) x$season %||% NA_character_, character(1))))
# 2026-09-28 (B43): THE CENSUS ENTERS A SEASON TOTAL THE WAY IT ENTERS THE PORT TOTAL. It entered
# as a constant, so a season total lacked the charter expansion's uncertainty and, on a single
# season, disagreed with port_total_*.csv by a few crab: the first render of the method of record
# wrote 96,110 [79,428, 120,560] here against 96,118 [79,418, 120,558] there, and every run that
# carried the census SE had the same kind of gap (2 to 13 crab). The season that holds the WHOLE census
# reuses the port block's seeded draws, so a single-season total IS the port total, draw for draw;
# seasons that share the census (per-season windows) draw their own, seeded from bss_seed and the
# season's position, with the caller's RNG restored.
# The scalar census (no census_windows) belongs to the season whose sub-seasons contain
# census_start_date; failing that (a window that starts inside the census window), to the season
# whose sub-seasons overlap [census_start_date, census_end_date]; failing that, to the only season.
# Before 2026-09-28 the second and third cases dropped the census from the season total while the
# port total kept it.
.scalar_census_season <- local({
  cs <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(params$census_start_date %||% NA))
  ce <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(params$census_end_date %||% NA))
  s_of <- function(test) unique(na.omit(vapply(subseasons, function(x) if (isTRUE(test(x))) x$season %||% NA_character_ else NA_character_, character(1))))
  hit <- s_of(function(x) !is.na(cs) && cs >= x$start && cs <= x$end)
  if (!length(hit)) hit <- s_of(function(x) !is.na(cs) && !is.na(ce) && x$start <= ce && x$end >= cs)
  if (!length(hit) && length(.seasons) == 1L) hit <- .seasons
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
})
.ccs_for <- function(sn) {
  cc <- pe_all$comm_charter
  if (!is.null(cc$by_season)) return(cc$by_season[[sn]])
  if (identical(sn, .scalar_census_season)) cc else NULL
}
.n_census_seasons <- sum(vapply(.seasons, function(sn) !is.null(.ccs_for(sn)), logical(1)))
# The port block's census draws may stand in for a season's census only when that season holds the
# WHOLE census: the scalar path, or per-season windows of which this run's season is the only one
# (a census_windows entry for a season outside the run is in the port total, so it is not this
# season's to absorb).
.census_is_whole <- function(sn) {
  cc <- pe_all$comm_charter
  is.null(cc$by_season) || (length(cc$by_season) == 1L && identical(names(cc$by_season), sn))
}
.season_census_draws <- function(ccs, cg, n, seed) {
  if (!identical(cg, "Dungeness_Kept") || !is.finite(ccs$carried_se %||% NA) || (ccs$carried_se %||% 0) <= 0)
    return(rep(ccs[[cg]] %||% 0, n))
  had <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  old <- if (had) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE) else NULL
  on.exit(if (had) assign(".Random.seed", old, envir = globalenv())
          else if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
  set.seed(seed)
  pmax(rnorm(n, ccs$Dungeness_Kept, ccs$carried_se), ccs$observed_dung %||% 0)
}
if (length(.seasons)) {
  season_rows <- list()
  for (cg in bss_catch_groups) for (sn in .seasons) {
    sC <- rep(0, n_draws_max); sE <- rep(0, n_draws_max); s_pe_C <- 0; s_pe_E <- 0
    for (pop in c("shore", "private_boat")) for (ss in subseasons) {
      if (!identical(ss$season %||% NA_character_, sn)) next
      label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_", cg); pe_label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
      b <- bss_all[[label]]
      s_pe_C <- s_pe_C + (pe_all[[pe_label]][[cg]] %||% 0)
      s_pe_E <- s_pe_E + (pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_total %||% 0)
      if (bss_use_pe_for(b)) {
        sC <- sC + (pe_all[[pe_label]][[cg]] %||% 0)
        sE <- sE + (pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_total %||% 0)
      } else {
        idx <- rep_len(seq_along(b$C_exp_draws), n_draws_max)
        sC <- sC + b$C_exp_draws[idx]; sE <- sE + b$E_draws[idx]
      }
    }
    # census: per season when available, else attribute the scalar window's season (B43: as draws)
    ccs <- .ccs_for(sn)
    if (!is.null(ccs))
      sC <- sC + if (.n_census_seasons == 1L && .census_is_whole(sn) && !is.null(.cc_draws_by_cg[[cg]])) .cc_draws_by_cg[[cg]] else
        .season_census_draws(ccs, cg, n_draws_max, as.integer(params$bss_seed %||% 1L) + match(sn, .seasons))
    sE <- sE + (ccs$effort_total %||% 0)
    season_rows[[paste(cg, sn)]] <- tibble(
      Catch_Group = cg, Season = sn,
      Census = if (!is.null(ccs)) round(ccs[[cg]] %||% 0) else 0,
      PE_catch = round(s_pe_C + (ccs[[cg]] %||% 0)),
      BSS_median = round(median(sC)), BSS_lo95 = round(quantile(sC, 0.025)),
      BSS_hi95 = round(quantile(sC, 0.975)),
      Effort_median = round(median(sE)))
  }
  season_totals <- dplyr::bind_rows(season_rows)
  utils::write.csv(season_totals, file.path(output_dir, "season_totals.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  if (length(.seasons) > 1) {
    cat("\n### Season totals\n\n")
    report_table(season_totals, caption = paste(
      "Per-season totals over the multi-season span. Each season sums its own fitted",
      "sub-seasons (same posterior draws and gate decisions as the port total above) plus",
      "its census component. Every sub-season is an INDEPENDENT fit with its own effort,",
      "CPUE and turnover parameters; nothing is shared across seasons except the shore",
      "turnover derivation (pooled across every I/E day unless tau_shore_derive_window_only = TRUE)",
      "and the config priors, so a season's total here equals a standalone single-season",
      "run of the same data up to those two inputs and Monte Carlo error.")) |> print()
  }
}
```

```{r port-total-show, echo=FALSE}
# 2026-09-29: the headline first, readably. Effort is on the fitted components' unit (gear
# deployments) plus the census vessel-trips, so it is labelled as such, not as a like-for-like sum.
.ft <- final_table
.ft$Estimate <- dplyr::recode(.ft$Estimate, Expected_Catch = "Dungeness kept: expected catch (the headline)",
                              Predictive_Catch = "Dungeness kept: predictive catch (a new season's observation noise)",
                              Effort = "Effort (gear deployments; census vessel-trips added)")
report_table(dplyr::transmute(.ft, Estimate, `Median` = BSS_median, `95% interval` = fmt_ci(BSS_median, BSS_lo95, BSS_hi95), `PE` = PE),
             digits = 0, caption = "Port total. The expected catch is the estimate to cite; the predictive catch adds the observation noise a repeat season would show.")

# The components behind it.
comp_rows <- list()
for (pop in c("shore", "private_boat")) for (ss in subseasons) {
  .lb <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_Dungeness_Kept"); .pl <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name); b <- bss_all[[.lb]]
  pe_pt <- pe_all[[.pl]]$Dungeness_Kept %||% NA_real_
  if (bss_use_pe_for(b)) {
    comp_rows[[.lb]] <- tibble(Component = sprintf("%s, %s", c(shore = "Shore", private_boat = "Private boat")[[pop]], ss$display_name),
                               Method = "PE (gate or data)", Median = pe_pt, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, PE = pe_pt)
  } else {
    q <- stats::quantile(b$C_exp_draws, c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975))
    comp_rows[[.lb]] <- tibble(Component = sprintf("%s, %s", c(shore = "Shore", private_boat = "Private boat")[[pop]], ss$display_name),
                               Method = "BSS", Median = q[[1]], lo = q[[2]], hi = q[[3]], PE = pe_pt)
  }
}
.cc0 <- pe_all$comm_charter
.char_draws <- .cc_draws_by_cg[["Dungeness_Kept"]] - (.cc0$commercial_dung %||% 0)
comp_rows$comm <- tibble(Component = "Commercial (census)", Method = "Census (exact count)",
                         Median = .cc0$commercial_dung %||% NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, PE = .cc0$commercial_dung %||% NA_real_)
comp_rows$char <- tibble(Component = "Charter (expansion)", Method = sprintf("Expansion (%s)", .cc0$charter_expansion %||% "vessel"),
                         Median = stats::median(.char_draws), lo = stats::quantile(.char_draws, 0.025), hi = stats::quantile(.char_draws, 0.975),
                         PE = .cc0$charter_dung %||% NA_real_)
component_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(comp_rows)
.pq <- stats::quantile(port_C_draws, c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975))
component_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(component_table,
  tibble(Component = "PORT TOTAL", Method = "sum of draws", Median = .pq[[1]], lo = .pq[[2]], hi = .pq[[3]], PE = pe_port_total("Dungeness_Kept")))
component_table$Share <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * component_table$Median / .pq[[1]])
utils::write.csv(component_table, file.path(output_dir, "component_totals.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
report_table(dplyr::transmute(component_table, Component, Method, Median = round(Median), `95% interval` = fmt_ci(Median, lo, hi),
                              PE = round(PE), `Share of port median` = Share),
             digits = 0, caption = paste("The components of the port total. Component medians do not add to the port median (medians of sums",
                                         "are not sums of medians); the port interval comes from summing the draws. Written to component_totals.csv."))
```

## 8. Monthly estimates

The total by month with 95% credible intervals. Fitted components contribute their daily posterior draws summed by month; the commercial/charter component is spread over its months by its daily catch. Monthly medians do not add to the port median.

```{r monthly, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# ---- 7.8 MONTHLY ESTIMATES ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n MONTHLY ESTIMATES\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

days_full <- prep_days_crab(params$est_date_start, params$est_date_end,
                            params, L_eff_model = L_eff_model)

month_lookup <- days_full |>
  mutate(month_label = format(event_date, "%Y-%m")) |>
  select(event_date, month_label)

all_months <- sort(unique(month_lookup$month_label))
monthly_C_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = n_draws_max, ncol = length(all_months),
                          dimnames = list(NULL, all_months))
monthly_E_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = n_draws_max, ncol = length(all_months),
                          dimnames = list(NULL, all_months))

for(cg in bss_catch_groups) {
  for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
    for(ss in subseasons) {
      label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_", cg)
      pe_label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
      b <- bss_all[[label]]

      days_ss <- prep_days_crab(ss$start, ss$end, params, L_eff_model = L_eff_model)
      days_ss$month_label <- format(days_ss$event_date, "%Y-%m")

      if(bss_use_pe_for(b)) {   # B1.8: PE if insufficient data OR failed scale-aware gate
        # B44 (2026-09-28): the PE's own strata, spread over their calendar days and summed
        # by month (pe_monthly_split.R). The months add up to the component totals exactly
        # and carry each cell's own CPUE; the effort-share split this replaced assumed one
        # CPUE for the whole sub-season and weighted months by their sampled days only.
        monthly_pe <- pe_monthly_split(pe_all[[pe_label]], days_ss, cg)

        for(m in monthly_pe$month_label) {
          if(m %in% all_months) {
            i_m <- monthly_pe$month_label == m
            monthly_C_draws[, m] <- monthly_C_draws[, m] + monthly_pe$month_catch[i_m]
            monthly_E_draws[, m] <- monthly_E_draws[, m] + monthly_pe$month_effort[i_m]
          }
        }
      } else {
        # Use C_expected (no Poisson noise) for monthly totals
        C_exp_bss <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "C_expected")$C_expected
        E_bss <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "E")$E
        n_fit_draws <- dim(C_exp_bss)[1]

        C_daily_mat <- C_exp_bss[,1,,1]
        E_daily_mat <- E_bss[,1,,1]

        for(m in unique(days_ss$month_label)) {
          day_idx <- which(days_ss$month_label == m)
          if(length(day_idx) == 0) next
          month_C <- if(length(day_idx)==1) C_daily_mat[, day_idx] else rowSums(C_daily_mat[, day_idx])
          month_E <- if(length(day_idx)==1) E_daily_mat[, day_idx] else rowSums(E_daily_mat[, day_idx])
          idx <- rep_len(1:n_fit_draws, n_draws_max)
          if(m %in% all_months) {
            monthly_C_draws[, m] <- monthly_C_draws[, m] + month_C[idx]
            monthly_E_draws[, m] <- monthly_E_draws[, m] + month_E[idx]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Add commercial/charter
if(!is.null(pe_all$comm_charter$daily_est)) {
  comm_daily <- pe_all$comm_charter$daily_est |>
    mutate(month_label = format(date, "%Y-%m"))
  comm_total <- pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept
  total_sampled_dung <- sum(comm_daily$est_dung)
  if(total_sampled_dung > 0) {
    for(m in unique(comm_daily$month_label)) {
      if(m %in% all_months) {
        share <- sum(comm_daily$est_dung[comm_daily$month_label == m]) / total_sampled_dung
        monthly_C_draws[, m] <- monthly_C_draws[, m] + comm_total * share
      }
    }
  }
}

monthly_summary <- tibble(
  Month = all_months,
  BSS_Catch_median = apply(monthly_C_draws, 2, median),
  BSS_Catch_lo95   = apply(monthly_C_draws, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  BSS_Catch_hi95   = apply(monthly_C_draws, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  BSS_Effort_median = apply(monthly_E_draws, 2, median),
  BSS_Effort_lo95   = apply(monthly_E_draws, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  BSS_Effort_hi95   = apply(monthly_E_draws, 2, quantile, 0.975)
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round))

print(monthly_summary |> select(Month, BSS_Catch_median, BSS_Catch_lo95, BSS_Catch_hi95))
write.csv(monthly_summary, file.path(output_dir, "monthly_estimates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p_monthly <- monthly_summary |>
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = all_months)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = BSS_Catch_median), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = BSS_Catch_lo95, ymax = BSS_Catch_hi95), width = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Dungeness catch (expected catch, median and 95% interval)",
       x = "Month", y = "Dungeness crab kept") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_monthly_catch.png"), p_monthly, width = 12, height = 6)


# ===========================================================================
```

```{r monthly-show, echo=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.cap='Monthly Dungeness catch with 95% intervals.'}
report_table(dplyr::transmute(monthly_summary, Month, Catch = BSS_Catch_median, `Catch 95% interval` = fmt_ci(BSS_Catch_median, BSS_Catch_lo95, BSS_Catch_hi95),
                              Effort = BSS_Effort_median, `Effort 95% interval` = fmt_ci(BSS_Effort_median, BSS_Effort_lo95, BSS_Effort_hi95)),
             digits = 0, caption = 'Monthly estimates: expected catch and effort (gear deployments) with 95% intervals.')
if (exists('p_monthly')) print(p_monthly)

### 8.1 Monthly catch by crabbing mode

The monthly trajectory by mode. Each fitted component contributes its posterior where it passed the gate; a component on PE contributes its PE point with a design-based effort SE, which omits the catch-rate uncertainty, so its interval here is a lower bound. The commercial/charter panel carries a per-vessel catch CV. This panel's census uncertainty is therefore not the one the port total carries (the charter expansion SE); the two agree on the medians.

```{r monthly-mode, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# 7.8b MONTHLY ESTIMATES BY CRABBING MODE (with per-mode uncertainty)
# ===========================================================================
# Companion to plot_monthly_catch.png. Breaks the monthly Dungeness catch out by
# crabbing mode, each month with a 95% interval. The uncertainty source matches
# the method actually selected for each component (convergence_report / pe_vs_bss):
#   Shore  (BSS, both sub-seasons): full posterior. Monthly catch draws are summed
#          from the daily C_expected draws, then 2.5/50/97.5 quantiles.
#   Private Boat: method is per sub-season (v7.0 scale-aware gate, B1.8). On the
#          method-of-record data every fit passes the gate and uses its BSS posterior
#          (full daily C_expected draws). A component on PE instead spreads its PE
#          point over months from its own strata (pe_monthly_split.R, B44), then
#          applies a design-based relative SE (stratified effort
#          SE / effort total) as ONE per-component lognormal scale shared across
#          months, so the monthly catches move together and the boat total carries
#          that relative SE. NOTE: the PE branch captures effort sampling
#          uncertainty but NOT CPUE sampling uncertainty, so a PE sub-season's
#          interval is a lower bound; the BSS posterior is the fuller
#          characterization. Branch selection is driven by bss_use_pe_for(), so if a
#          component's gate verdict changes in a future run this block follows it
#          automatically.
#   Commercial/Charter (census): point distributed by sampled-harvest share with
#          a catch-per-vessel sampling CV as the relative SE (small, high coverage).
# The PE branch splits the component by month from the PE's own strata
# (pe_monthly_split.R, B44), the same helper 7.8 uses, so the two blocks cannot drift.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n MONTHLY ESTIMATES BY MODE\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

modes_lvl <- c("Shore", "Private Boat", "Commercial/Charter")
mk_mat <- function() matrix(0, nrow = n_draws_max, ncol = length(all_months),
                            dimnames = list(NULL, all_months))
bymode_C <- setNames(lapply(modes_lvl, function(x) mk_mat()), modes_lvl)

# lognormal scale, mean 1, target relative SE (mean-preserving)
# B46 (2026-09-28): each call draws under its own seed (bss_seed + the call's index) with the
# caller's RNG restored. It used to draw from whatever state the port-total chunk's set.seed()
# had left, so it was reproducible only by accident, and not at all under census_uncertainty = "none".
.rln_k <- 0L
rln_scale <- function(n, rel_se) {
  .rln_k <<- .rln_k + 1L
  rel_se <- max(rel_se, 1e-4)
  sdlog  <- sqrt(log(1 + rel_se^2))
  bss_with_seed((params$bss_seed %||% 1L) + .rln_k, exp(stats::rnorm(n, -sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog)))
}

for(cg in bss_catch_groups) {
  for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
    mode_nm <- if(pop == "shore") "Shore" else "Private Boat"
    for(ss in subseasons) {
      label    <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_", cg)
      pe_label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
      b <- bss_all[[label]]

      days_ss <- prep_days_crab(ss$start, ss$end, params, L_eff_model = L_eff_model)
      days_ss$month_label <- format(days_ss$event_date, "%Y-%m")

      if(bss_use_pe_for(b)) {   # B1.8: PE if insufficient data OR failed scale-aware gate
        # B44 (2026-09-28): the PE's own strata by month (pe_monthly_split.R), as in 7.8.
        monthly_pe <- pe_monthly_split(pe_all[[pe_label]], days_ss, cg)

        eff_total <- pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_total %||% NA_real_
        eff_se    <- pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_se %||% NA_real_
        rel_se <- if(!is.na(eff_total) && eff_total > 0 && !is.na(eff_se) && eff_se > 0)
                    eff_se / eff_total else {
                      bss_warn("monthly", sprintf("%s: no PE effort SE; the by-mode monthly panel uses a relative SE of 0.30.", pe_label), severity = "note"); 0.30 }
        scale_draws <- rln_scale(n_draws_max, rel_se)   # common effort-level uncertainty

        for(m in monthly_pe$month_label) {
          if(m %in% all_months) {
            bymode_C[[mode_nm]][, m] <- bymode_C[[mode_nm]][, m] +
              monthly_pe$month_catch[monthly_pe$month_label == m] * scale_draws
          }
        }
      } else {
        C_exp_bss   <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "C_expected")$C_expected
        n_fit_draws <- dim(C_exp_bss)[1]
        C_daily_mat <- C_exp_bss[,1,,1]
        for(m in unique(days_ss$month_label)) {
          day_idx <- which(days_ss$month_label == m)
          if(length(day_idx) == 0 || !(m %in% all_months)) next
          month_C <- if(length(day_idx)==1) C_daily_mat[, day_idx] else rowSums(C_daily_mat[, day_idx])
          idx <- rep_len(1:n_fit_draws, n_draws_max)
          bymode_C[[mode_nm]][, m] <- bymode_C[[mode_nm]][, m] + month_C[idx]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Commercial/charter (census): distribute by sampled-harvest share, with a
# catch-per-vessel sampling CV as the relative SE (robust fallback if unavailable).
if(!is.null(pe_all$comm_charter$daily_est)) {
  comm_daily    <- pe_all$comm_charter$daily_est |> mutate(month_label = format(date, "%Y-%m"))
  comm_total    <- pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0
  total_sampled <- sum(comm_daily$est_dung)
  rel_se_comm <- tryCatch({
    cpv <- dwg$interview |> filter(population == "comm_charter") |> pull(dungeness_kept)
    cpv <- cpv[is.finite(cpv)]
    if(length(cpv) > 1 && mean(cpv) > 0) (sd(cpv) / sqrt(length(cpv))) / mean(cpv) else 0.12
  }, error = function(e) { bss_warn("monthly", "Commercial/charter per-vessel CV not computed; 0.12 used in the by-mode monthly panel.", severity = "note"); 0.12 })
  scale_comm <- rln_scale(n_draws_max, rel_se_comm)
  if(total_sampled > 0) {
    for(m in unique(comm_daily$month_label)) {
      if(m %in% all_months) {
        sh <- sum(comm_daily$est_dung[comm_daily$month_label == m]) / total_sampled
        bymode_C[["Commercial/Charter"]][, m] <- bymode_C[["Commercial/Charter"]][, m] + (comm_total * sh) * scale_comm
      }
    }
  }
}

monthly_bymode <- purrr::map_dfr(modes_lvl, function(md) {
  M <- bymode_C[[md]]
  tibble(
    Mode   = md,
    Month  = all_months,
    median = apply(M, 2, median),
    lo95   = apply(M, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
    hi95   = apply(M, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
  )
}) |>
  mutate(Mode  = factor(Mode, levels = modes_lvl),
         Month = factor(Month, levels = all_months),
         across(c(median, lo95, hi95), round))

print(monthly_bymode, n = nrow(monthly_bymode))
write.csv(monthly_bymode, file.path(output_dir, "monthly_estimates_by_mode.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

mode_cols <- c("Shore" = "#2c7fb8", "Private Boat" = "#d95f0e", "Commercial/Charter" = "#31a354")

# (1) Grouped (dodged) bars, one colour per mode, with 95% interval error bars.
p_bymode_dodge <- monthly_bymode |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = median, fill = Mode)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Dungeness Catch by Crabbing Mode",
       subtitle = "Median and 95% interval: BSS where the fit passed the gate, else the PE point with its effort SE;\ncommercial/charter with a per-vessel catch CV",
       x = "Month", y = "Dungeness crab caught", fill = "Mode") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top")
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_monthly_catch_by_mode.png"), p_bymode_dodge, width = 13, height = 6)

# (2) Faceted companion (free y) so shore and commercial panels stay readable
# next to the larger boat panel.
p_bymode_facet <- monthly_bymode |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = median, fill = Mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), width = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols) +
  facet_wrap(~Mode, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Monthly Dungeness Catch by Crabbing Mode",
       subtitle = "Median with 95% interval (free y-axis per panel)",
       x = "Month", y = "Dungeness crab caught") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_monthly_catch_by_mode_facet.png"), p_bymode_facet, width = 12, height = 9)


# ===========================================================================
```

if (exists('p_bymode_facet')) print(p_bymode_facet + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma))

## 9. Catch by crabbing mode

The total by crabbing mode, from the same draws as the port total: each mode sums its fitted components' posterior draws (or PE points where a fit fell back), so the intervals are joint over the mode's sub-seasons. The PE column is the design-based estimate for comparison. (Until 2026-09-29 this table showed the PE alone, which contradicted the headline.)

```{r catch-mode, results='hide'}
# 7.9 CATCH BY CRABBING MODE
# ===========================================================================

cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n CATCH BY CRABBING MODE\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

.mode_draws <- function(pop) {
  tot <- rep(0, n_draws_max)
  for (ss in subseasons) {
    b <- bss_all[[paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_Dungeness_Kept")]]
    tot <- tot + if (bss_use_pe_for(b)) (pe_all[[paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)]]$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0)
                 else b$C_exp_draws[rep_len(seq_along(b$C_exp_draws), n_draws_max)]
  }
  tot
}
.md <- list(shore = .mode_draws("shore"), boat = .mode_draws("private_boat"), cc = .cc_draws_by_cg[["Dungeness_Kept"]], port = port_C_draws)
.q <- function(x, p) as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, p))
mode_table <- tibble(
  Mode = c("Shore (Dock/Jetty/Beach)", "Private Boat", "Commercial/Charter", "PORT TOTAL"),
  BSS_median = vapply(.md, .q, numeric(1), p = 0.5),
  BSS_lo95   = vapply(.md, .q, numeric(1), p = 0.025),
  BSS_hi95   = vapply(.md, .q, numeric(1), p = 0.975),
  PE_Catch = c(
    pe_pop_sum("shore", "Dungeness_Kept"),
    pe_pop_sum("private_boat", "Dungeness_Kept"),
    pe_field("comm_charter", "Dungeness_Kept"), NA
  ),
  PE_Effort = c(
    pe_pop_sum("shore", "effort_total"),
    pe_pop_sum("private_boat", "effort_total"),
    pe_field("comm_charter", "effort_total"), NA
  )
)
mode_table$PE_Catch[4] <- sum(mode_table$PE_Catch[1:3], na.rm = TRUE)
mode_table$PE_Effort[4] <- sum(mode_table$PE_Effort[1:3], na.rm = TRUE)
print(mode_table |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round)))
write.csv(mode_table, file.path(output_dir, "catch_by_mode.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


# ===========================================================================
```

```{r catch-mode-show, echo=FALSE}
report_table(dplyr::transmute(mode_table, Mode, Catch = round(BSS_median), `95% interval` = fmt_ci(BSS_median, BSS_lo95, BSS_hi95),
                              `Share of port median` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * BSS_median / BSS_median[Mode == "PORT TOTAL"]),
                              `PE catch` = round(PE_Catch)),
             digits = 0, caption = "Season catch by crabbing mode (expected catch; BSS draws where the gate passed). Medians do not add to the port median.")
