### 9.1 Catch by gear type

In the pooled model the gear-type catch is an allocation after estimation: each population and sub-season's total draws are split by the gear catch shares in that sub-season's interviews, drawn by a **trip-level bootstrap** (crab arrive in trips, so the trip is the sampling unit; review item 6, 2026-09-08). Each gear therefore carries both sources of uncertainty. It is an apportionment of the pooled total, not a per-gear catch-rate model; commercial/charter catch is all pot by construction. The share intervals are in `gear_shares_bootstrap.csv`.

```{r catch-gear, results='hide', fig.show='hide'}
# 7.10 CATCH BY GEAR TYPE (trip-level bootstrap shares x component total draws)
#
# Pooled model: the gear split is an apportionment of each component's catch by the
# catch shares observed in that component's interviews. REVIEW ITEM 6 (2026-09-08)
# replaced two things at once:
#   (1) Dirichlet(catch counts + 0.5) -> a nonparametric TRIP-level bootstrap of the
#       shares. The Dirichlet treated every crab as an independent multinomial draw; crab
#       arrive in trips (one pot boat lands 25), so the effective sample size is the number
#       of trips and the old intervals were several times too narrow.
#   (2) one season-wide share vector per population -> shares PER population x sub-season,
#       applied to that sub-season's own total draws. The old pooling attributed "Pot" catch
#       to the pot-closure period, where pots are illegal.
# The helper lives in 03_R_functions/gear_share_bootstrap.R. Comm/charter is all Pot by
# construction (census). tryCatch falls back to a point allocation if a draw object is
# unavailable, so the section can never break the knit.
# ===========================================================================

cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n CATCH BY GEAR TYPE (bootstrap shares x totals)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

gear_levels <- gear_primary_levels

gear_int <- dwg$interview |>
  filter(population %in% c("shore","private_boat")) |>
  mutate(gear_primary = gear_primary_class(gear_type),
         catch = as.numeric(dungeness_kept))

# Observed (point) shares per population x sub-season, for the report and the fallback.
gear_props <- bind_rows(lapply(subseasons, function(ss) {
  gear_int |>
    filter(between(event_date, ss$start, ss$end)) |>
    group_by(population, gear_primary) |>
    summarise(total_catch = sum(catch, na.rm = TRUE), n_int = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(population) |>
    mutate(prop_catch = if (sum(total_catch) > 0) total_catch / sum(total_catch) else NA_real_,
           subseason = ss$name) |>
    ungroup()
}))
cat("\n  Observed catch proportions by gear type (per sub-season):\n")
print(gear_props |> select(subseason, population, gear_primary, n_int, total_catch, prop_catch) |>
        mutate(prop_catch = round(prop_catch, 3)))

total_shore_catch <- pe_pop_sum("shore", "Dungeness_Kept")
total_boat_catch  <- pe_pop_sum("private_boat", "Dungeness_Kept")

# One component's total draws: its BSS expected-catch draws where the gate passed, the PE
# point otherwise (recycled to n_target so the bootstrap shares can multiply it).
gear_component_total_draws <- function(pop, ss_name, n_target) {
  lab <- paste0(pop, "_", ss_name, "_Dungeness_Kept")
  b   <- bss_all[[lab]]
  if (!is.null(b) && !bss_use_pe_for(b) && !is.null(b$C_exp_draws)) {
    d <- as.numeric(b$C_exp_draws)
    if (length(d) >= n_target) d[seq_len(n_target)] else bss_with_seed(params$bss_seed %||% 1L, sample(d, n_target, replace = TRUE))
  } else {
    rep(pe_all[[paste0(pop, "_", ss_name)]]$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0, n_target)
  }
}

gear_summary <- tryCatch({
  n_gd <- 4000
  per_gear <- matrix(0, n_gd, length(gear_levels), dimnames = list(NULL, gear_levels))
  gear_share_detail <- list()
  for (pop in c("shore", "private_boat")) {
    for (ss in subseasons) {
      iv <- gear_int |> filter(population == pop, between(event_date, ss$start, ss$end))
      shares <- gear_share_bootstrap(iv, n_boot = n_gd, levels = gear_levels,
                                     seed = params$bss_seed + match(pop, c("shore","private_boat")) * 1000 +
                                            match(ss$name, vapply(subseasons, `[[`, "", "name")))
      # A sub-season whose interviews carry no catch at all (or none) has undefined shares;
      # fall back to the population's season-wide point shares, and say so.
      if (all(is.na(shares))) {
        fb <- gear_share_point(gear_int |> filter(population == pop), gear_levels)
        if (all(is.na(fb))) fb <- setNames(c(1, 0, 0, 0, 0), gear_levels)
        shares <- matrix(fb, n_gd, length(gear_levels), byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, gear_levels))
        bss_warn("gear split", sprintf("%s / %s has no catch-bearing interviews; its gear split uses the population's season-wide point shares.", pop, ss$name), severity = "note")
      } else if (anyNA(shares)) {
        # a rare replicate with zero total catch: replace it by the point shares
        pt <- gear_share_point(iv, gear_levels)
        shares[is.na(shares[, 1]), ] <- matrix(pt, sum(is.na(shares[, 1])), length(gear_levels), byrow = TRUE)
      }
      tot <- gear_component_total_draws(pop, ss$name, n_gd)
      per_gear <- per_gear + shares * tot
      gear_share_detail[[paste(pop, ss$name)]] <- tibble(
        population = pop, subseason = ss$name, n_interviews = nrow(iv),
        gear_primary = gear_levels,
        share_median = apply(shares, 2, median),
        share_lo95   = apply(shares, 2, quantile, 0.025),
        share_hi95   = apply(shares, 2, quantile, 0.975))
    }
  }
  per_gear[, "Pot"] <- per_gear[, "Pot"] + (pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0)
  write.csv(bind_rows(gear_share_detail), file.path(output_dir, "gear_shares_bootstrap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  tibble(
    gear_primary = gear_levels,
    Catch_median = round(apply(per_gear, 2, median)),
    lo95     = round(apply(per_gear, 2, quantile, 0.025)),
    hi95     = round(apply(per_gear, 2, quantile, 0.975))
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Proportion = round(Catch_median / sum(Catch_median), 3)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Catch_median))
}, error = function(e) {
  bss_warn("gear split", sprintf("Gear bootstrap propagation failed (%s); the gear table is a point allocation with no intervals.", conditionMessage(e)))
  ge <- gear_props |>
    group_by(population, gear_primary) |>
    summarise(total_catch = sum(total_catch), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(population) |> mutate(prop_catch = total_catch / sum(total_catch)) |> ungroup() |>
    mutate(pop_total = dplyr::case_when(population == "shore" ~ total_shore_catch,
                                        population == "private_boat" ~ total_boat_catch),
           est_catch = round(pop_total * prop_catch)) |>
    dplyr::select(gear_primary, est_catch)
  ge <- bind_rows(ge, tibble(gear_primary = "Pot",
                             est_catch = round(pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0)))
  ge |> group_by(gear_primary) |>
    summarise(Catch_median = sum(est_catch), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(lo95 = NA_real_, hi95 = NA_real_, Proportion = round(Catch_median / sum(Catch_median), 3)) |>
    arrange(desc(Catch_median))
})

cat("\n--- Catch by Gear Type (trip-level bootstrap shares x component totals) ---\n")
print(gear_summary)
write.csv(gear_summary, file.path(output_dir, "catch_by_gear_type.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p_gear <- gear_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(Catch_median > 0 | !is.na(hi95) & hi95 > 0) |>
  mutate(gear_primary = fct_reorder(gear_primary, Catch_median),
         label_y = pmax(hi95, Catch_median, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gear_primary, y = Catch_median)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), width = 0.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  # labels sit PAST the interval, so they no longer print over the whiskers (2026-09-29)
  geom_text(aes(y = label_y, label = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", format(Catch_median, big.mark = ","), Proportion * 100)),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(title = "Dungeness catch by gear type", subtitle = "Trip-level bootstrap gear shares x component total draws; median and 95% interval",
       x = NULL, y = "Dungeness crab kept") +
  theme_bw() + coord_flip()
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "plot_catch_by_gear_type.png"), p_gear, width = 10, height = 6)


```

## 11. Model diagnostics

The gate says whether the sampler worked; this section says whether the model carries the data. **Posterior-predictive calibration** (below) compares each observation with its predictive distribution: coverage near nominal and PIT histograms that are flat mean a calibrated stream; a hump means the predictive is too wide, a U too narrow. **Model adequacy** (11.5) summarises the flags per fit, **prior influence** (11.6) lists the parameters whose posterior is essentially the prior, and the **block cross-validation** (11.7) scores each effort stream on whole held-out weeks, the interpolation the model is actually used for.

```{r diag-perfit, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.12 PER-FIT MODEL DIAGNOSTICS (B1.6) ----
# Additive per-fit diagnostics: structural parameters, divergence localization,
# and posterior predictive calibration. write_bss_diagnostics() is sourced from
# 03_R_functions/model_diagnostics.R and is fully tryCatch-wrapped, so a diagnostic
# failure prints a note and never interrupts the run. Storing bss_data with each
# fit (Section 7) is what enables the PPC; without it the PPC is skipped cleanly.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n MODEL DIAGNOSTICS\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[label]]
  if(is.null(b$fit)) next                  # PE-only entry: nothing to diagnose
  cat(sprintf("  %s:\n", label))
  # 2026-08-30: the gate verdict travels INTO the per-fit tables, so a parameter row lifted
  # out of a rejected fit's file carries that fact with it.
  write_bss_diagnostics(b$fit,
                        if(!is.null(b$bss_data)) b$bss_data else NULL,
                        label, output_dir,
                        fit_method = b$gate_info$method_selected %||%
                          (if (isTRUE(b$use_bss)) "BSS" else "PE (convergence fail)"))
  # 2026-09-04: persist the draws the PPC is computed from. Three separate defects in the
  # diagnostic arithmetic have each cost a full multi-hour re-fit to correct, most recently
  # the ZINB catch stream being scored as NB2. See 03_R_functions/save_bss_ppc_draws.R.
  if (isTRUE(params$save_ppc_draws) && !is.null(b$bss_data))
    save_bss_ppc_draws(b$fit, b$bss_data, label, output_dir,
                       max_draws = params$save_ppc_draws_max %||% NULL)
}


```

```{r diag-perfit-show, echo=FALSE}
# Surface the posterior-predictive calibration written above so the health check is on
# the page, not only in ppc_calibration_<fit>.csv. Healthy: 95% coverage near 0.95 and
# PIT mean near 0.50; a coverage far from nominal or a PIT far from 0.50 flags a
# mis-calibrated (usually over-dispersed) predictive for that data stream.
ppc <- read_fit_outputs("ppc_calibration")
ppc_disp <- if (!is.null(ppc)) tryCatch(
  dplyr::transmute(ppc,
    Fit         = fit_lbl,
    Stream      = data_type,
    `Cover 50%` = round(coverage_50, 2),
    `Cover 95%` = round(coverage_95, 2),
    `PIT mean`  = round(pit_mean, 2),
    `PIT sd`    = round(pit_sd, 2),
    n           = n_obs),
  error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
report_table(ppc_disp,
  paste("Posterior-predictive calibration by fit and data stream. Healthy: Cover 95%",
        "near 0.95 and PIT mean near 0.50; coverage well above nominal means the",
        "predictive is too wide (over-dispersed), the effort streams are the known case."))
```

```{r diag-pit-show, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}

  for (.f in .pits) cat(sprintf("![PIT histogram, %s](%s){width=100%%}\n\n",
                                short_fit(sub("^ppc_pit_(.*)\\.png$", "\\1", basename(.f))), .f))
}

### 11.1 Effort over-dispersion decomposition

Splits each effort-count predictive variance into its Poisson floor, negative-binomial observation over-dispersion, and latent-process parts, written per fit. It identifies which lever drives any excess effort variance before a prior or model change is considered.

```{r diag-overdisp, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.13 EFFORT OVER-DISPERSION DECOMPOSITION (T1.5) ----
# Additive per-fit diagnostic. The v7.0 PPC showed the negative-binomial
# effort model is over-dispersed (gear/trailer PIT central humps, coverage_50
# ~ 0.63-0.75 vs the nominal 0.50); that says the effort predictive is too
# wide but not which part of the model to tune. This decomposes each effort-
# count predictive variance, by the law of total variance, into its Poisson
# floor E[mu], the NB observation over-dispersion E[mu^2/r_E] (the r_E /
# sigma_r_E lever), and the latent process variance Var(mu) (the sigma_eps_E /
# single-cell level lever), and reports their shares so the lever is identified
# before any prior or model change. write_effort_overdispersion_diag() is
# sourced from 03_R_functions/diagnose_effort_overdispersion.R and is fully
# tryCatch-wrapped; it writes only CSVs (effort_overdispersion_decomp_<label>
# and ..._byobs_<label>) and changes nothing in the model. It needs the in-
# memory fit and its bss_data (stored with each fit in Section 7), which is why
# it runs here in the fit session rather than from the saved summary CSVs.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n EFFORT OVER-DISPERSION DECOMPOSITION (T1.5)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[label]]
  if(is.null(b$fit)) next                  # PE-only entry: nothing to decompose
  write_effort_overdispersion_diag(b$fit,
                                   if(!is.null(b$bss_data)) b$bss_data else NULL,
                                   label, output_dir)
}


```

```{r diag-overdisp-show, echo=FALSE}
# Surface the effort over-dispersion decomposition written above. Shares sum to 1 and
# name the lever for any excess effort variance: the Poisson floor, NB observation
# over-dispersion (r_E / sigma_r_E), or latent AR-process variance (sigma_eps_E).
od <- read_fit_outputs("effort_overdispersion_decomp")
od_disp <- if (!is.null(od)) tryCatch(
  dplyr::transmute(od,
    Fit           = fit_lbl,
    Stream        = data_type,
    Poisson       = round(share_poisson, 2),
    `NB overdisp` = round(share_nb_overdisp, 2),
    `Latent AR`   = round(share_latent, 2),
    `Cover 50%`   = round(ppc_coverage_50, 2)),
  error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
report_table(od_disp,
  paste("Effort-count predictive variance decomposition (shares sum to 1): Poisson floor,",
        "negative-binomial observation over-dispersion, and latent AR-process variance.",
        "The dominant share is the lever to tune if the effort predictive is too wide."))
```

### 11.2 Extended per-fit outputs and PSIS-LOO

The extended output series (parameter posteriors, AR paths, coverage maps, PPC residuals, sampler diagnostics, prior-vs-posterior tables) and PSIS-LOO cross-validation are written to the run folder for later analysis; nothing here changes an estimate.

```{r diag-extended, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.13b EXTENDED RUN OUTPUTS (O1-O11) ----
# Additive persistence of in-memory quantities not previously saved, so the R
# workspace is rarely needed for later diagnosis. Per-fit (O1-O6, O8, O9): full
# parameter posterior summary, AR latent path, AR-period data coverage, modeled
# daily CPUE, per-observation PPC residuals (exact randomized PIT), HMC sampler
# diagnostics (E-BFMI), summed-quantity draws, prior-vs-posterior. Run-level (O7,
# O10, O11): monthly PE-vs-BSS by mode, gear proportions, per-fit data summary.
# Sourced from 03_R_functions/save_run_diagnostics.R; every writer is tryCatch-
# wrapped and writes only CSVs, so this changes no estimate. The fit objects
# (O12) are deliberately not saved, to avoid output/ bloat.
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n EXTENDED RUN OUTPUTS (O1-O11)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[label]]
  if(is.null(b$fit)) next                  # PE-only entry: nothing to extract
  # 2026-08-27: pass the run seed so the diagnostic draw subsampling is reproducible
  # (see the note in save_run_diagnostics.R; the port total stays RNG-sensitive regardless).
  write_fit_extended_diagnostics(b$fit, b$bss_data, b$days_ss, label, output_dir,
                                 seed = params$bss_seed %||% 1L)
  write_loo_diagnostics(b$fit, b$bss_data, b$days_ss, label, output_dir)
  # 2026-09-26 (D31 -> B39): leave-one-WEEK-out PSIS block CV of the effort streams, the
  # interpolation test pointwise LOO cannot make. Writes loo_block_<stream>_<label>.csv;
  # tryCatch-wrapped per stream; changes no estimate (03_R_functions/bss_block_cv.R).
  write_block_cv_diagnostics(b$fit, b$bss_data, b$days_ss, label, output_dir)
  # POOL-5: CPUE estimator triad, saturation exponent, effort-linearity, and the
  # E/h unit assertion (03_R_functions/bss_cpue_diagnostics.R). Diagnostic-only:
  # writes cpue_estimators_/cpue_saturation_/cpue_linearity_<label>.csv and changes
  # no estimate. This is the check that surfaces a boat/shore effort-unit defect
  # (e.g. catch flat in soak time) the same way it did for gear-resolved. Wrapped
  # so a diagnostic error (or the unit assertion) can never abort the run.
  tryCatch(write_cpue_diagnostics(b, label, output_dir),
           error = function(e)
             cat(sprintf("  CPUE diagnostics skipped for %s: %s\n", label, conditionMessage(e))))
}
write_run_level_diagnostics(bss_all, pe_all,
                            if(exists("gear_props")) gear_props else NULL,
                            params, output_dir)
# improvement-plan item 5.5 (2026-08-30): model ADEQUACY, reported beside the convergence
# gate rather than folded into it. The gate asks whether the sampler worked; this asks
# whether the model is carrying the data. It changes no selection. Runs after the per-fit
# LOO and PPC writers because it reads their output.
write_model_adequacy(bss_all, output_dir, params)


```

```{r diag-extended-show, echo=FALSE}
# CPUE effort-unit validity, per-fit data coverage, and PSIS-LOO, read back from the
# CSVs written above so the key diagnostics render on the page instead of only on disk.

# (a) CPUE estimator triad + linearity + saturation: is the effort unit harvest-valid?
.est <- read_fit_outputs("cpue_estimators")
.lin <- read_fit_outputs("cpue_linearity")
.sat <- read_fit_outputs("cpue_saturation")
cpue_disp <- if (!is.null(.est)) tryCatch({
  d <- dplyr::select(.est, fit_lbl, effort_unit, n_obs, cpue_ratio_of_sums, cpue_model_implied)
  if (!is.null(.lin)) d <- dplyr::left_join(d, dplyr::select(.lin, fit_lbl, beta_h, linearity_flag), by = "fit_lbl")
  if (!is.null(.sat)) d <- dplyr::left_join(d, dplyr::select(.sat, fit_lbl, sat_beta = beta, saturation_flag), by = "fit_lbl")
  dplyr::transmute(d,
    Fit          = fit_lbl,
    Unit         = effort_unit,
    n            = n_obs,
    `CPUE RoS`   = round(cpue_ratio_of_sums, 2),
    `CPUE model` = round(cpue_model_implied, 2),
    beta_h       = round(beta_h, 2),
    `linear?`    = dplyr::if_else(linearity_flag, "FLAG", "ok", missing = "-"),
    `sat beta`   = round(sat_beta, 2),
    `sat?`       = dplyr::if_else(saturation_flag, "FLAG", "ok", missing = "-"))
}, error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
report_table(cpue_disp,
  paste("CPUE effort-unit validity. beta_h is the catch-vs-effort elasticity (harvest-",
        "unbiased when it covers 1, shown as 'linear? = ok'); the model CPUE should track",
        "the design-based ratio-of-sums (RoS). 'sat? = FLAG' (catch sub-linear in soak",
        "time) is expected for pots and is the reason the unit is deployments, not hours."))

# (b) Per-fit data coverage: how much the BSS must lean on the process model.
.fds <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "fit_data_summary.csv"),
                                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
fds_disp <- if (!is.null(.fds)) tryCatch(
  dplyr::transmute(.fds,
    Fit          = short_fit(fit),
    Method       = method,
    AR           = ar_resolution,
    Days         = D,
    `Eff obs`    = n_effort_obs,
    Interviews   = n_interviews,
    `I/E obs`    = n_ie_obs,
    `% days eff` = round(pct_days_with_effort, 0),
    `% days int` = round(pct_days_with_interview, 0)),
  error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
report_table(fds_disp,
  paste("Per-fit data coverage: latent days, effort observations, interviews, and I/E",
        "observations, with the percent of days carrying any effort/interview data. Thin",
        "coverage is where the BSS leans hardest on the AR process and priors."))

# (c) PSIS-LOO by stream: predictive fit and reliability (Pareto k).
.loo <- read_fit_outputs("loo_summary")
loo_disp <- if (!is.null(.loo)) tryCatch(
  dplyr::transmute(.loo,
    Fit             = fit_lbl,
    Stream          = stream,
    n               = n_obs,
    elpd_loo        = round(elpd_loo, 1),
    p_loo           = round(p_loo, 1),
    `Pareto k>0.7`  = `n_pareto_k_gt_0.7`),
  error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
report_table(loo_disp,
  paste("PSIS-LOO by data stream. p_loo is the effective number of parameters; a large",
        "'Pareto k>0.7' count means LOO is unreliable for that stream (the model is near-",
        "saturated there), so read its elpd_loo with caution."))
```

### 11.3 Divergence localization

Where the divergent transitions (if any) concentrate. **Healthy:** small `|SMD|` across the board, meaning divergences are diffuse and not biasing any particular parameter or total.

```{r divergence-diagnostics-show, echo=FALSE}
# Surface the top divergence-localization drivers written by the per-fit diagnostics.
# Large |SMD| (standardized median difference between divergent and bulk draws) points
# at the parameter/geometry the divergences concentrate in (e.g. a hierarchical funnel).
dl <- read_fit_outputs("divergence_localization")
# A parameter that enters no likelihood in a fit (decoupled: sigma_mu_E once A31 collapses a
# single-section level, R_G_boat in a shore fit) samples its prior, so where its divergent
# draws sit says nothing about the fit's geometry; it is listed in 11.6 and left out here.
.decoupled <- tryCatch({
  .sp <- read_fit_outputs("structural_params")
  if (!is.null(.sp) && "decoupled" %in% names(.sp))
    dplyr::transmute(dplyr::filter(.sp, as.logical(decoupled) %in% TRUE), fit_lbl, param = sub("\\[.*$", "", parameter))
  else NULL }, error = function(e) NULL)
dl_disp <- if (!is.null(dl) && "smd" %in% names(dl)) tryCatch(
  dl |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(smd)) |>
    (\(d) if (is.null(.decoupled)) d else dplyr::anti_join(dplyr::mutate(d, .p = sub("\\[.*$", "", param)),
                                                          dplyr::rename(.decoupled, .p = param), by = c("fit_lbl", ".p")))() |>
    dplyr::group_by(fit_lbl) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(abs(smd), n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::transmute(Fit = fit_lbl, Parameter = param, SMD = round(smd, 2),
                     `median (bulk)` = round(median_bulk, 2),
                     `median (div)`  = round(median_div, 2)),
  error = function(e) NULL) else NULL
report_table(dl_disp,
  paste("Top divergence-localization drivers per fit (largest |SMD|). A large |SMD| is",
        "where divergent draws depart most from the bulk; it names the geometry to watch.",
        "Small values across the board mean divergences are diffuse, not biasing a total.",
        "Prior-only parameters (Section 11.6) are left out."))
```






### 11.4 Summer-extrapolation transparency (T1.1)

How much of each fitted component's BSS catch falls on days with **no interview**, where the CPUE is imputed by the AR process and priors rather than observed. A high extrapolated share means that component's harvest rests on the model filling unsampled time; it is the transparency counterpart to the summer-dominance caveat, and the place to be most cautious about the headline number. The share is computed from summed daily medians, so read it as a coverage diagnostic, not a re-estimate of the total.

```{r extrapolation-transparency, echo=FALSE}
# T1.1: decompose each fit's BSS catch into interview-days vs extrapolated (no
# interview) days, from the persisted daily catch (bss_daily_catch_*) and daily CPUE
# (bss_daily_cpue_*, which carries n_interviews) outputs. A day is "extrapolated" when
# it has zero interviews, so its CPUE comes entirely from the AR process and priors.
# Diagnostic only; writes extrapolation_transparency.csv.
.dc <- read_fit_outputs("bss_daily_catch")
.dq <- read_fit_outputs("bss_daily_cpue")
extrap_tbl <- NULL
if (!is.null(.dc) && !is.null(.dq) && "n_interviews" %in% names(.dq)) {
  extrap_tbl <- tryCatch({
    dplyr::left_join(
      dplyr::transmute(.dc, fit_lbl, event_date = as.character(event_date), catch = .data[["median"]]),
      dplyr::transmute(.dq, fit_lbl, event_date = as.character(event_date), n_interviews),
      by = c("fit_lbl", "event_date")) |>
      dplyr::mutate(n_interviews = dplyr::coalesce(n_interviews, 0)) |>
      dplyr::group_by(Fit = fit_lbl) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        `days total`         = dplyr::n(),
        `days sampled`       = sum(n_interviews > 0),
        `catch total`        = round(sum(catch, na.rm = TRUE)),
        `catch extrapolated` = round(sum(catch[n_interviews == 0], na.rm = TRUE)),
        .groups = "drop") |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        `% days sampled`       = round(100 * `days sampled` / `days total`, 0),
        `% catch extrapolated` = round(100 * `catch extrapolated` / `catch total`, 1))
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}
if (!is.null(extrap_tbl) && nrow(extrap_tbl) > 0) {
  port_extrap_pct <- round(100 * sum(extrap_tbl$`catch extrapolated`) / sum(extrap_tbl$`catch total`), 1)
  utils::write.csv(extrap_tbl, file.path(output_dir, "extrapolation_transparency.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  report_table(extrap_tbl,
    paste0("Share of each fitted component's BSS catch on days with no interview (CPUE ",
           "imputed by the AR process). Across the fitted components, ", port_extrap_pct,
           "% of the summed BSS catch falls on extrapolated days. A high '% catch ",
           "extrapolated' flags a component whose harvest rests on the model filling ",
           "unsampled time; shares use summed daily medians, so read as a coverage ",
           "diagnostic, not a re-estimate of the total."))
} else {
  cat("_Extrapolation transparency unavailable (daily catch / CPUE outputs not found)._")
}
```

### 11.5 Model adequacy

Reported beside the gate, never gating it (`model_adequacy.csv`). **p_loo fraction**: the effective number of parameters as a share of the observations in the worst stream (high means the model is nearly memorising that stream). **Pareto k > 0.7**: observations whose leave-one-out estimate is unreliable. **PIT bias** and **coverage deviation**: how far the worst stream's predictive calibration is from nominal. The flags summarise these against the thresholds in `bss_model_adequacy.R`.

```{r adequacy-show, echo=FALSE}
.adq <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(file.path(output_dir, "model_adequacy.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(.adq) && nrow(.adq)) {
  .flags <- c(flag_overparameterised = "overparameterised", flag_loo_unreliable = "LOO unreliable", flag_pit_bias = "PIT bias",
              flag_miscalibrated = "miscalibrated", flag_dispersion_neff = "dispersion n_eff")
  .fl <- apply(.adq[, intersect(names(.flags), names(.adq)), drop = FALSE], 1, function(r) {
    f <- names(r)[as.logical(r) %in% TRUE]; if (length(f)) paste(.flags[f], collapse = ", ") else "none" })
  report_table(data.frame(check.names = FALSE, Fit = short_fit(.adq$fit),
                          `p_loo fraction (worst stream)` = sprintf("%.3f (%s)", .adq$p_loo_frac, .adq$p_loo_worst_stream),
                          `Pareto k > 0.7` = .adq$n_pareto_bad,
                          `PIT bias (worst)` = sprintf("%.3f (%s)", .adq$pit_worst_bias, .adq$pit_worst_stream),
                          `50% coverage deviation (worst)` = sprintf("%.3f (%s)", .adq$cov50_worst_dev, .adq$cov50_worst_stream),
                          Flags = .fl),
               caption = "Model adequacy per fit (model_adequacy.csv). A flag is a reason to read that fit's streams with care, not a gate failure.")
} else cat("_model_adequacy.csv was not written this run._")
```

### 11.6 Prior influence

Parameters whose posterior barely moved from the prior (`prior_influential` in `prior_vs_posterior_<fit>.csv`: contraction below the threshold in `save_run_diagnostics.R`), and parameters that enter no likelihood in a fit and so report their prior exactly (`decoupled` in `structural_params_<fit>.csv`). Neither is an estimate. A prior-influenced parameter that the total depends on (a turnover, for example) means that part of the total rests on the prior's centre.

```{r prior-influence-show, echo=FALSE}
.pvp <- read_fit_outputs("prior_vs_posterior")
.stp <- read_fit_outputs("structural_params")
.pi_tab <- NULL
if (!is.null(.pvp) && "prior_influential" %in% names(.pvp)) {
  .pi_tab <- .pvp |> dplyr::filter(prior_influential %in% TRUE) |> dplyr::group_by(Fit = fit_lbl) |>
    dplyr::summarise(`Prior-influenced (contraction)` = paste(sprintf("%s (%.2f)", parameter, contraction), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
}
if (!is.null(.stp) && "decoupled" %in% names(.stp)) {
  .dc <- .stp |> dplyr::filter(decoupled %in% TRUE) |> dplyr::group_by(Fit = fit_lbl) |>
    dplyr::summarise(`Prior only (enters no likelihood)` = paste(unique(sub("\\[.*$", "", parameter)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
  .pi_tab <- if (is.null(.pi_tab)) .dc else dplyr::full_join(.pi_tab, .dc, by = "Fit")
}
if (!is.null(.pi_tab) && nrow(.pi_tab)) {
  .pi_tab[is.na(.pi_tab)] <- "none"
  report_table(.pi_tab, caption = "Parameters that report (mostly) their prior, per fit. Contraction is 1 - posterior SD / prior SD.")
} else cat("_No prior-influenced or prior-only parameters were flagged._")
```

### 11.7 Leave-one-week-out cross-validation of the effort streams

Pointwise LOO scores single days, but the model's job is to fill whole unsampled stretches. The block cross-validation (`loo_block_<stream>_<fit>.csv`, B39) leaves out each week in turn and scores the effort stream there by PSIS. A low reliable share (Pareto k > 0.7 on many weeks) means the week-level score cannot be trusted for that stream; where it is reliable, the elpd per observation is comparable between runs on the same data.

```{r blockcv-show, echo=FALSE}
.bcv <- read_fit_outputs("loo_block")
if (!is.null(.bcv) && nrow(.bcv)) {
  # file names are loo_block_<stream>_<fit>.csv, so the label carries the stream as a prefix
  .bcv_s <- .bcv |> dplyr::mutate(Fit = sub("^(gear|trailer|osp|joint)_", "", fit_lbl)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(Fit, Stream = data_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(Weeks = dplyr::n(), Observations = sum(n_obs), `Reliable weeks` = sum(reliable %in% TRUE),
                     `elpd (sum)` = round(sum(elpd_block), 1), `elpd per obs` = round(sum(elpd_block) / max(sum(n_obs), 1), 3),
                     `worst Pareto k` = round(max(pareto_k, na.rm = TRUE), 2), .groups = "drop")
  report_table(.bcv_s, caption = "Leave-one-week-out PSIS cross-validation by fit and effort stream (the joint row leaves out every boat stream of the week together).")
} else cat("_No block cross-validation output this run._")
```

### 11.8 Sampler health

Per chain: divergent transitions, the mean and maximum tree depth, the step size and the energy Bayesian fraction of missing information (E-BFMI; below 0.3 means the sampler explored the tails poorly). Written to `sampler_diagnostics_<fit>.csv`.

```{r sampler-show, echo=FALSE}
.smp <- read_fit_outputs("sampler_diagnostics")
if (!is.null(.smp) && nrow(.smp))
  report_table(.smp |> dplyr::group_by(Fit = fit_lbl) |>
                 dplyr::summarise(Chains = dplyr::n(), Divergent = sum(divergent), `Mean treedepth` = round(mean(mean_treedepth), 1),
                                  `Max treedepth` = max(max_treedepth), `Mean step size` = signif(mean(mean_stepsize), 2),
                                  `Min E-BFMI` = round(min(ebfmi, na.rm = TRUE), 2), `Low E-BFMI chains` = sum(ebfmi_low_flag %in% TRUE),
                                  .groups = "drop"),
               caption = "Sampler health per fit, over its chains.")
```

## 12. Effort and CPUE multipliers

The fitted day-type effects: how much more effort and how much higher a catch rate a weekend or holiday carries than a weekday, as multipliers with 95% intervals.

```{r multipliers, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.14 EFFORT & CPUE MULTIPLIERS ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n EFFORT & CPUE MULTIPLIERS\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

multiplier_results <- list()
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[label]]
  if(is.null(b$pe_fallback) || !b$pe_fallback) {
    B1_draws <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "B1")$B1
    B2_draws <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "B2")$B2
    B1C_draws <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "B1_C_out")$B1_C_out

    weekend_eff_mult <- exp(B1_draws)
    holiday_eff_mult <- exp(B1_draws + B2_draws)
    weekend_cpue_mult <- exp(B1C_draws)

    multiplier_results[[label]] <- tibble(
      fit = label,
      weekend_effort_mult = sprintf("%.2fx (%.2f-%.2f)",
        median(weekend_eff_mult), quantile(weekend_eff_mult, 0.025), quantile(weekend_eff_mult, 0.975)),
      holiday_effort_mult = sprintf("%.2fx (%.2f-%.2f)",
        median(holiday_eff_mult), quantile(holiday_eff_mult, 0.025), quantile(holiday_eff_mult, 0.975)),
      weekend_cpue_mult = sprintf("%.2fx (%.2f-%.2f)",
        median(weekend_cpue_mult), quantile(weekend_cpue_mult, 0.025), quantile(weekend_cpue_mult, 0.975)),
      B1_C_median = round(median(B1C_draws), 3),
      B1_C_lo95 = round(quantile(B1C_draws, 0.025), 3),
      B1_C_hi95 = round(quantile(B1C_draws, 0.975), 3)
    )
  }
}
if(length(multiplier_results) > 0) {
  multiplier_df <- bind_rows(multiplier_results)
  cat("\n  Multipliers relative to weekdays:\n")
  for(i in 1:nrow(multiplier_df)) {
    cat(sprintf("    %s:\n      Weekend effort: %s\n      Holiday effort: %s\n      Weekend CPUE: %s\n",
                multiplier_df$fit[i],
                multiplier_df$weekend_effort_mult[i],
                multiplier_df$holiday_effort_mult[i],
                multiplier_df$weekend_cpue_mult[i]))
  }
  write.csv(multiplier_df, file.path(output_dir, "effort_cpue_multipliers.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}


```

```{r multipliers-show, echo=FALSE}
if (exists('multiplier_df')) report_table(dplyr::transmute(multiplier_df, Fit = short_fit(fit), `Weekend effort` = weekend_effort_mult,
                                                           `Holiday effort` = holiday_effort_mult, `Weekend catch rate` = weekend_cpue_mult),
                                          caption = 'Fitted multipliers relative to a weekday: median (95% interval).')
```

### 12.1 Expansion ratios (R_G and R_G_boat)

The gear-per-crabber ratio `R_G` (learned from the shore interviews) and the gear-per-boat-group ratio `R_G_boat` (learned from the boat interviews) that carry the counts onto the gear-deployment scale. Each ratio is declared in every fit but informed only in its own population's fits; in the other it reports its prior and is marked PRIOR ONLY. The `R_G` prior centre is the season's interview ratio unless `R_G_prior_mu` overrides it (the sensitivity sweep is `06_diagnostics/run_rg_sweep.R`).

```{r expansion, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.16 R_G AND R_G_boat POSTERIORS ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n EXPANSION RATIOS (R_G, R_G_boat)\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

expansion_results <- list()
for(label in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[label]]
  if(is.null(b$pe_fallback) || !b$pe_fallback) {
    R_G_draws      <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "R_G")$R_G
    # POOL-1: R_T replaced by R_G_boat (gear per boat group). Both are always-present
    # parameters now; in the population where a ratio is unused it samples its prior.
    R_G_boat_draws <- rstan::extract(b$fit, "R_G_boat")$R_G_boat

    # 2026-08-30: R_G_boat is DECOUPLED in a shore fit. Both ratios are declared with proper
    # priors unconditionally, so a shore fit's R_G_boat samples its prior and prints as a
    # perfectly reasonable "4.02 gear/group (1.51-10.54)" beside the boat fits' genuine 3.55.
    # structural_params_*.csv has flagged this since 2026-08-27; this file did not, which is
    # how the 2026-08-29 review found the value being read as an estimate. The flag and a
    # suffix on the string, so it cannot be quoted by accident from either.
    .rgb_decoupled <- is.null(b$bss_data) ||
      ((b$bss_data$T_n %||% 0) == 0 && (b$bss_data$OSP_n %||% 0) == 0)
    # 2026-09-29: R_G is informed only by the shore gear interviews (IntA_gear), so in a boat fit
    # it is its prior too; that was reported as an estimate (1.25 [0.69, 2.27] on 2024-25).
    .rg_decoupled <- is.null(b$bss_data) || (b$bss_data$IntA_gear %||% 0) == 0
    expansion_results[[label]] <- tibble(
      fit = label,
      R_G_interpretation = sprintf("%.2f gear/crabber (%.2f-%.2f)%s",
        median(R_G_draws), quantile(R_G_draws, 0.025), quantile(R_G_draws, 0.975),
        if (.rg_decoupled) "  [PRIOR ONLY: no shore gear interviews in this fit]" else ""),
      R_G_boat_interpretation = sprintf("%.2f gear/group (%.2f-%.2f)%s",
        median(R_G_boat_draws), quantile(R_G_boat_draws, 0.025), quantile(R_G_boat_draws, 0.975),
        if (.rgb_decoupled) "  [PRIOR ONLY: no boat count stream in this fit]" else ""),
      R_G_boat_decoupled = .rgb_decoupled,
      R_G_decoupled = .rg_decoupled
    )
  }
}
if(length(expansion_results) > 0) {
  expansion_df <- bind_rows(expansion_results)
  for(i in 1:nrow(expansion_df)) {
    cat(sprintf("  %s: R_G=%s, R_G_boat=%s\n",
                expansion_df$fit[i], expansion_df$R_G_interpretation[i],
                expansion_df$R_G_boat_interpretation[i]))
  }
  write.csv(expansion_df, file.path(output_dir, "expansion_ratios.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}


```

```{r expansion-show, echo=FALSE}
if (exists('expansion_df')) report_table(dplyr::transmute(expansion_df, Fit = short_fit(fit), `R_G (gear per crabber)` = R_G_interpretation,
                                                          `R_G_boat (gear per boat group)` = R_G_boat_interpretation),
                                         caption = 'Expansion-ratio posteriors, median (95% interval). PRIOR ONLY marks a ratio no data in that fit informs.')
```

### 12.2 Turnover as fitted

The season-level turnover `tau_bar` each fit estimated around the prior centre of [Section 3.1](#the-expansion-factors-shore-and-boat-turnover). A posterior close to the prior (Section 11.6 flags it) means the component's scale rests on the derived centre; the shore fits are the case to watch, because only the in-window I/E days inform them.

```{r tau-show, echo=FALSE}
.tb <- read_fit_outputs("structural_params")
if (!is.null(.tb)) {
  .tb <- .tb[grepl("^tau_bar", .tb$parameter), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(.tb)) report_table(data.frame(check.names = FALSE, Fit = .tb$fit_lbl,
      `Prior centre` = ifelse(grepl("^shore", .tb$fit_lbl), sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(params$tau_shore_prior_mu)), sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(params$tau_boat_prior_mu))),
      `tau_bar posterior` = fmt_ci(.tb$median, .tb$lo95, .tb$hi95, digits = 3), n_eff = round(.tb$n_eff), `R-hat` = sprintf("%.3f", .tb$Rhat)),
    caption = "Fitted season-level turnover per fit, median (95% interval).")
  else cat("_No shared turnover in this run (shared_tau = FALSE)._")
}
```

### 12.3 The crabbing fraction f

The share of private-boat effort that is crab-directed, a monthly logit random walk informed by the sampler's boat contacts (and OSP's crab-only share when delivered, as a lower bound through the combo share `c`). It multiplies the boat effort one for one, so a month with few contacts leans on its neighbours through the walk. From `crab_fraction_strata_<fit>.csv`.

```{r f-show, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Crabbing fraction f by month (median and 95% interval) for each boat fit; point size is the number of boat contacts."}
.fs <- read_fit_outputs("crab_fraction_strata")
if (!is.null(.fs) && nrow(.fs)) {
  report_table(dplyr::transmute(.fs, Fit = fit_lbl, Month = label, `Contacts (crabbing)` = sprintf("%d (%d)", contacts, contacts_crabbing),
                                f = fmt_ci(f_median, f_lo95, f_hi95, digits = 2), `Combo share c` = fmt_ci(c_median, c_lo95, c_hi95, digits = 2),
                                `OSP days` = osp_days),
               caption = "Crabbing fraction f and combo share c by month, median (95% interval).")
  p_f <- ggplot(.fs, aes(x = label, y = f_median, group = fit_lbl, color = fit_lbl)) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = f_lo95, ymax = f_hi95), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(size = contacts)) + geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) + scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 4)) +
    labs(x = "Month", y = "Crabbing fraction f", color = "Fit", size = "Contacts") +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  print(p_f)
} else cat("_The crabbing fraction is not estimated in this run._")
```

### 12.4 Effort day covariates as fitted

Every fit's day-covariate block (`K_open`): which columns it carries, on how many of its days each column is set, and the fitted effect on the latent effort (`B_open_out`, with its rate ratio). Under the method of record (CHANGE_REGISTER A30) the private-boat all-gear fit carries the NWS Small-Craft-Advisory flag `nws_sca_any` and every other fit carries nothing (`marine_hazard_gear_regimes`, B42); an other-fishery opener column appears here only when `opener_covariate_mode` selects one. Section 3.4 shows the covariate's pre-fit screen on the sampled days; this table is the fitted model. Written to `effort_day_covariates.csv`.

```{r day-covariates, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.16b EFFORT DAY COVARIATES AS FITTED (2026-09-28, B43) ----
# Until 2026-09-28 the report showed the covariate's pre-fit screen and the configured scope,
# and never the fitted coefficient or which fits carried the column: the preps print that per
# fit, and the fit loop's chunk hides its output. bss_day_covariate_report.R builds the table
# from bss_all, so it is the fits that are reported, not the configuration.
day_cov_df <- tryCatch(bss_day_covariate_table(bss_all, params), error = function(e) {
  bss_warn("covariates", paste("Effort day covariate table not built:", conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"); NULL })
if (!is.null(day_cov_df) && nrow(day_cov_df) > 0) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(day_cov_df)))
    cat(sprintf("  %s: %s%s\n", day_cov_df$fit[i], day_cov_df$covariate[i],
                if (is.na(day_cov_df$rate_ratio[i])) "" else sprintf(" on %d of %d days, rate ratio %s",
                  day_cov_df$days_flagged[i], day_cov_df$fit_days[i], day_cov_df$rate_ratio[i])))
  write.csv(day_cov_df, file.path(output_dir, "effort_day_covariates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r day-covariates-show, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(day_cov_df) && nrow(day_cov_df) > 0)
  report_table(dplyr::transmute(day_cov_df, Fit = short_fit(fit), Covariate = covariate, Source = source,
                                `Days flagged` = days_flagged, `Column sum` = column_sum, `Fit days` = fit_days,
                                `Coefficient` = fmt_ci(coef_median, coef_lo95, coef_hi95, digits = 2), `Rate ratio` = rate_ratio),
               'Effort day covariates as fitted: per fit, the columns of the K_open block, the days each flags (column_sum is the column total, which differs for an imputed fractional column), and the posterior of its coefficient (rate ratio = exp(coefficient), the multiplier on latent effort on a flagged day).')
```

## 13. PE vs BSS comparison

The design-based PE and the Bayesian estimate for each component, on the same effort unit, so a gap is a genuine disagreement between the methods and not a unit artifact. Close agreement is reassuring; a large gap usually marks a data-thin component, where the PE's thin-cell fills (Section 4) and the BSS's AR process fill the unsampled days differently. `Totals use` says which one the port total carries.

```{r pe-vs-bss, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.17 PE VS BSS COMPARISON ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n PE VS BSS COMPARISON\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

comparison <- list()
for(pop in c("shore","private_boat")) {
  for(ss in subseasons) {
    label_cg <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name, "_Dungeness_Kept")
    pe_label <- paste0(pop, "_", ss$name)
    b <- bss_all[[label_cg]]

    pe_catch <- pe_all[[pe_label]]$Dungeness_Kept %||% 0
    pe_effort <- pe_all[[pe_label]]$effort_total %||% 0

    if(!is.null(b) && (is.null(b$pe_fallback) || !b$pe_fallback)) {
      bss_catch <- b$C_expected_sum["50%"]
      bss_effort <- b$E_sum["50%"]
      catch_diff_pct <- round((bss_catch - pe_catch) / pe_catch * 100, 1)
      effort_diff_pct <- round((bss_effort - pe_effort) / pe_effort * 100, 1)
      conv <- convergence_df |> filter(fit == label_cg)
      method <- if(nrow(conv) > 0 && conv$pass_convergence[1]) "BSS" else "PE"
    } else {
      bss_catch <- NA; bss_effort <- NA
      catch_diff_pct <- NA; effort_diff_pct <- NA
      method <- "PE"
    }

    comparison[[length(comparison)+1]] <- tibble(
      component = paste0(pop, " (", ss$display_name, ")"),
      PE_effort = round(pe_effort), BSS_effort = round(bss_effort),
      effort_diff_pct = effort_diff_pct,
      PE_catch = round(pe_catch), BSS_catch = round(bss_catch),
      catch_diff_pct = catch_diff_pct,
      method_selected = method
    )
  }
}
comparison[[length(comparison)+1]] <- tibble(
  component = "comm_charter (census)",
  PE_effort = round(pe_all$comm_charter$effort_total), BSS_effort = NA, effort_diff_pct = NA,
  PE_catch = round(pe_all$comm_charter$Dungeness_Kept), BSS_catch = NA, catch_diff_pct = NA,
  # Review item 4 (2026-09-08/09): say what was observed and what the unsampled days are.
  # 2026-09-11: the two populations, two estimators, stated in the method column
  method_selected = local({ .c <- pe_all$comm_charter; sprintf(
    paste0("Commercial CENSUS %s (%s crab, %.0f vessel-trips on %d tally days, %d unsampled days %s; per-vessel mean over %d interviews SE %s) ",
           "+ Charter EXPANSION (%s frame%s, %s; %.0f trips, %d interviewed = %.0f%%, %s crab observed -> %s crab, SE %s). Carried into the port ",
           "interval: %s (census_uncertainty = '%s')"),
    if (identical(.c$census_expansion %||% "none", "none")) "(exact sum over the tally days)" else "(day-type stratified)",
    format(round(.c$commercial_dung %||% NA), big.mark = ","), .c$commercial_vessels %||% NA,
    sum(.c$daily_full$observed %||% NA), sum(!(.c$daily_full$observed %||% NA)),
    if (identical(.c$census_expansion %||% "none", "none")) "= no operation" else sprintf("imputed at %s", format(round(.c$imputed_dung %||% NA), big.mark = ",")),
    # 2026-09-29: the commercial per-vessel mean rests on the COMMERCIAL interviews; this read
    # charter_interviews (20 on 2024-25) where the count is commercial_interviews (141).
    .c$commercial_interviews %||% NA, format(round(.c$commercial_se %||% NA), big.mark = ","),
    .c$charter_frame %||% "tally",
    if ((.c$n_roster_only_days %||% 0L) > 0) sprintf(" incl. %s crab on %d day(s) with no tally", format(round(.c$charter_roster_dung %||% 0), big.mark = ","), .c$n_roster_only_days) else "",
    .c$charter_expansion %||% "pooled", .c$charter_trips %||% NA, .c$charter_interviews %||% NA,
    100 * (.c$charter_sampled_frac %||% NA_real_), format(round(.c$charter_observed_dung %||% NA), big.mark = ","),
    format(round(.c$charter_dung %||% NA), big.mark = ","), format(round(.c$charter_se %||% NA), big.mark = ","),
    format(round(.c$carried_se %||% 0), big.mark = ","), .c$census_uncertainty %||% "charter") })
)
comparison_df <- bind_rows(comparison)
# 2026-08-30: say explicitly whether the BSS column was USED.
# `method_selected` already recorded the gate verdict, but a rejected fit still leaves its
# BSS_catch sitting in the adjacent column with nothing marking it as unused. The
# 2026-08-29 gear run is the worked example: BSS_catch = 32,689 for private_boat (All gear)
# beside method_selected = "PE", while the port total correctly substituted the PE. A reader
# scanning the BSS column has no way to know. bss_reported answers it in one field.
comparison_df$bss_reported <- comparison_df$method_selected == "BSS"
print(comparison_df)
write.csv(comparison_df, file.path(output_dir, "pe_vs_bss_comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

```{r pe-vs-bss-show, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
.cmp <- comparison_df
.cmp$method_short <- ifelse(grepl("census", .cmp$component), "Census + charter expansion", .cmp$method_selected)
.cmp$Component <- sub("^comm_charter \\(census\\)$", "Commercial/charter", sub("^private_boat ", "Private boat ", sub("^shore ", "Shore ", .cmp$component)))
print(report_table(dplyr::transmute(.cmp, Component, `PE effort` = round(PE_effort), `BSS effort` = round(BSS_effort),
                                    `Effort BSS vs PE (%)` = round(effort_diff_pct, 1), `PE catch` = round(PE_catch), `BSS catch` = round(BSS_catch),
                                    `Catch BSS vs PE (%)` = round(catch_diff_pct, 1), `Totals use` = method_short),
                   digits = 1, caption = paste("Point Estimator against the Bayesian estimate by component (BSS medians). Effort is in gear deployments;",
                                               "the census row in vessel-trips. 'Totals use' is the estimate the port total carries.")))
.cens <- .cmp$method_selected[grepl("census", .cmp$component)]
if (length(.cens)) cat("\n**Commercial/charter component:** ", .cens, "\n", sep = "")
```

## 14. Run summary

The window, the sampling coverage, the interviews the fits used, and how many fits passed the gate.

```{r season-summary, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.18 SEASON SUMMARY ----
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n SEASON SUMMARY\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")

season_days <- as.integer(as.Date(params$est_date_end) - as.Date(params$est_date_start) + 1)
total_effort_days <- n_distinct(c(dwg$shore_effort$event_date, dwg$boat_effort$event_date))
total_interview_n <- nrow(dwg$interview)
# 2026-09-29: the interviews the fits actually used (after the incomplete-trip and gear filters),
# beside the raw count of every interview in the window, which includes commercial/charter.
fitted_interview_n <- sum(vapply(bss_all, function(b) if (!is.null(b$bss_data)) as.numeric(b$bss_data$IntC %||% 0) else 0, numeric(1)))
n_bss_fits <- sum(!sapply(bss_all, function(b) !is.null(b$pe_fallback) && b$pe_fallback))
n_pass <- sum(convergence_df$pass_convergence, na.rm=TRUE)

cat(sprintf("\n  Season: %s to %s (%d days)\n", params$est_date_start, params$est_date_end, season_days))
cat(sprintf("  Effort days sampled: %d (%d%%)\n", total_effort_days, round(total_effort_days/season_days*100)))
cat(sprintf("  Total interviews: %d\n", total_interview_n))
cat(sprintf("  BSS convergence: %d of %d fits passed\n", n_pass, n_bss_fits))

season_summary <- tibble(
  metric = c("Model configuration", "Season start", "Season end", "Season days",
             "Effort days sampled", "Total interviews", "Interviews used by the fits", "BSS fits attempted", "BSS fits passed",
             "Day length", "AR temporal resolution"),
  # 2026-09-29: this driver IS the pooled model. It read the orchestrator's `model`, which is
  # "both" when the two models render in turn, so the table said "both CPUE".
  value = c(sprintf("%s CPUE; seasons %s; effort unit %s; AR %s; marine term %s", "pooled",
                    paste(params$season_filter, collapse = " + "), params$shore_effort_unit %||% "?",
                    if (is.null(params$ar_escalate) || isFALSE(params$ar_escalate)) "adaptive (capped)" else "escalation ladder (scoped)",
                    params$marine_hazard_mode %||% "off"),
            params$est_date_start, params$est_date_end,
            as.character(season_days), as.character(total_effort_days),
            format(total_interview_n, big.mark = ","), format(fitted_interview_n, big.mark = ","), as.character(n_bss_fits), as.character(n_pass),
            if (!bss_needs_day_length(params)) "not used (gear-deployment unit; the expansion is the turnover)"
            else if (!is.null(L_eff_model)) L_eff_model$method else "civil_twilight",
            paste(unique(na.omit(unlist(ar_resolutions))), collapse = ", "))
)
write.csv(season_summary, file.path(output_dir, "season_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


```

## 15. Run parameters, timing and software

The full parameters are written to `run_parameters.txt` and the R session to `session_info.txt`; the tables below give the wall-clock by section and the software that produced this run.

```{r save-params, results='hide'}
# ---- 7.19 SAVE PARAMETERS ----
timer_stop("6_outputs")
# 2026-09-04 DEFECT FIX. This was `str(params)` with its defaults, and str() truncates a
# list at list.len = 99 entries with a "[list output truncated]" line. run_config carries 120
# keys, so EVERY run_parameters.txt in this repo before this date is missing about 21 of
# them, silently. That file is not decoration: config_delta() in the batch runners compares
# two runs key by key from it, and annotate_decoupled_run.R reads run flags out of it. A
# truncated dump gives that machinery false POSITIVES (a key that scrolled off one side of a
# comparison reads as "differs") and, far worse, false NEGATIVES (a key that genuinely
# differs but sits past entry 99 in both dumps is never compared at all). The 2026-09-03 Z0
# stage reported 9 UNEXPECTED config keys on a run whose config was in fact correct; all 9
# were keys that crossed the truncation boundary when new keys were added above them.
# list.len is set well above the key count and nchar.max is raised so long vectors are not
# elided either.
writeLines(capture.output(str(params, list.len = 1000, nchar.max = 2000, vec.len = 100)),
           file.path(output_dir, "run_parameters.txt"))

# B1.6: session and version capture for reproducibility. Pins package and Stan
# versions and the seed with each output set, so a result is reproducible from
# the committed artifacts.
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(output_dir, "session_info.txt"))
cat(sprintf("\nrstan %s; StanHeaders %s; bss_seed %s\n",
            utils::packageVersion("rstan"),
            utils::packageVersion("StanHeaders"),
            params$bss_seed),
    file = file.path(output_dir, "session_info.txt"), append = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("\nAll outputs saved to: %s\n", output_dir))
cat(paste(" ", list.files(output_dir), collapse="\n"), "\n")

# ---- TIMING SUMMARY ----
run_total <- difftime(Sys.time(), run_start_time, units = "mins")
cat("\n", strrep("=",60), "\n TIMING SUMMARY\n", strrep("=",60), "\n")
timing_df <- tibble(
  Section = names(bss_timer_log()),
  Minutes = sapply(bss_timer_log(), function(x) round(as.numeric(x$elapsed), 1))
)
print(timing_df, n = 20)
# 2026-09-05: persist it. Per-fit wall-clock by AR resolution is what a batch runtime
# estimate is built from, and until now it existed only as console output inside a
# results='hide' chunk, so the 2026-09-05 pre-run audit had to scrape the gear HTML for it.
utils::write.csv(timing_df, file.path(output_dir, "run_timings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\n  TOTAL RUNTIME: %.1f minutes (%.1f hours)\n",
            as.numeric(run_total), as.numeric(run_total)/60))

# save.image(file = file.path(output_dir, "BSS-GH-pooled-CPUE-model_workspace.RData"))
```

```{r run-info-show, echo=FALSE}
report_table(dplyr::mutate(timing_df, Section = sub("^BSS_(.*)_Dungeness_Kept_att([0-9]+)$", "fit: \\1 (attempt \\2)", Section)),
             digits = 1, caption = sprintf("Wall-clock minutes by section; total %.1f minutes.", as.numeric(run_total)))
.si <- sessionInfo()
report_table(data.frame(check.names = FALSE, Item = c("R", "rstan", "StanHeaders", "Platform", "Code (git)", "Seed / init_r"),
  Value = c(.si$R.version$version.string, as.character(utils::packageVersion("rstan")),
            tryCatch(as.character(utils::packageVersion("StanHeaders")), error = function(e) "?"), .si$platform,
            sprintf("%s%s", run_git_sha, if (run_git_dirty) " (uncommitted changes)" else ""),
            sprintf("%s / %s", params$bss_seed, params$bss_init_r %||% 2))),
  caption = "Software and reproducibility. A render of the same code, data and configuration on the same platform reproduces this run's draws.")
```

## 16. Run warnings and notes

Every condition this run recorded, in one place: fallbacks (a turnover prior centred on its fallback, a component on its PE), skipped diagnostics, census frame conditions, and every R warning and message a step raised. **Warnings** can affect a number and should be read before citing the estimate; **notes** record a choice or a missing optional input. Written to `run_warnings.csv`. An empty table means the run recorded nothing.

```{r run-warnings-show, echo=FALSE}
# 2026-09-29 (D36 / the report overhaul). Two sources: bss_warn() calls (a structured log in
# 03_R_functions/bss_run_warnings.R) and every warning or message knitr captured from any chunk
# (the setup hooks). A bss_warn() warning is also raised as an R warning, so its knitr copy is
# dropped here rather than listed twice; repeats are counted, not repeated.
.bw <- bss_warn_log()
.kc <- .report_conditions$log
.bw_tab <- if (nrow(.bw)) data.frame(Source = .bw$source, Severity = .bw$severity, Message = .bw$message, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL
.kc_tab <- if (nrow(.kc)) {
  .m <- sub("^\\[[^]]+\\] ", "", .kc$message)
  .keep <- !(.m %in% .bw$message)
  data.frame(Source = sprintf("R %s (chunk %s)", .kc$type[.keep], .kc$chunk[.keep]),
             Severity = ifelse(.kc$type[.keep] == "warning", "warning", "note"), Message = .m[.keep], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else NULL
run_warnings <- dplyr::bind_rows(.bw_tab, .kc_tab)
if (!is.null(run_warnings) && nrow(run_warnings)) {
  run_warnings <- run_warnings |> dplyr::count(Severity, Source, Message, name = "Times") |>
    dplyr::arrange(factor(Severity, levels = c("warning", "note")), Source)
  utils::write.csv(run_warnings, file.path(output_dir, "run_warnings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  report_table(run_warnings, digits = 0, caption = sprintf("Run warnings (%d) and notes (%d), each listed once with the number of times it was raised.",
                                                           sum(run_warnings$Severity == "warning"), sum(run_warnings$Severity == "note")))
} else {
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(Severity = character(0), Source = character(0), Message = character(0), Times = integer(0)),
                   file.path(output_dir, "run_warnings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("No warnings or notes were recorded this run.\n")
}
```

`r if (isTRUE(params$divergence_appendix)) "## Appendix A: divergence diagnostics\n\nParameter-by-parameter divergence localization (opt-in: \x60divergence_appendix = TRUE\x60 in \x60run_config.R\x60)." else ""`

```{r divergence-diagnostics, echo=FALSE, eval=isTRUE(params$divergence_appendix)}

# load('output/20260619/pooled-CPUE/BSS-GH-pooled-CPUE-model_workspace.RData')

source(here::here("03_R_functions/divergence_diagnostic.R"))
# Robust to the sub-season set (build_subseasons): iterate over every fitted BSS
# component and skip PE-fallback components that have no Stan fit, rather than
# hardcoding fit labels (which omitted private_boat_ring_net_only and would miss the
# pre/post all-gear keys of a mid-season closure).
for (nm in names(bss_all)) {
  b <- bss_all[[nm]]
  if (is.null(b) || isTRUE(b$pe_fallback) || is.null(b$fit)) next
  cat(sprintf("\n=== Divergence diagnostics: %s ===\n", nm))
  tryCatch(diagnose_divergences(b$fit), error = function(e) bss_warn("divergence appendix", sprintf("%s: skipped (%s)", nm, conditionMessage(e)), severity = "note"))
}
```

## Appendix B: Other-fishery opener spillover

A hypothesis test, not a model change: do other coastal fishery openers (Marine Area 2 finfish, coastal razor-clam digs near Grays Harbor) pull crab effort or catch rate onto or off opener days beyond what the day type and the month already explain? The **adjusted** table is the test: the opener's coefficient in `lm(response ~ day_type + month + opener)`. It feeds the opener screen in Section 3.3 and changes no estimate by itself.

```{r fishery-spillover-raw-show, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(sp_raw_disp)) {
  report_table(sp_raw_disp, paste("Raw comparison: mean crab effort (daily counts) and CPUE (Dungeness per gear",
    "deployment) on other-fishery opener days vs other days. These are confounded with day-type and season;",
    "read the adjusted table below for the marginal effect."))
} else {
  cat(if (isTRUE(params$run_fishery_spillover_diag))
        "_Fishery-opener spillover diagnostic produced no output this run._"
      else "_Fishery-opener spillover diagnostic is off (`run_fishery_spillover_diag = FALSE`)._")
}
```

```{r fishery-spillover-adj-show, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(sp_adj_disp)) report_table(sp_adj_disp, paste("Adjusted association: the opener coefficient in",
  "lm(response ~ day-type + month + opener), the marginal effect after removing the weekend and monthly signal",
  "the model already captures. Positive = more effort/CPUE on opener days. A blank estimate with a Note means",
  "the opener could not be separated from day-type/month in this season."))
```

```{r fishery-spillover-notes, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(spillover)) {
  cat("**Identifiability notes (read before interpreting):**\n\n")
  for (nt in spillover$notes) cat("- ", nt, "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```
